settings.construction: For a signature Σ with countably infinitely many individual constants and at least one relational constant, take a set of action models for L(Σ) complete for C(Σ), and coalesce them at a new root whose individual domain is the set of individual constants, each constant denoting itself there and being carried by the distinguished arrow to each component onto its interpretation in that component; relational constants are glued as in Definition E.2, with free root extensions. Evaluation point: the root.

meets.two-actual-components: The components are complete for C(Σ), so two of them satisfy Actuality at their roots; the root domains are the fullest.
meets.complete-components: The action models for L(Σ) are a set complete for C(Σ), so in particular for C.
meets.free-root-component: The root domains are as full as compatibility allows.

arguments.text: The root satisfies Maximalist Classicism for Σ, since every C(Σ)-consistent sentence holds at some component root. It satisfies Possibility+ (signature Σ): for P with free individual variables x̄, instantiate x̄ by pairwise distinct root individuals, that is, distinct constants c̄′ not occurring in P; P[c̄′/x̄] is C(Σ)-consistent because the c̄′ are fresh, so it is possible at the root. The instances of the pure form follow.

Distinct constants denote distinct root individuals, so there are infinitely many individuals at the root, giving the Infinity Schema at type e and, the root domains being as full as possible so that the numeral intensions exist, the Axiom of Infinity at type e.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: Every canonical necessary-Peano guard fails at the root. For each source type $\sigma$, the pure sentence $\neg I^*_\sigma$ is consistent with C: in a full one-world model with finite individuals every type is finite, and sufficiently large Frege cardinalities coincide. Completeness of the component family makes this sentence possible at the root, so $\Box I^*_\sigma$ is false. Every guarded FTN instance is therefore true. No fixed power carrier is asserted. This is the same guard argument as arithmetic-necessitism-complete-components, now applied to the exact FTN definition. Direct source: the mathematical-necessitism handoff, 29 October 2026, coalesced group supplement and reference-analytic- necessitism §6, unpaginated (misc).

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), answering Cian Dorr's conjecture
arguments.text: Tame Rigidity fails at a relational argument type in models of C (ultralimit-fork, symmetric-qualitative-links), so some component $M$ refutes it at its root $M_0$: some $F_M$ of type $\sigma\to t$, $\sigma$ relational, is weakly rigid there but not rigid. A root entity $F$ of that type is a root extension $F_o$ together with a component $F_N$ in each component $N$, and a formula about $F$ at a world of $N$ is the same formula about $F_N$ in $N$. Since the components of root entities are arbitrary, $F$ is weakly inextensible at the root exactly when, for every $N$, every $X_N$ that necessarily holds of the $N$-components of the members of $F_o$ has $F_N\le X_N$. For each other component $N$ fix $z_N$, and for each $y$ in the extension of $F_M$ at $M_0$ let $x_y$ be the root entity with $M$-component $y$ and $N$-components $z_N$, free at the root by the condition. Put $F_o:=\{x_y\}$, $F_N:=\lambda y\, .\,y=z_N$, a haecceity, rigid in every model of C, and keep $F_M$. Then $F$ is persistent and weakly inextensible at the root, each component's condition being the weak inextensibility of its own component, but not inextensible, since $F_M$ is not inextensible in $M$ and every arrow from the root into $M$ factors through the distinguished one. So Tame Rigidity fails at the root.

arguments.text:
The transfer of tame-rigidity-component, applied to a rigid relation whose power property is not rigid. The pure sentence $\exists A^{tt}\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(A)\land\neg\operatorname{Rigid} (\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le A)$ is consistent with C (it holds in the one-individual variants of finite-support-pair-injections-or-collapses and symmetric-collapse-pair, with $A:=\top$), so some component $m$ satisfies it at its root, with witness $A$. Its extension $D$ there is nonempty: otherwise weak inextensibility tested on $\bot$ makes $A=\bot$, whose power property is the haecceity of $\bot$, which is rigid.
For $p\in D$ let $\widehat p$ be the root proposition false at the root, with $m$-component $p$ and $\bot$ in every other component; let $F$ have root extension $\{\widehat p:p\in D\}$, $m$-component $A$, and in each other component $i$ the haecceity of $\bot$. Both are in the domain, the root domains being fullest. $F$ is weakly persistent at the root, $A$ and the haecceities being persistent. It is weakly inextensible there: if $H$ necessarily holds of every $\widehat p$, its root extension contains them, $A\le H_m$ by the weak inextensibility of $A$, and the haecceity of $\bot$ entails $H_i$; entailment in the sum is componentwise. Every other accessible world lies in a component, where $F$'s components are rigid; so $F$ is rigid. The $m$-component of its power property is that of $A$, transport respecting abstraction, rigidity and entailment, and every arrow into $m$ factors through the distinguished one; so it is not rigid. Rigid Power fails at the root, at type $t\to t$.

models.definition:
For a signature Σ with countably infinitely many individual constants and at least one relational constant, take a set of action models for L(Σ) complete for C(Σ), and coalesce them at a new root whose individual domain is the set of individual constants, each constant denoting itself there and being carried by the distinguished arrow to each component onto its interpretation in that component; relational constants are glued as in Definition E.2, with free root extensions. Evaluation point: the root.

The root has one distinguished arrow to the root of each component, and every arrow from the root into a component factors through it.

Root domains are as full as compatibility allows: a root proposition is a choice, for each component, of a proposition of that component’s root domain, together with a truth value at the root’s identity arrow, and a root entity of a relational type is likewise a family of component entities with a root component that is an arbitrary function of the root arguments.

met.actual-world-isolated: The singleton root proposition, true at the root's identity arrow and nowhere in a component, is in the domain and entails every truth; the components have no arrows back to the root (Classicism, Appendix E, p. 83, on the distinctness-preserving collapse).
met.two-actual-components: The components are complete for C(Σ), so two of them satisfy Actuality at their roots; the root domains are the fullest.
met.complete-components: The action models for L(Σ) are a set complete for C(Σ), so in particular for C.
met.free-root-component: The root domains are as full as compatibility allows.

settings.construction: Fix a set $A$ of action models complete for C, with disjoint objects and arrows, and the signature $\Sigma_0=\{d\}$ with one constant $d$ of type $e$. Add an object $W_0$. Its arrows out are its identity and, for each object $V$ of a model in $A$ and each individual $a$ at $V$, an arrow $\langle V,a\rangle$ into $V$, the interpretation of $\Sigma_0$ sending $d$ to $a$; an arrow $k$ of the component composes with it to give $\langle V^{\prime},k\cdot a\rangle$. The only individual at $W_0$ is $d$, and $\langle V,a\rangle$ sends it to $a$. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow. Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type, the root entity with the closed term $\lambda\bar x\, .\,\top$ and full extension at the identity.

domains.text: An entity at $W_0$ of a relational type is an intension over the arrows out of $W_0$ for which there is a closed term $t$ of $\mathcal L(\Sigma_0)$ whose interpretation at $V$ under $d\mapsto a$ is its value at $\langle V,a\rangle$, for every arrow $\langle V,a\rangle$; its value at the identity is unconstrained. Its transport along $\langle V,a\rangle$ is then the entity $t$ denotes at $V$, so it lands in the component domain.

meets.complete-components: The models in $A$ are complete for C.
meets.free-root-component: The value of a root entity at the identity arrow is unconstrained, the identity being the only arrow into $W_0$.
meets.sigma-top: This is the interpretation the construction fixes.

arguments.text: A closed pure sentence holds at $\langle V,a\rangle$ iff it holds at $V$ in its component. Every pure sentence consistent with C holds at the root of some model in $A$, so it is possible at $W_0$: Maximalism (pure) in its possibility form. For Possibility+ (pure), the only individual at $W_0$ is $d$, so an instance with two or more distinct individual variables has a false antecedent, and for one variable $x$ a consistent pure $P(x)$ holds of some individual $a$ at the root $V$ of some model in $A$; then $P(d)$ holds at $\langle V,a\rangle$, since $\langle V,a\rangle$ sends $d$ to $a$.

At type $e$: $\Diamond\exists x\, .\,x
e d$ holds at $W_0$, some component having two individuals, but the only individual at $W_0$ is $d$ and $\Diamond(d
e d)$ fails. At type $t$, in the form $\Diamond\exists p\, .\,Xp	o\exists p\, .\,\Diamond Xp$: let $X$ be the root property denoted by $\lambda p\, .\,\operatorname{Atom}(p)\land\exists q\, .\,(\operatorname{Atom}(q)\land q
e p)\land \Box\mathrm{ND}\land\mathrm{Atomicity}\land orall x orall y\, .\,x=y$. Its instantiation is consistent with C (the full S5 model over the two-element group with one individual), so $\Diamond\exists p\, .\,Xp$ holds at $W_0$. A root proposition $p$ has a closed sentence $t$ of $\mathcal L(\Sigma_0)$ as its value at every arrow into a component. At a world $w$ where $\Box\mathrm{ND}$, Atomicity and $ orall x orall y\, .\,x=y$ hold there is necessarily exactly one individual (BF follows from $\Box$ND, and $x=y	o\Box\,x=y$), so $t$ and the pure sentence $ orall x\, .\,t[x/d]$ are the same proposition at $w$, which is not contingent there by the recorded result $\Box$ND + Atomicity (type $t$) ⇒ No Pure Contingency; being S5 ($\Box$ND gives 5), it is $	op$ or $ ot$ at $w$, and neither is an atom beside another atom. arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: The root propositions with the term $\bot$ and the two values at the identity are distinct at $W_0$, since the value at the identity of a root property of propositions is unconstrained and so some root property separates them, and they coincide at every arrow into a component. So two distinct propositions are possibly identical.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: Two root propositions false at the identity, with sentences $t$ and $t^{\prime}$, are identical iff $t\leftrightarrow t^{\prime}$ holds at every object of every model in $A$ under every interpretation of $d$, which by completeness is iff it is a theorem of C($\Sigma_0$); and the first entails the second iff $t\to t^{\prime}$ is a theorem. So those propositions form the Lindenbaum algebra of C($\Sigma_0$), a countable Boolean algebra without atoms: every consistent $t$ has a consistent proper strengthening, such as $t$ with a sentence fixing a number of propositions that $t$ leaves open. The root propositions are this algebra with a truth value at the identity adjoined. Atomicity fails at type $t$, every nonzero proposition false at the identity lacking an atom below it, and so at all relational types. Boolean Completeness at type $t$ fails since a countable atomless Boolean algebra is not complete, and Countable Boolean Completeness since it is not even countably complete, a strictly decreasing sequence without a greatest lower bound being available there; any family of root propositions is the value at the identity of a root property, the value at the identity being unconstrained.

revisions.by: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), prompted by Daniel Kodsi, 25 October 2026 (the error and the repair); checked and recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
revisions.note: The Lindenbaum algebra is not atomless: "the Fregean Axiom holds and there are exactly $n$ individuals" is complete over C, so for each $n\ge1$ it gives an atom $A_n$. The verdicts stand. Countably many root propositions cannot supply joins for all the subfamilies of the pairwise disjoint $A_n$, so one subfamily has no join, which refutes Boolean Completeness at type $t$; the root relation sending $A_n$ to the number $\operatorname{Suc}^n\mathbf 0$ of type $(tt)t$ makes that subfamily countable, which refutes Countable Boolean Completeness; and Maximalism excludes Atomicity. See the write-up, section "Atoms, completeness and Forcing Possibilism".

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), prompted by Daniel Kodsi, 25 October 2026; checked and recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: At every type. The atoms $A_n$ of the revised lindenbaum argument are pairwise disjoint. Every set of tuples of root entities is the value at the identity of a root relation, so internal Dedekind finiteness, injections and isomorphisms at $W_0$ agree with the external ones. A Dedekind-finite complete Boolean algebra is then finite, and so is one with fewer elements than the countably many root propositions, a countably infinite one having an injection back. A finite one with $k$ atoms is isomorphic to the propositions below $A_1\lor\dots\lor A_k$, which is not $\top$, since $A_{k+1}$ is disjoint from it. See the write-up.

arguments.text: Both principles are evaluated at the identity of $W_0$ alone, where the quantified relations range over root entities with arbitrary values at the identity. For Well-Ordering at a type $\sigma$, let $R$ have at the identity a well-ordering of the root entities of type $\sigma$, chosen in the metatheory, and the term $\bot$ elsewhere; every root property of that type has as its value at the identity a set of those entities, so $R$ well-orders the type there. For Transversal Choice, the transversal of an equivalence relation at the identity has a choice of one member of each class as its value there and the term $\bot$ elsewhere.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: At type $e\to t$. Let $Y$ be the root property with the term $\lambda x\, .\,\top$ and the value $\{d\}$ at the identity. It is weakly persistent, $Y$ holding of $d$ at every arrow. It is weakly inextensible at $W_0$: a root property $X$ with $\Box Xd$ holds of $d$ at the identity and, its term holding at $\langle V,a\rangle$ of $a$, of every individual at every component world, so $Y\le X$. But its transport into a component is the universal property of individuals, which is weakly inextensible at a world only if BF at type $e$ holds there, and some component refutes BF at its root, the components being complete for C. So $Y$ is weakly rigid but not rigid.

arguments.text: Every canonical necessary-Peano guard fails at the root. arguments.text: Vacuously, at every type $\sigma$. The negation of $I^*_\sigma$, that zero is a successor or successor is not injective on the numbers at $\sigma$, is a pure sentence consistent with C: it holds in the full model with one world, one individual and two propositions, where every type is finite and the finite cardinalities beyond the size of the type coincide. models.notes: Built on 20 October 2026, at Cian Dorr's suggestion, as a coalesced root whose entities are exactly the ones definable by closed terms, uniformly across the components, so that every root entity is pure-definable at every component world where there is one individual. Its purpose is the closed pure sentence Ψ, "nothing is possibly a contingent proposition at a world where □ND, Atomicity and $\forall x\forall y\, .\,x=y$ hold", which holds at the root (see the write-up): Ψ is consistent with Maximalist Classicism, the premise of maximalism-signature-incompatible-with-strong-possibility-pure. Maximalism for Σ fails here only because Σ is interpreted at the top; interpreting its constants by closed terms of a larger $\Sigma_0$ would give Maximalism for Σ but lose Ψ. That it is a model of C is argued in the write-up; no second reader has checked it, and no Lean verification is claimed.
models.definition:
Fix a set $A$ of action models complete for C, with disjoint objects and arrows, and the signature $\Sigma_0=\{d\}$ with one constant $d$ of type $e$. Add an object $W_0$. Its arrows out are its identity and, for each object $V$ of a model in $A$ and each individual $a$ at $V$, an arrow $\langle V,a\rangle$ into $V$, the interpretation of $\Sigma_0$ sending $d$ to $a$; an arrow $k$ of the component composes with it to give $\langle V^{\prime},k\cdot a\rangle$. The only individual at $W_0$ is $d$, and $\langle V,a\rangle$ sends it to $a$. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow. Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type, the root entity with the closed term $\lambda\bar x\, .\,\top$ and full extension at the identity.

The root has an arrow to every object of every component, one for each interpretation there of a fixed signature, and the root's individuals are that signature's individual constants.

An entity at $W_0$ of a relational type is an intension over the arrows out of $W_0$ for which there is a closed term $t$ of $\mathcal L(\Sigma_0)$ whose interpretation at $V$ under $d\mapsto a$ is its value at $\langle V,a\rangle$, for every arrow $\langle V,a\rangle$; its value at the identity is unconstrained. Its transport along $\langle V,a\rangle$ is then the entity $t$ denotes at $V$, so it lands in the component domain.

met.actual-world-isolated: The singleton root proposition, true at the root's identity arrow and nowhere in a component, is in the domain and entails every truth; the components have no arrows back to the root (Classicism, Appendix E, p. 83, on the distinctness-preserving collapse).
met.complete-components: The models in $A$ are complete for C.
met.free-root-component: The value of a root entity at the identity arrow is unconstrained, the identity being the only arrow into $W_0$.
met.sigma-top: This is the interpretation the construction fixes.

arguments.text: Let $N$ and $M$ be two components whose roots satisfy Actuality, with true atoms $a_N$ and $a_M$, and let $P$ be the root proposition false at the root, with component $a_N$ at $N$, $a_M$ at $M$ and bottom elsewhere. $P$ is possible, and it is a self-atom: under the distinguished arrow into $N$ it becomes $a_N$, and a true atom is a self-atom, as it entails every truth, including the truth that it entails every truth; likewise at $M$; and at the root it is false. settings.construction: Fix a set $A$ of action models complete for C($\Sigma$), with disjoint objects and arrows, and a signature $\Sigma^+\supseteq\Sigma$ with countably infinitely many constants of every type. Add an object $W_0$. Its arrows out are its identity and, for each object $V$ of a model in $A$ and each interpretation $I$ of $\Sigma^+$ at $V$, an arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ into $V$; an arrow $k$ of the component composes with it to give $\langle V^{\prime},k\cdot I\rangle$. The individuals at $W_0$ are the individual constants of $\Sigma^+$, and $\langle V,I\rangle$ sends each to its interpretation. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow. Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: each constant $c$ of Σ denotes $\hat c$, the entity whose transport along every $\langle V,I\rangle$ is $I(c)$ and whose extension at the identity is empty.

domains.text: An entity at $W_0$ of a relational type is an intension over the arrows out of $W_0$ that is pinned down by a finite set $S$ of constants of $\Sigma^+$ (two arrows into the same object whose interpretations agree on $S$ give it the same value) and whose transport along every arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ is in the domain of $V$ in its component; its value at the identity is unconstrained.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 25 October 2026
arguments.text: Self-atoms are atoms (type t) fails at the root, and with it Self-atoms are strong atoms (type t). Some component has an object $V$ satisfying Actuality, with true atom $a_V$, since the components are complete and Actuality is consistent with C(Σ); and $a_V$ is a self-atom, so for an arrow $m$ out of $V$ its transport is $a_V$ exactly when $m\in a_V$ (then $a_V$ is the true atom at $m$’s target, the atom containing the identity there), and otherwise excludes the identity. Let $c$ be a propositional constant of $\Sigma^+$ and $P$ the root proposition false at the identity and true exactly at the arrows $\langle V,I\rangle$ with $I(c)=a_V$: pinned down by $\{c\}$, with transport along such an arrow the set of $m$ with $m\cdot a_V=a_V$, that is $a_V$, an atom at $V$. So $P$ is possible and a self-atom. It is not an atom: for another propositional constant $c^{\prime}$, the arrows with $I(c)=a_V$ and $I(c^{\prime})=\top$ form a proper nonempty part pinned down by $\{c,c^{\prime}\}$.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: At every type, in the form $\Diamond\exists x\, .\,Fx\to\exists x\, .\,\Diamond Fx$. Each constant $c$ of type $\sigma$ gives an entity $\hat c$ at $W_0$, pinned down by $\{c\}$, with $\langle V,I\rangle\cdot\hat c=I(c)$ (for $\sigma=e$, $c$ itself). Let $F$ be pinned down by a finite $S$ and true of $y$ at $\langle V,I\rangle$. Choose $c$ of type $\sigma$ outside $S$ and let $I^{\prime}$ agree with $I$ except that $I^{\prime}(c)=y$. Then $\langle V,I^{\prime}\rangle$ agrees with $\langle V,I\rangle$ on $S$, so $F$ holds there of $y=\langle V,I^{\prime}\rangle\cdot\hat c$, and $\Diamond F\hat c$.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: A closed sentence of $\Sigma$ holds at $\langle V,I\rangle$ iff it holds at $V$ in its component under the restriction of $I$ to $\Sigma$, the constants of $\Sigma$ denoting the entities $\hat c$. Every $\Sigma$-sentence consistent with C($\Sigma$) holds at the root of some model in $A$ under some interpretation, which extends to $\Sigma^+$, so it is possible at $W_0$: Maximalism for $\Sigma$ in its possibility form, and with it the pure form.

arguments.text: The only atom is $\delta$, the proposition true at the identity alone. A proposition $p$ true at some $\langle V,I\rangle$, pinned down by a finite $S$, is split by $\hat c$ for a propositional constant $c\notin S$: $p$ is true at the two arrows that differ from $\langle V,I\rangle$ only in sending $c$ to $\top$ and to $\bot$, and $\hat c$ is true at just one of them. Any other nonzero proposition is $\delta$. Now let $X$ have as its value at the identity four individual constants and let $R$ order them as the four-element Boolean algebra, both empty elsewhere. $(X,R)$ is a finite complete Boolean algebra, every subset of the four being the value at the identity of a root property. An interval below some $p$ isomorphic to it would contain two atoms, which would be atoms of the whole algebra. From Astra's note "Pure Maximalism and Forcing Possibilism" (25 October 2026, §6), in Daniel Kodsi's pull request #18.

In each $N\in\{N_+,N_-\}$, carry out the construction of coalesced-pinned-substitutions-root with a single component, finite-support-monotone-maps as built in $N$, giving an action model $M_N$ with root object $R_N$. Being an action model, and the truth of a formula at a world, are computed by recursion inside $N$, so $M_N$ is an action model of C in the metatheory, with the same truths. The components are $M_{N_+}$ and $M_{N_-}$, and the root $W_0$ is built over them as in coalesced-pinned-substitutions-root. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow. arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: □Atomlessness: $W_0$ is atomless by the argument atomlessness of coalesced-pinned-substitutions-root, which needs of the components only that $\top\ne\bot$ in them; each $R_N$ is atomless by the same argument, carried out in $N$; and finite-support-monotone-maps is atomless. So Atomlessness holds at every world. CH, at type $et$: at $R_N$ the entity with value $E$ at every map of the constants and empty at the arrows into the component is pinned down by $\varnothing$ and lands, with extension $E$ at the identity, for any set $E$ of tuples in $N$. So quantifiers over relations at $R_N$ range over all such sets, there are continuum many (in $N$) entities of type $et$ there, and the real number structures at $et$ there are $N$'s complete ordered fields on sets of them, CH holding of them iff $N\models\mathrm{CH}$. A closed pure sentence holds at an arrow $\langle R_N,I\rangle$ iff it holds at $R_N$, so at $W_0$ the arrows into $R_{N_-}$ refute $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{et}(\mathfrak R)\to\operatorname{CH}(\mathfrak R)$ and those into $R_{N_+}$ its counterpart with $\neg\operatorname{CH}$.

settings.construction: Let $T$ be C together with $\Box$Atomlessness, $\Box I^*_e$ and the negation of BF at type $t$, a recursively axiomatized theory. $T$ holds in finite-support-monotone-maps, which is atomless, fails BF at type $t$, and has infinitely many individuals and the standard numerals as its numbers at $e$ (the property of being a numeral is pinned down by $\emptyset$); it has one object, so its boxes are idle. So $T$ is consistent, by soundness. $T$ proves $I^*_e$, and so the Peano axioms for its numbers at $e$, so by Gödel's second incompleteness theorem $T+\neg\operatorname{Con}(T)$ is consistent, and by the completeness of action models for C (Classicism, Theorem 3.23: every formula consistent with C holds at some world of some action model) it holds at an object $V_2$ of some action model. The single component is that model cut down to the objects reachable from $V_2$, so that every closed sentence keeps its truth value at each object. The root $W_0$ is built over it exactly as in coalesced-pinned-substitutions-root: an arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ into each object $V$ of the component for each interpretation $I$ of $\Sigma^+$ there, and an arrow from $W_0$ to itself for each type-preserving map of the constants of $\Sigma^+$. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow. Interpretation of Σ as there. The write-up's argument that the root is a model of C does not use the completeness of the family of components, only that each is an action model of C.

arguments.text: The arrows out of $W_0$ end at $W_0$ (the maps of the constants) or at objects of the component, and a closed sentence holds at an arrow iff it holds at the identity of its target. At every object of the component Atomlessness holds, by $\Box$Atomlessness at $V_2$, the component being generated from $V_2$. At $W_0$ it holds by the argument atomlessness of coalesced-pinned-substitutions-root, which uses of the components only that $\top\ne\bot$ at each of their objects: a possible $p$ pinned down by $S$ that contains a map is split by a fresh individual constant, and one that contains only arrows into the component by a fresh propositional constant sent to $\top$ or to $\bot$. So $\Box$Atomlessness holds. BF holds at every type by the argument barcan of that model, which uses only fresh constants.

arguments.text:
At type $e$. $W_0$ is extensionally full at its identity: any set of tuples there is the extension of the entity with that value at every map of the constants and $ ot$ at every arrow into the component, pinned down by $\emptyset$ and landing. So the property with the numerals as its extension is an inductive property at $W_0$, the numbers there are the standard numerals, and Sum and Prod are standard on them (a relation refuting a false instance is in the domain). The individuals at $W_0$ are the infinitely many individual constants, so distinct numerals are distinct there and $I^*_e$ holds at $W_0$, and it holds throughout the component by $\Box I^*_e$ at $V_2$; so $\Box I^*_e$ holds at $W_0$. With $A:=\operatorname{Con}(T)$, an arithmetical sentence, $A$ holds at $W_0$, whose arithmetic is standard, and fails at $V_2$; so neither $\Box(I	o A)$ nor $\Box(I	o
eg A)$ holds at $W_0$, and the Necessity of Arithmetic fails. The Necessity of Analysis fails as in coalesced-two-extensional-arithmetics-root, with $W_0$ and $V_2$ for the two components: the Dedekind cuts over the numbers form a real number structure at each, every real number structure at a world is isomorphic to it, and $\exists n\in N\,.\,\operatorname{Proof}_T(n, ot)$ is false in those at $W_0$ and true in those at $V_2$. Arithmetic Necessitism fails by the inextensibility of $\mathbb N_e$: let $X:=\lambda x\, .\,\mathbb N x\land
eg\exists m\in\mathbb N\, .\,m<x\land \operatorname{Proof}_T(m, ot)$, a closed pure term. Each number at $W_0$ is a numeral $\mathbf n$, and at every world $X\mathbf n$ holds, since under $I^*_e$ the numbers below $\mathbf n$ are the numerals below it and each $
eg\operatorname{Proof}_T(\mathbf m, ot)$ is a true bounded sentence, $T$ being consistent. But at $V_2$ some number $m$ codes a proof of $ ot$ from $T$, and $\operatorname{Suc}m$ is a number lacking $X$; so $\mathbb N_e\le X$ fails. The Axiom of Infinity (type e) holds at $W_0$: its finite cardinalities are the numerals, and none holds of the universal property, which has infinitely many instances there.

So both necessitated bridge principles for atoms hold at every type. Self-atoms are atoms (type t) fails at $W_0$: the proposition $P$ true exactly at the arrows into $V$ is pinned down by $\emptyset$, with transport $\top$ along every $\langle V,I\rangle$, so it lands; it is possible, and wherever it is true it is $\top$ at $V$, an atom, so it is a self-atom, but not an atom at the atomless $W_0$.

domains.text: An entity at $W_0$ of a relational type is an intension over the arrows out of $W_0$ that is pinned down by a finite set $S$ of constants of $\Sigma^+$ (two arrows $\langle V,I\rangle$, $\langle V,I^{\prime}\rangle$ with $I{\restriction}S=I^{\prime}{\restriction}S$, or two maps of the constants agreeing on $S$, give it the same value) and whose transport along every arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ is in the domain of $V$ in its component. Transport along a map $f$ keeps an entity in the domain: it is pinned down by $f(S)$, and its transports are transports of the original.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 25 October 2026
arguments.text: Self-atoms are atoms (type t) fails at the root, and with it Self-atoms are strong atoms (type t). Some component has an object $V$ satisfying Actuality, with true atom $a_V$, since the components are complete and Actuality is consistent with C(Σ); and $a_V$ is a self-atom, so for an arrow $m$ out of $V$ its transport is $a_V$ exactly when $m\in a_V$ (then $a_V$ is the true atom at $m$’s target, the atom containing the identity there), and otherwise excludes the identity. Let $c$ be a propositional constant of $\Sigma^+$ and $P$ the root proposition false at the identity and at every map of the constants and true exactly at the arrows $\langle V,I\rangle$ with $I(c)=a_V$: pinned down by $\{c\}$, with transport along such an arrow the set of $m$ with $m\cdot a_V=a_V$, that is $a_V$, an atom at $V$. So $P$ is possible and a self-atom. It is not an atom: for another propositional constant $c^{\prime}$, the arrows with $I(c)=a_V$ and $I(c^{\prime})=\top$ form a proper nonempty part pinned down by $\{c,c^{\prime}\}$.

arguments.text: At every type, in the form $\Diamond\exists x\, .\,Fx\to\exists x\, .\,\Diamond Fx$, for $F$ pinned down by a finite $S$. A witness $y$ at an arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ is handled as in coalesced-pinned-interpretations-root, by a fresh constant $c$ with $I^{\prime}(c)=y$. A witness $y$ at a map $f$ is an entity at $W_0$, pinned down by some finite $S_y$: let $g$ send $S_y$ to fresh constants outside $S$, and $f^{\prime}$ agree with $f$ on $S$ and send them back, so that $f^{\prime}\circ g$ fixes $S_y$. Then $F$ holds at $f^{\prime}$ of $y=f^{\prime}\cdot(g\cdot y)$, so $\Diamond F(g\cdot y)$.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: A closed sentence of $\Sigma$ holds at $\langle V,I\rangle$ iff it holds at $V$ in its component under the restriction of $I$ to $\Sigma$, the constants of $\Sigma$ denoting the entities $\hat c$. Every $\Sigma$-sentence consistent with C($\Sigma$) holds at the root of some model in $A$ under some interpretation, which extends to $\Sigma^+$, so it is possible at $W_0$: Maximalism for $\Sigma$ in its possibility form, and with it the pure form.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: A true proposition pinned down by a finite $S$ contains every map of the constants fixing $S$ pointwise, since such a map agrees with the identity on $S$. For a constant $c\notin S$ the set of maps fixing $S\cup\{c\}$, together with no arrow into a component, is a truth not entailed by it: a map fixing $S$ and moving $c$ separates them. So no truth entails every truth, as in the all-maps finitely pinned model.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: The arguments of finite-support-two-object-all-maps carry over, the maps of the constants playing the part of the maps of $\mathbb N$, with every proposition used containing no arrow into a component, so that its transports there are empty and land. Truths are ND-necessary: the transposition of two constants $c,d$ is invertible, so it sees every truth, while the true proposition that $c$ is fixed is false there. Vicinity: a truth pinned down by $S$ contains a map fixing $S$ that collapses two individual constants outside $S$; that they are distinct is true and possible at no world seen from there. Weakly Inextensible Comprehension at type $t\to t$: as there, for the propositions $p_c$ that the individual constant $c$ is fixed, the test property $X$ being defined at the maps as there and as the property of being $\bot$ at the arrows into components, which is definable and so lands. Boolean Completeness at type $t$: enumerate the individual constants and take the propositions $A_m$ that a map is constant on the first $2m$ of them and first changes value at the next, whose least pinned covers strictly shrink; the property with that family as its value at every map and empty at the components is in the domain.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: Let $p$ be possible, pinned down by a finite $S$. If $p$ contains a map $f$, the maps in $p$ agreeing with $f$ at a fresh individual constant $c$ form a possible proposition below $p$, pinned down by $S\cup\{c\}$ and landing (it has no arrow into a component), and a map agreeing with $f$ on $S$ and not at $c$ shows that it is not $p$. Otherwise $p$ contains some $\langle V,I\rangle$; for a fresh constant $c$ of type $t$, the members of $p$ whose interpretation sends $c$ to $\top$ form a proposition pinned down by $S\cup\{c\}$ whose transports are the conjunctions of those of $p$ with the propositions that the interpretation of $c$ is $\top$, so it lands; it is possible and below $p$, and an interpretation agreeing with $I$ on $S$ and sending $c$ to $\bot$ shows it is not $p$. The atom of finite-support-two-object-all-maps, at its singleton object, has no counterpart.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: As in collapse-at-root of finite-support-two-object-all-maps. Write $\mathrm{fix}_S$ for the maps of the constants fixing the finite set $S$ pointwise, the least truth pinned down by $S$, and $\delta_S$ for the maps injective on $S$. $\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}_S=\delta_S$: no composite with an arrow into a component is a map, and a map injective on $S$ is undone on $S$ by another. At a map $k$, $\Diamond_{\ne}$ of the transport of $\mathrm{fix}_S$ holds iff $k\in\delta_S$, and at an arrow into a component that transport is $\bot$; so $\hat\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}_S=\delta_S$ too, and $\Box_{\ne}$ and $\hat{\hat\Box}$ coincide, each holding of exactly the propositions containing some $\delta_S$. BF at type $t$ holds for $\hat{\hat\Box}$: an arrow in $\delta_N$ agrees on any pinning set with a bijection $b$ of the constants, and an entity pinned down there has at it the value it has at $b$, which contains every transport along $b$, that is, everything. So by Proposition D8 of The Bounds of Possibility $\Box_5$ implies two-hat necessity. The truth $\mathrm{fix}_{\{c\}}$ is not two-hat necessary, every $\delta_S$ containing a bijection moving $c$, so not 5-necessary.

arguments.text: A self-atom of any relational type at an object $W$ is instantiated at some arrow $k$ out of $W$, and its transport along $k$ is an atom at $k$’s target instantiated at the identity there. The existential projection of an atom $I$ of a relational type, the proposition $\exists\bar x\, .\,I\bar x$, is an atom of type $t$: it is in the domain, it is not bottom, and for any proposition $p$ the entity $I\land\lambda\bar x\, .\,p$ lies below the atom $I$, so is $I$ or bottom, which puts $p$ above the projection or disjoint from it. So the projection is a true atom at $k$’s target, which the condition excludes. Hence no reachable object has a self-atom, and Self-atoms are atoms and Self-atoms are strong atoms hold vacuously at every type and every reachable object, while Self-Atomicity (type t) fails at the evaluation point, the top proposition having no self-atom below it.

conditions.text: Actuality fails at the identity of every object reachable from the evaluation point: no atom of the domain of propositions there contains that identity. In a one-object model this is the failure of Actuality at the evaluation point, Actuality being a closed sentence.

The root $W_0$ has an arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ for each interpretation $I$ of $\Sigma^+$ at $V$ and an arrow to itself for each type-preserving map of the constants of $\Sigma^+$. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow. Interpretation of Σ as there. The write-up's argument that the root is a model of C uses only that each component is an action model of C.

As for interpretation arrows, and the root has besides an arrow to itself for every type-preserving map of the signature's constants to themselves, acting on the root's individuals and composing with the interpretation arrows by precomposition.

As in coalesced-pinned-substitutions-root, intensions over the arrows out of $W_0$ pinned down by a finite set of constants of $\Sigma^+$, whose transports along the arrows into $V$ land in its domains.

met.no-actuality-anywhere: The objects reachable from $W_0$ are $W_0$ and $V$. Actuality fails at $V$, as recorded for finite-support-truncations, and at $W_0$, where Atomlessness holds (argument atomlessness), there being no atom at all.

arguments.text: Let $N$ and $M$ be two components whose roots satisfy Actuality, with true atoms $a_N$ and $a_M$, and let $P$ be the root proposition false at the root, with component $a_N$ at $N$, $a_M$ at $M$ and bottom elsewhere. $P$ is possible, and it is a self-atom: under the distinguished arrow into $N$ it becomes $a_N$, and a true atom is a self-atom, as it entails every truth, including the truth that it entails every truth; likewise at $M$; and at the root it is false. It is not an atom, since the root proposition with component $a_N$ alone lies strictly below it. So Self-atoms are atoms (type t) fails at the root, and with it Self-atoms are strong atoms (type t).

models.definition:
Take the alternative coalesced-sum root of Appendix E, p. 83: a set of source action models complete for C, coalesced at a new root whose individual domain is a singleton, the unique root individual being carried by each distinguished arrow to a chosen individual of that component. Evaluation point: the root.

The root has one distinguished arrow to the root of each component, and every arrow from the root into a component factors through it.

Root domains are as full as compatibility allows: a root proposition is a choice, for each component, of a proposition of that component’s root domain, together with a truth value at the root’s identity arrow, and a root entity of a relational type is likewise a family of component entities with a root component that is an arbitrary function of the root arguments.

references.note: The coalesced sum, with an arrow for every interpretation into every component object and the fullest root domains compatible with the components.

settings.construction: Fix a set $A$ of action models complete for C($\Sigma$), with disjoint objects and arrows, and a signature $\Sigma^+\supseteq\Sigma$ with countably infinitely many constants of every type. Add an object $W_0$. Its arrows out are, for each object $V$ of a model in $A$ and each interpretation $I$ of $\Sigma^+$ at $V$, an arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ into $V$, with $k\circ\langle V,I\rangle=\langle V^{\prime},k\cdot I\rangle$ for an arrow $k:V\to V^{\prime}$ of the component; and for every type-preserving map $f$ of the constants of $\Sigma^+$ to themselves an arrow $f:W_0\to W_0$, the identity map being $1_{W_0}$, with maps composing as functions and $\langle V,I\rangle\circ f=\langle V,I\circ f\rangle$. The individuals at $W_0$ are the individual constants of $\Sigma^+$; $\langle V,I\rangle$ sends each to its interpretation and $f$ acts on them as on constants. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow. Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: each constant $c$ of Σ denotes $\hat c$, with transport $I(c)$ along $\langle V,I\rangle$, empty extension at every map, and $f\cdot\hat c=\widehat{f(c)}$.

domains.text: An entity at $W_0$ of a relational type is any intension over the arrows out of $W_0$ whose transport along every arrow $\langle V,I\rangle$ is in the domain of $V$ in its component. Transport along a map $f$ keeps an entity in the domain, its transports along the $\langle V,I\rangle$ being transports of the original along the $\langle V,I\circ f\rangle$.

meets.complete-components: The models in $A$ are complete for C($\Sigma$), so in particular for C.
meets.free-root-component: Any extension at the identity of $W_0$ is that of the entity with that extension at the identity and the empty extension at every other arrow, whose transports into the components are empty.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: The proposition $a:=\{1_{W_0}\}$ is in the domain: its transport along a map $f$ is $\{m:m\circ f=1_{W_0}\}$, a set of maps, and along every $\langle V,I\rangle$ it is empty. It is true, and it entails every truth, since a truth contains $1_{W_0}$.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: As in coalesced-pinned-substitutions-root, whose arguments use only the arrows $\langle V,I\rangle$. A $\Sigma$-formula holds of individual constants $\bar c$ at $\langle V,I\rangle$ iff it holds of $I(\bar c)$ at $V$ under the restriction of $I$ to $\Sigma$. A closed $\Sigma$-sentence consistent with C($\Sigma$) holds at the root of some model in $A$ under some interpretation, which extends to $\Sigma^+$; and a $\Sigma$-formula $P(\bar x)$ consistent with C($\Sigma$) holds there of some $\bar b$, and for distinct $\bar c$ an $I$ with $I(\bar c)=\bar b$ makes $P(\bar c)$ possible at $W_0$. So Maximalism and Possibility+ hold for $\Sigma$, and with them the pure forms.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: The functionality of a subrelation is evaluated at the root’s identity arrow only, while the subrelation condition is boxed; so for a serial root relation take the subrelation whose root component is a functional choice from the root component, by choice in the metatheory, and whose component parts are empty. Where some component refutes Relational Choice at its root, as when the components are complete for C, its necessitation fails.

references.note: The coalesced sum, here of a single one-world component.

settings.construction: The component is a one-world Henkin model $H$, as an action model with one object and only its identity arrow. Its individuals are labels $L_i$ and options $A_i^0,A_i^1$ ($i\in\mathbb N$). The group $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ acts on them, $g$ fixing each $L_i$ and sending $A_i^\epsilon$ to $A_i^{\epsilon+g(i)}$ (mod 2), and on functions by conjugation; its domain of each relational type $\sigma\tau$ holds the functions from $D_\sigma$ to $D_\tau$ fixed by every group element that is $0$ on some finite set, and $D_t=\{0,1\}$. These domains are closed under the logical constants and lambda abstraction, terms denoting equivariantly, so $H$ is an extensional Henkin model of C. Coalesce $H$ at a new root as in Definition E.2. The root's individuals are those of $H$, carried to themselves by the arrow into $H$. Evaluation point: the root. Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

meets.free-root-component: The root domains are as full as compatibility allows.
meets.sigma-top: This is the interpretation the construction fixes.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), prompted by Daniel Kodsi, 26 October 2026; checked and recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: At the types $e$ and $e$. In $H$, let $U$ relate each $L_i$ to $A_i^0$ and $A_i^1$, and each option to $L_0$: it is fixed by the whole group, so in the domain, and serial. No functional subrelation $S$ of $U$ is in the domain of $H$: $S$ is fixed by the group elements that are $0$ on some finite set $N$; for $i\notin N$, the element swapping the two options of pair $i$ alone fixes $S$ and $L_i$, so it carries the $S$-output of $L_i$, one of those options, to a second $S$-output. Now let $R$ be the root relation with the universal relation as its root component and $U$ as its component in $H$: it is necessarily serial. A necessarily functional $S\le R$ would have as its component in $H$ a functional subrelation of $U$ in the domain of $H$. So Modalized Relational Choice fails, and with it □Relational Choice.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), prompted by Daniel Kodsi, 26 October 2026; checked and recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: In $H$, a property with an instance $b$ entails the haecceity of $b$, which is in the domain, being fixed by whatever fixes $b$. At the root, let $F$ be necessarily instantiated: its root component has an instance $a$ and its component in $H$ an instance $b$. The root property with root component $\{a\}$ and the haecceity of $b$ as its component entails $F$ and is necessarily uniquely instantiated; it does not matter that $b$ need not be the image of $a$. So Intensional Choice holds at both objects.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), prompted by Daniel Kodsi, 26 October 2026; checked and recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: The arrow into $H$ carries the root domains onto those of $H$ at every type: an entity of $H$ is the component of the root entity with that component and an empty root component, and individuals go to themselves. So if $Fx$ is necessary for every root $x$, $F$'s component holds of every entity of $H$, and $\forall x\,.\,Fx$ is necessary: BF holds at the root, and trivially in the one-world $H$. There are four root propositions and two in $H$, so Boolean Completeness (type $t$) holds at both objects.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: In $H$ the singletons of tuples are fixed by whatever fixes their entries, so $H$ is atomic, and in a one-world model atoms are strong atoms. At the root, the singletons of root tuples with empty $H$-component, and the entities with empty root extension and a singleton $H$-component, are atoms, every nonzero entity is above one, and both kinds are strong atoms. A self-atom instantiated at the root is an atom; one instantiated only at $a$ has empty root extension and an atom of $H$ as $H$-component, so it is an atom too.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: Root extensions are arbitrary, so the property of cardinalities that hold at the root only of properties with finite root extension is in the domain, and the argument infinitely-many-individuals runs at the root, which has infinitely many individuals. There are four propositions at the root and two in $H$.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: At $\sigma=e$. Let $P_i$ have empty root extension and $H$-component $\{A_i^0\}$. An upper bound has an $H$-component containing every $A_i^0$, fixed by the swaps vanishing on some finite $N$, so containing $A_i^1$ for $i\notin N$; removing one such $A_j^1$ gives a smaller upper bound. The numbers at $e$ at the root are the distinct numerals, root extensions being arbitrary, and the relation pairing $P_i$ with the $i$th numeral is in the domain, so the family is countable relative to $e$.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: The numerals are fixed by the whole group, so the property of being a numeral is admitted in $H$ and at the root, and the numbers at every type are the numerals, crisply. A type is finite at both objects (those built from $t$ alone) or infinite at both; at a finite type $I_\sigma$ fails everywhere, and at an infinite one every relation among numerals is fixed by the group, so sum and product are standard at both objects. Persistence and inextensibility of the numbers are as in arithmetic-necessitism-extensionally-full.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: In the one-world $H$ every relation is rigid, so rigidity at the root is weak rigidity there, and Tame Rigidity holds. Rigid Power: a rigid root $F$ with root extension $S$ has as $H$-component the least finitely supported superset $T$ of $a\cdot S$. For a finitely supported $T'\subseteq T$, let $S'$ be the members of $S$ sent into $T'$: any finitely supported $T''\supseteq a\cdot S'$ gives the finitely supported superset $(T''\cap T')\cup(T\setminus T')$ of $a\cdot S$, so $T''\supseteq T'$, and $(S',T')$ is rigid and below $F$. So the rigid relations below $F$ in $H$ are the transports of rigid ones at the root, and the power property of $F$ is weakly rigid, hence rigid. In $H$ the principle is trivial.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: Both hold at the root (recorded) and trivially in the one-world $H$.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: Distinctness-Necessity at $t$ fails at the root and holds in the one-world $H$; so its negation is true at the root and not possible at $a$.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: At the root real number structures are standard, root extensions being arbitrary. In $H$, a real number structure has a carrier and relations fixed by the swaps vanishing on some finite $N$, each of which acts as an order-automorphism of a complete ordered field, hence trivially on the carrier; so every subset of the carrier and every relation on it is admitted, and the structure is standard with full second-order quantification. So an analytical sentence is true in every real number structure at every world, or false in every one.

models.notes: Recorded for the separation of Relational Choice with Intensional Choice from Modalized Relational Choice: Relational Choice holds at the root by choice in the metatheory (the group's argument relational-choice-free-root), while the choice-free component $H$ has no selector for its pair relation.
