models.definition:
An ideally full action model in the sense of Classicism, Appendix D, over a category with two objects, each carrying the ideal of finite sets: a model of C by Proposition D.4. The member's construction and evaluation point follow.

The model of finite-support-two-object-all-maps: two objects, $W_0=\mathbb N$ and $W_1=\{0\}$, with all functions between them as arrows, $W_i^\ddagger$ the finite subsets of $W_i$, ideally full. Evaluation point: $W_1$, at its identity arrow. The worlds it sees are its identity and the maps $c_n:0\mapsto n$ into $W_0$.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

meets.infinitely-many-propositions-everywhere: At $W_1$ every set of the arrows $1_{W_1}$ and $c_n:0\mapsto n$ is pinned down by $\{0\}$; at $W_0$ the sets of arrows pinned down by a finite set are infinitely many.
meets.sigma-top: This is the interpretation the definition fixes.
meets.codomain-intensions: The model is ideally full at both objects, and an intension whose value at an arrow depends only on the arrow's codomain is pinned down by $\emptyset$.
meets.extensionally-full: Every intension at $W_1$ is in the domain (see the argument for Atomicity), so any set of tuples is the extension at the identity of one of them.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 25 October 2026
arguments.text: At $W_1$ the true atom is $\{1_{W_1}\}$, which under $c_n$ becomes $\{!\}$, a set of one arrow, so it is a strong atom and Strong Actuality holds. It fails at $W_0$, which $c_n$ reaches, since Actuality fails there; so □Strong Actuality fails. The self-atoms are $\{1_{W_1}\}$ at $W_1$ and $\{!\}$ at $W_0$, both strong atoms, and at relational types they carry one tuple (the argument of finite-support-two-object-all-maps); so Self-atoms are strong atoms holds at both objects, at every type.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: An arrow out of $W_1$ is fixed by its value at $0$, so any two arrows with a common target that agree on $\{0\}$ are equal, and every intension at $W_1$ is pinned down by $\{0\}$. The model being ideally full, every domain at $W_1$ holds all intensions of its type, ordered by inclusion at each arrow: a complete atomic Boolean algebra. So Atomicity and Boolean Completeness hold at every type, and the singleton of the identity arrow is a true proposition entailing every truth.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: A closed sentence holds at $c_n$ iff it holds at the identity of $W_0$, the evaluation point of finite-support-two-object-all-maps. Boolean Completeness (type t) fails there by that model's argument; and Atomicity (type t) fails there, since BF holds and Inextensible Comprehension fails, while Atomicity (type t) with BF gives $\Box$Actuality, hence Actuality, which with BF gives Inextensible Comprehension. So neither is necessary at $W_1$.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: At $W_1$ there is one individual, at $c_n$ the natural numbers. The closed pure sentence that there is exactly one individual is true at $W_1$ and false at each $c_n$, so No Pure Contingency fails, as does the Infinity Schema (type e) at $W_1$. BF fails for the haecceity of $0$: it holds necessarily of every individual, but not of every individual at $c_n$. The Axiom of Infinity (type e) holds at $c_n$, by the argument of finite-support-two-object-all-maps, so it is possible.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: ND holds at $W_1$: $(c_n\cdot Y)_k=Y_{k\circ c_n}$, and $k\circ c_n$ is $1_{W_1}$ for the map back to $W_1$ and $c_m$ for each $m$ as $k$ ranges over the maps on $\mathbb N$, so transport along $c_n$ determines $Y$ at every world. Given $U$ functional at the identity with values $Z_y$, put $X_k:=\{(k\cdot y,\bar a):\bar a\in(Z_y)_k\}$, well defined by ND, and in the domain, which at $W_1$ holds every intension (see full-at-singleton); and $Xy=Z_y$.

withdrawn.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, after a trawl subagent's report
withdrawn.reason: The step from the equality of transports to membership in the carrier by inextensibility does not follow: inextensibility bounds a rigid carrier from above, by the transports of its actual instances, and puts nothing new into its actual extension.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: At $W_1$, at type $t$. The propositions at $W_1$ are all the sets of its arrows out, the identity and the $c_n$, each such set being pinned down by $\{0\}$; they are continuum many, and the model being extensionally full at $W_1$ there is a real number structure of propositions there, complete since every subset of its carrier is the extension of a subproperty. Suppose $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid one, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$. Its boxed clauses hold at $c_1$ and along the arrows after it, and $X_{c_1}$, its instances at $W_0$, is a complete ordered field there. But no proposition $x$ at $W_0$ is determined by its transport along the arrow $k$ of $W_0$ collapsing $0$ and $1$: with $q$ the set of arrows out of $W_0$ separating $0$ from $1$, pinned down by $\{0,1\}$ and containing no arrow after $k$, $y:=x\mathbin{\triangle}q$ is in the domain, differs from $x$, and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$; for $x\in X_{c_1}$ persistence gives $k\cdot y\in X_{k\circ c_1}$, inextensibility $y\in X_{c_1}$, and necessary distinctness $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$. So $X_{c_1}$ is empty, a contradiction, and Analytic Necessitism fails.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: All maps between the objects are arrows, so from $1_{W_1}$ and from $1_{W_0}$ both identities are reachable, and a closed sentence holds at an arrow iff at its codomain's identity. So a boxed sentence holds at $W_1$ iff at $W_0$, the evaluation point of finite-support-two-object-all-maps, whose verdicts these are.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: An arrow out of $W_1$ is fixed by its value at $0$, so every intension at $W_1$ is pinned down by $\{0\}$ and in the domain. A weakly rigid $Y$ with extension $E$ is therefore the exact image $h\mapsto h\cdot E$: weak persistence gives one inclusion, weak inextensibility tested against that exact image the other; and exact images are rigid.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, in a trawl for cheaply settled verdicts; checked by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: The propositions at $W_1$ are all the sets of its arrows out, continuum many, and the model is extensionally full there, so completeness, finiteness, size and isomorphism are the external notions. A complete Boolean algebra that is Dedekind finite or smaller than the continuum is finite, with $2^k$ elements, and isomorphic to the propositions below $\{c_0,\ldots,c_{k-1}\}$, which is not $\top$.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, auditing the withdrawn arguments for the failure of Analytic Necessitism
arguments.text: At type $\tau:=tt$. For each object $V$ reachable from the evaluation point fix an injection $A\mapsto E^A_V$ from the sets of natural numbers into the sets of propositions at $V$, possible as these are infinitely many, and let $Y_A$ be the intension whose value at an arrow into $V$ is $E^A_V$: it depends only on the codomain, so it is in the domain, and its transport along an arrow into $V$ is the $Y_A$ of $V$, distinct for distinct $A$. Carry the real numbers onto the $Y_A$ and take as relations the codomain-only intensions whose value at $V$ is the corresponding set of tuples of the $Y_A$ of $V$. Along every arrow the structure is carried to the like structure at the target, an isomorphic copy, which is a real number structure there: bounded sets of its elements have least upper bounds among them and every inductive subproperty contains its natural numbers. Such a structure is rigid, its instances are necessarily distinct, and it is necessarily a real number structure; and the codomain-only intension of type $((\tau)^kt)t$ whose value at each object is the set of codomain-only $k$-ary relations among the carrier there is a represented power of arity $k$, since at every world each $k$-ary relation agrees on the carrier with one of them. So the consequents of Analytic Necessitism and of its second-order form hold, and both principles hold. (The argument of the withdrawn analytic-necessitism-unretracted-arrow would refute this structure; its step from inextensibility is the gap.)

withdrawn.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
withdrawn.reason: The stated hypotheses do not establish the native all-carrier AN/SOAN schemata. A structure at tt (or another selected carrier) does not answer an instance at e or t. A counterexample is the full one-object model on the countable monoid with an absorbing zero and fixed natural-number individuals, where an actual real field at t has no necessarily distinct carrier. See [proof](../writeups/analytic-necessitism-carrier-correction.md), sections 1–3, for the full countermodels and exact condition checks. The original text and attribution are preserved; its selected-carrier construction is not rejected by this withdrawal.

conditions.text: At every object reachable from the evaluation point, the domain contains every intension whose value at an arrow depends only on the arrow's codomain.
conditions.reason: The model is ideally full at both objects, and an intension whose value at an arrow depends only on the arrow's codomain is pinned down by $\emptyset$.

conditions.text: There are infinitely many propositions at every object reachable from the evaluation point.
conditions.reason: At $W_1$ every set of the arrows $1_{W_1}$ and $c_n:0\mapsto n$ is pinned down by $\{0\}$; at $W_0$ the sets of arrows pinned down by a finite set are infinitely many.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: The numbers at a type $\sigma$ are the instances of $\mathbb N_\sigma$, the least property containing $\mathbf 0_\sigma$ and closed under $\operatorname{Suc}_\sigma$ (Background); the numerals $\mathbf 0_\sigma$, $\operatorname{Suc}_\sigma\mathbf 0_\sigma,\ldots$ are closed terms, so each denotes at every object, and transport along an arrow carries its denotation at the source to its denotation at the target. At any object $v$ reachable from the evaluation point, extensional fullness gives a property whose extension at $v$ is exactly the numerals there; it contains $\mathbf 0_\sigma$ and is closed under successor, so the numbers at $v$ are exactly the numerals, every numeral being an instance of every inductive property. Persistence of $\mathbb N_\sigma$ and, given $\Box I^*_\sigma$, the necessary distinctness of the numbers are theorems of C (the proof of necessary-rigid-comprehension-implies-arithmetic-necessitism). Inextensibility, $\Box\forall X\,.\,(\forall n\,.\,\mathbb N_\sigma n\to\Box Xn)\to\mathbb N_\sigma\le X$: at a reachable $v$ and for an arrow $j$ from $v$ to $u$, the numbers at $u$ are the numerals there, which are the transports along $j$ of the numbers at $v$, so any $X$ that necessarily holds of the numbers at $v$ holds at $u$ of the numbers there. So $\mathbb N_\sigma$ is rigid, and Arithmetic Necessitism holds at every type. No choice is used.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, at Cian Dorr's suggestion
arguments.text: For each object $U$ and type $\sigma$ fix a well-ordering $<_U$ of the domain $D^\sigma_U$, and let $W$ be the intension of type $\sigma\to\sigma\to t$ with $W(h):={<_{\operatorname{cod}h}}$. Its value depends only on the arrow's codomain, so by the condition it is in the domain, and at every world its extension well-orders that world's type-$\sigma$ domain. Given $F$ with $\Box\exists x\, .\,Fx$, put $G:=\lambda x\, .\,Fx\land\forall y\, .\,(Fy\to\neg Wyx)$, the $W$-least $F$. It is definable from $F$ and $W$, so in the domain; $G\le F$, and its extension at every arrow is the singleton of the least element of $F$'s. So Intensional Choice holds, and the same at every reachable object gives $\Box$Intensional Choice. Cian Dorr's observation that such models are qualitatively full, made precise.

arguments.text: At any reachable object $W$, let $U$ be a serial relation in the domain there. Using the axiom of choice, pick for each $x$ a $y$ with $(x,y)$ in the extension of $U$ at the identity, and let $S$ be the intension whose value at every arrow $W\to W$ is the graph of this choice and whose value at arrows with any other codomain is empty; it depends only on the codomain, so the condition puts it in the domain, and at the identity it is a functional subrelation of $U$. Likewise a set of representatives of an equivalence relation at $W$, made into such an intension, is a transversal. Since $W$ was any reachable object, both principles hold at every world.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: Let $v$ be any object reachable from the evaluation point and $\mathfrak R$ a real number structure at $v$ (Background, Analysis). Its completeness is tested against the subproperties of its carrier present at $v$, and by extensional fullness every subset of the carrier's extension there is the extension at the identity of one of them; so the carrier, with the extensions of $\le$, $+$ and $\times$, is a complete ordered field in the sense of the metatheory and, by Huntington's theorem, a theorem of ZF, is isomorphic to the real numbers. For the same reason the extension of $N$, the least subproperty containing $0$ and closed under adding $1$, is its set of natural numbers, that set being the extension of a subproperty. A second-order analytical sentence $A(\mathfrak R)$ quantifies over the relations among entities of the structure's type at $v$, applied to the structure's elements, and their extensions at the identity are all the relations on the carrier, again by extensional fullness. So $A(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $v$ exactly when $A$ holds in the real numbers under full second-order semantics, which depends neither on $v$ nor on $\mathfrak R$. Hence $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to A(\mathfrak R)$ holds when $A$ is true of the reals and $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to\neg A(\mathfrak R)$ when it is false: every instance of the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, and with it the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis, as recorded. No choice is used.

models.definition:
An ideally full action model in the sense of Classicism, Appendix D, over a category with two objects, each carrying the ideal of finite sets: a model of C by Proposition D.4. The member's construction and evaluation point follow.

Appendix D, p. 79, the paragraph beginning “One particularly interesting result”: two objects, $W_0=\mathbb N$ and $W_1=\{0\}$, with all functions between them as arrows, $W_i^\ddagger$ the finite subsets of $W_i$, and the model ideally full as in Proposition D.5. Evaluation point: $W_0$, at its identity arrow.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

meets.infinitely-many-propositions-everywhere: At $W_0$ the sets of arrows pinned down by a finite set are infinitely many; at $W_1$ every set of the arrows $1_{W_1}$ and $c_n:0\mapsto n$ is pinned down by $\{0\}$.
meets.finitely-pinned-domains: Ideally full with the ideal of finite sets: every intension pinned down by a finite set is in the domain, and every entity in a domain is one.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions at $W_0$ include, for each $n$, the set of arrows sending $0$ to $n$.
meets.non-injective-arrow: Any non-injective map of $\mathbb N$, say the constant map with value $0$, is an arrow out of $W_0$.
meets.codomain-intensions: The model is ideally full at both objects, and an intension whose value at an arrow depends only on the arrow's codomain is pinned down by $\emptyset$ (Appendix D, the remark after Definition D.3).
meets.sigma-top: This is the interpretation the definition fixes.
meets.extensionally-full: The model is ideally full, hence extensionally full at every object (Appendix D, the remark after Definition D.3).

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 25 October 2026
arguments.text: Write $!$ for the only arrow $W_0\to W_1$ and $c_n$ for the arrow $W_1\to W_0$ with value $n$. At $W_1$ every proposition is pinned down by $\{0\}$, so the domain is full and the atoms are the singletons. $\{c_n\}$ is not a self-atom: its transport along $c_n$ is the set of maps $m$ of $\mathbb N$ with $m(n)=n$, pinned down by $\{n\}$ but not an atom. So Atoms are self-atoms (type t), and with it Atoms are strong atoms (type t), fail at $W_1$, which $!$ reaches, and their boxed forms fail at $W_0$. No self-atom contains an arrow into $W_0$ at either object, since its transport along that arrow would be an atom containing $1_{W_0}$ and Actuality fails at $W_0$; so the self-atoms are $\{1_{W_1}\}$ at $W_1$ and $\{!\}$ at $W_0$, the latter pinned down by $\varnothing$ and an atom. Both are strong atoms: $\{!\}$ becomes $\{1_{W_1}\}$ under $!$ and $\{!\}$ under any map of $\mathbb N$, and $\{1_{W_1}\}$ becomes $\{!\}$ under $c_n$. A self-atom of a relational type has a self-atom as its existential projection, so sits over one of these, with one tuple, by the transport condition; so it is an atom and a strong atom. Hence Self-atoms are atoms and Self-atoms are strong atoms hold at both objects, at every type.

BF holds at $W_0$, since every map agrees on any finite set with a surjection, and fails at $W_1$, where $\forall y\,\Box\,x=y$ holds of the one individual but $\Box\forall y\,x=y$ does not; so BF holds without $\Box$BF.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: The closed sentence that there is exactly one individual denotes the singleton of the unique map to $W_1$, a nonempty proposition with no nonempty proper subproposition.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: The individuals are the natural numbers and identity at the evaluation arrow is literal, so no numeral counts them. The propositions that a given individual is fixed by the arrow, one for each individual, are pairwise distinct and each has that individual as finite support, so there are infinitely many propositions. The set of numerals at each type is invariant under every arrow, hence has empty support and lies in the domain, so finite cardinality is standard and no finite cardinality holds of the universal property at either type.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: The transposition of $5$ and $6$ is an arrow with an inverse, so for any true $q$ the composite of a member of $q$ with the inverse carries the transposition into $q$, making $\Diamond q$ true there, while the true proposition that $5$ is fixed is false there.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr (observation); recorded by Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: The model is ideally full, hence extensionally full at every object (Appendix D, the remark after Definition D.3): for any set $R$ of tuples from the domains at an object $V$, the intension that assigns to every arrow out of $V$ into an object $U$ a fixed set $R_U$ of tuples from $U$’s domains, with $R_V=R$, is pinned down by $\emptyset$, so it is the intension of an element of $V^{\bar\sigma\to t}$ with extension $R$ at $1_V$. Given a relation $U$ serial at $V$, choose for each $x$ a $y$ with $(Ux)y$, by choice in the metatheory; the graph is such an $R$, and its element $S$ is functional and a subrelation of $U$ at $1_V$, both conditions being unboxed. The closed Relational Choice instance is true at an arrow $h\colon W_0\to V$ iff it is true at $1_V$ in the truncation by $h$, whose domains at $V$ are those of the model, so it holds at every arrow and $\Box$Relational Choice follows.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: Any set $F$ of propositions is the extension of the profile $\langle h,p\rangle\mapsto\{i : i\cdot p\in F\}$, and for $F$ the family of propositions $A_m$ that a map $W_0\to W_0$ is constant on $\{0,\ldots,2m-1\}$ and first changes value at $2m$, the least superset of $\bigcup F$ pinned down by $\{0,\ldots,N\}$, the maps whose first change is at an even position or beyond $N$, strictly shrinks as $N$ grows, so $F$ has no least upper bound. The family is countable in the model's sense, the relation pairing $A_m$ with the numeral $m$ being in the domain by extensional fullness, so Countable Boolean Completeness fails too.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr
arguments.text: At $W_0$ the finite cardinalities are the standard numerals and $I^*$ is true; at $W_1$ the numerals remain pairwise distinct, because they differ at the arrows back into $W_0$ and identity is necessary, $I^*$ is again true, the numerals are the finite cardinalities by extensional fullness, and $\operatorname{Sum}$ and $\operatorname{Prod}$ are standard, their graphs being in the domain; so every arithmetical sentence has its standard truth value at every world.

revisions.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
revisions.note: The Necessity of Arithmetic is now a schema in the type $\sigma$ whose finite cardinalities are the numbers, and the argument covers every $\sigma$ unchanged. At $W_0$ every type has infinitely many entities, so $I^*_\sigma$ is true there, and the numerals at $\sigma$ are standard by the argument for the Axioms of Infinity, whose set of numerals at each type is invariant under every arrow. At $W_1$ the numerals at $\sigma$ still differ at the arrows back into $W_0$, the set of them is in the domain and closed under zero and successor, and the graphs of $\operatorname{Sum}_\sigma$ and $\operatorname{Prod}_\sigma$ are in the domain, as at $e$.

arguments.text: At type $t\to t$, for the family $E$ of propositions $p_n$ that $n$ is fixed: for $Y$ inextensible with extension $E$ pinned down by the finite set $S$, pick $k\notin S$ and let $X$, pinned down by $S_X:=S\cup\{k\}$, hold at an arrow $h$ into $W_0$ exactly of the propositions $\{i : i(m)=n\}$ with $n\notin S_X$ and of the propositions $\{i : i(h(n))=n\}$ with $n\in S_X$; $X$ is necessary of every $p_n$, so $Y\le X$, yet at a map $h$ fixing $S$ pointwise and moving $k$, where $h\cdot Y=Y$, the extension of $X$ omits $p_k$.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), at Cian Dorr's request; checked and recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text:
Boxed Rigid Power, by lifting at each object; criterion (1) is part (1) of tame-rigidity-factorizable, which holds with several objects. Write $c$ for the map to the singleton and $i_n$ for the map from it with value $n$.
(a) Stable hulls. Let $F$ be rigid at $\mathbb N$ with extension $E$, $P$ a nonempty finite set containing a pin of $F$, and $A\subseteq E$ closed under the self-maps fixing $P$. Then $Y:=B_P(A)$ has extension $A$, lies below $F$, and is rigid. Weak rigidity at $\mathbb N$ is as in rigid-power-surjections, part (a), with self-maps (into the singleton, $r:=c$). For a self-map $h$, a member $k^{\prime}a$ of $Y_{kh}$ ($k^{\prime}$ agreeing with $kh$ on $P$) is $j(ra)$ with $ra\in Y_h$, $r$ agreeing with $h$ on $P$ and sending the rest of a pin of $a$ to fresh points, and $j$ agreeing with $k$ on any given finite $N\supseteq hP$; and $Y_c=cA=cY_h$ since $cr=c$; so $h\cdot Y$ is weakly rigid. At the singleton a weakly rigid relation is the exact image of its extension; $c\cdot F$ is rigid, so $F_{i_nc}=i_ncE$, and a member $x=ga$ of $Y_{i_nc}$ ($g$ agreeing with $i_nc$ on $P$) lies in $i_ncE$, so $x=i_ncx=i_ncga=i_nca$, $cg$ being $c$. So $c\cdot Y=T(cA)$, which is rigid.
(b) Lifting at $\mathbb N$. A weakly rigid $H$ with extension $E$ has $H_j=jE$ for every surjective self-map $j$, as in rigid-power-surjections, part (b). Given a rigid $F$, an arrow $k$, a finite $N$ containing a pin of $F$, and a rigid $X\le k\cdot F$ with extension $D$ pinned down by $T$: if $k$ is a self-map, extend $k|_N$ to a surjection $j$ with finitely many non-singleton fibres, all finite, take $P$ containing $N$, those fibres and preimages of $T$, and $A:=\{a\in E:ja\in D\}$; for $u$ fixing $P$, $ju=vj$ with $v$ fixing $T$, so $uA\subseteq A$, and $j\cdot B_P(A)=X$ by (a) and the exact-image fact. If $k=c$, take $A:=\{a\in E:ca\in D\}$, stable since $cu=c$, and $c\cdot B_P(A)=X$.
(c) At the singleton every rigid $F$ is $T(E)$ and every $T(A)$, $A\subseteq E$, is admitted; a rigid $X\le i_n\cdot F$ with extension $D$ is $i_n\cdot T(cD)$, since $ci_n=1$. So the power property of every rigid relation, at either object, is weakly rigid, and Rigid Power holds at every world. Weakly Rigid Power still fails, with Tame Rigidity.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: Write $\mathrm{fix}_N$ for the arrows agreeing with the identity on the finite set $N$, the least true proposition pinned by $N$, and $\delta_N$ for the arrows injective on $N$. At $W_0$ the arrows are all maps $\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and the one map $c$ to $W_1=\{0\}$. $\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}^{00}_N$ is the set of maps injective on $N$, together with $c$ when $|N|\le1$; the same set is $\hat\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}^{00}_N$, since an injective-on-$N$ map is undone by a bijection and $c$ by the map picking the point of $N$, which returns to every truth at $W_1$ ($W_1$ is a point, so its domains are full and $c\circ v=1_{W_1}$). So $\Box_{\ne}$ and $\hat{\hat\Box}$ coincide at the evaluation point. BF at type $t$ holds for $\hat{\hat\Box}$ there: for $Y$ pinned by $X_Y$ and $N\supseteq X_Y$ with two elements, every $k\in\hat\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}^{00}_N$ is a map injective on $N$, which agrees on $X_Y$ with a bijection $b$, and $Y_k=Y_b$ contains every transport along $b$, i.e. everything; so by Proposition D8 of The Bounds of Possibility $\Box_5$ implies two-hat necessity at $W_0$, and at $W_1$ too, which is full. The truth $\mathrm{fix}^{00}_{\{0\}}$ is not 5-necessary, since $\Box_5\le\hat{\hat\Box}$ fails on it (a bijection moving $0$ is in every $\hat\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}^{00}_N$). At $W_1$, the maps $W_1\to W_0$ are retracted by $c$ but not invertible, so, $W_1$ being full, $\{1_{W_1}\}$ is two-hat necessary and not ND-necessary there: the identity $\Box_{\ne}=\hat{\hat\Box}$ fails. (The verdicts this argument also establishes but does not record are derived by the engine.)

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, auditing the withdrawn arguments for the failure of Analytic Necessitism
arguments.text: At type $\tau:=tt$. For each object $V$ reachable from the evaluation point fix an injection $A\mapsto E^A_V$ from the sets of natural numbers into the sets of propositions at $V$, possible as these are infinitely many, and let $Y_A$ be the intension whose value at an arrow into $V$ is $E^A_V$: it depends only on the codomain, so it is in the domain, and its transport along an arrow into $V$ is the $Y_A$ of $V$, distinct for distinct $A$. Carry the real numbers onto the $Y_A$ and take as relations the codomain-only intensions whose value at $V$ is the corresponding set of tuples of the $Y_A$ of $V$. Along every arrow the structure is carried to the like structure at the target, an isomorphic copy, which is a real number structure there: bounded sets of its elements have least upper bounds among them and every inductive subproperty contains its natural numbers. Such a structure is rigid, its instances are necessarily distinct, and it is necessarily a real number structure; and the codomain-only intension of type $((\tau)^kt)t$ whose value at each object is the set of codomain-only $k$-ary relations among the carrier there is a represented power of arity $k$, since at every world each $k$-ary relation agrees on the carrier with one of them. So the consequents of Analytic Necessitism and of its second-order form hold, and both principles hold. (The argument of the withdrawn analytic-necessitism-unretracted-arrow would refute this structure; its step from inextensibility is the gap.)

The original text and attribution are preserved; its selected-carrier construction is not rejected by this withdrawal.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with $ka=kb$ for two distinct points $a$ and $b$ of the set the arrows act on, and let $q$ be the set of arrows $j$ out of $w$ with $ja\ne jb$. It contains the identity, is pinned down by $\{a,b\}$, is symmetric (an arrow separates $a$ from $b$ iff its composite with a permutation of the points does), and contains no arrow $j\circ k$. Let $\tau$ be $tt$, or $tttt$ in the case noted below. No entity $x$ of type $\tau$ at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: let $y$ agree with $x$ except at the arrows in $q$, where the top entity of the argument type of $\tau$ is added to its value or removed from it. Then $y$ is pinned down by a finite set along with $x$, is symmetric if $x$ is, so is in the domain; it differs from $x$ and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. If $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ of type $\tau$, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$ (Background, Analysis), an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above would give $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ by persistence, $Xy$ by inextensibility, and $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$ by the necessary distinctness of the instances: so $X$ has no instance. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds, however, at type $\tau$. The propositions are infinitely many and, in the recorded instances, include a copy of the natural numbers, so by extensional fullness the entities of type $tt$, which include one with any set of propositions as extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the reals, whose order, sum, product and natural numbers are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain; the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty, so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{tt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$. (Should the propositions be infinite without including a copy of the natural numbers, the same holds at type $tttt$, the sets of sets of propositions being Dedekind-infinite in ZF.) So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

withdrawn.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, after a trawl subagent's report
withdrawn.reason: The step from $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ to $Xy$ (or $y\in X_h$) by inextensibility does not follow: inextensibility bounds a rigid carrier from above, by the transports of its actual instances, and puts nothing new into its actual extension. The conclusion is false in many of the models the argument was applied to: entities fixed by every arrow, or transported injectively, can carry a rigid real number structure that is necessarily one (see analytic-necessitism-codomain-fixed and analytic-necessitism-full-continuum).

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: The numbers at a type $\sigma$ are the instances of $\mathbb N_\sigma$, the least property containing $\mathbf 0_\sigma$ and closed under $\operatorname{Suc}_\sigma$ (Background); the numerals $\mathbf 0_\sigma$, $\operatorname{Suc}_\sigma\mathbf 0_\sigma,\ldots$ are closed terms, so each denotes at every object, and transport along an arrow carries its denotation at the source to its denotation at the target. At any object $v$ reachable from the evaluation point, extensional fullness gives a property whose extension at $v$ is exactly the numerals there; it contains $\mathbf 0_\sigma$ and is closed under successor, so the numbers at $v$ are exactly the numerals, every numeral being an instance of every inductive property. Persistence of $\mathbb N_\sigma$ and, given $\Box I^*_\sigma$, the necessary distinctness of the numbers are theorems of C (the proof of necessary-rigid-comprehension-implies-arithmetic-necessitism). Inextensibility, $\Box\forall X\,.\,(\forall n\,.\,\mathbb N_\sigma n\to\Box Xn)\to\mathbb N_\sigma\le X$: at a reachable $v$ and for an arrow $j$ from $v$ to $u$, the numbers at $u$ are the numerals there, which are the transports along $j$ of the numbers at $v$, so any $X$ that necessarily holds of the numbers at $v$ holds at $u$ of the numbers there. So $\mathbb N_\sigma$ is rigid, and Arithmetic Necessitism holds at every type. No choice is used.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: Let $v$ be any object reachable from the evaluation point and $\mathfrak R$ a real number structure at $v$ (Background, Analysis). Its completeness is tested against the subproperties of its carrier present at $v$, and by extensional fullness every subset of the carrier's extension there is the extension at the identity of one of them; so the carrier, with the extensions of $\le$, $+$ and $\times$, is a complete ordered field in the sense of the metatheory and, by Huntington's theorem, a theorem of ZF, is isomorphic to the real numbers. For the same reason the extension of $N$, the least subproperty containing $0$ and closed under adding $1$, is its set of natural numbers, that set being the extension of a subproperty. A second-order analytical sentence $A(\mathfrak R)$ quantifies over the relations among entities of the structure's type at $v$, applied to the structure's elements, and their extensions at the identity are all the relations on the carrier, again by extensional fullness. So $A(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $v$ exactly when $A$ holds in the real numbers under full second-order semantics, which depends neither on $v$ nor on $\mathfrak R$. Hence $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to A(\mathfrak R)$ holds when $A$ is true of the reals and $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to\neg A(\mathfrak R)$ when it is false: every instance of the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, and with it the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis, as recorded. No choice is used.

settings.construction:
A singleton-base specialization of Bacon’s full Boolean-valued construction in §B.2. Work in ZFC, let $A$ be a nontrivial complete atomless Boolean algebra, and set $B=\mathbf{2}\times A$, $D_e=\{*\}$, $D_t=B$, and $D_{\sigma\to\tau}=D_\tau^{D_\sigma}$ for every admitted function type. Use ordinary application and abstraction, Boolean connectives, quantifiers given by meets and joins, and crisp equality. Evaluation point: the atom $a=(1,0_A)$; a proposition is true iff its first coordinate is $1$.

$A$ is fixed by cases on the continuum hypothesis in the ambient set theory. If CH holds, $A$ is $\operatorname{RO}(\operatorname{Add}(\omega,\omega_2))$, the algebra adding $\aleph_2$ Cohen reals, as in Bacon's §B.2; if CH fails, $A$ is $\operatorname{RO}(\operatorname{Col}(\omega_1,2^{\aleph_0})\times\operatorname{Add}(\omega,1))$, which collapses the continuum to $\aleph_1$ and adds one Cohen real. Either way forcing with $A$ adds a Cohen real, $A$ has at least continuum many elements, and CH takes the opposite value in $V^A$ to its value in $V$.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

models.notes:
Full verification is in the write-up.

The source uses an infinite individual domain, ZFC + CH, and the algebra adding $\aleph_2$ Cohen reals, to make CH contingent. The record keeps that algebra when CH holds and uses its dual when CH fails, so it requires only ZFC; the singleton individual domain does no harm, the real number structures living at type $t$. For an extensionally full model in ZFC, Relational Choice follows by representing a set-theoretic functional subrelation, and Plenitude then gives Functional Choice. The qualitative-contrast model of Classicism does not meet this fullness condition: its finite-support and symmetry restrictions exclude the needed selector. In the present model, $R(p,q):=(p\land q=\top)\lor(\neg p\land q=\bot)$ has Seriality and Functionality of value $1_B$, but $\exists f\,\forall p\,R(p,f(p))$ has value exactly $a$. The write-up includes the atomless-component calculation and the comparison with the older model. The finite check tests the Boolean calculation, not the infinite construction.

Work in ZFC, let $A$ be a nontrivial complete atomless Boolean algebra, and set $B=\mathbf{2}\times A$, $D_e=\{*\}$, $D_t=B$, and $D_{\sigma\to\tau}=D_\tau^{D_\sigma}$ for every admitted function type. Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

Universe, fixed for this record: the construction is carried out inside Gödel's constructible universe $L$, which ZFC proves to be a model of ZFC + $V=L$. Read in the ambient universe, the result is still a Boolean-valued model of the same kind, with the same values: every element of the algebra lies in $L$, and every clause of the semantics takes the meet or join of a family that lies in $L$ (by induction on formulas), whose meet or join in $L$ is its meet or join outright, since every candidate bound is itself an element of the algebra, hence in $L$. Its domains are full in the sense of $L$, and every argument for the member, being a proof in ZFC about the model's values, holds of it. In particular $L\models\mathrm{CH}$, so an algebra chosen by cases on CH is the one for CH.

models.definition:
Bacon's full Boolean-valued construction of §B.2 with $A:=\operatorname{RO}(\operatorname{Add}(\omega,1))$, the algebra adding one Cohen real. Set $B=\mathbf 2\times A$, $D_e=\omega$, $D_t=B$, and $D_{\sigma\to\tau}=D_\tau^{D_\sigma}$ for every admitted function type. Use ordinary application and abstraction, Boolean connectives, quantifiers given by meets and joins, and crisp equality. Evaluation point: the atom $a=(1,0_A)$; a proposition is true iff its first coordinate is $1$.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

Universe, fixed for this record: the construction is carried out inside Gödel's constructible universe $L$, which ZFC proves to be a model of ZFC + $V=L$. Read in the ambient universe, the result is still a Boolean-valued model of the same kind, with the same values: every element of the algebra lies in $L$, and every clause of the semantics takes the meet or join of a family that lies in $L$ (by induction on formulas), whose meet or join in $L$ is its meet or join outright, since every candidate bound is itself an element of the algebra, hence in $L$. Its domains are full in the sense of $L$, and every argument for the member, being a proof in ZFC about the model's values, holds of it. In particular $L\models\mathrm{CH}$, so an algebra chosen by cases on CH is the one for CH.

met.sigma-top: This is the interpretation the definition fixes.

models.name: Full action model: double retraction with free sites, glued constants

certificate.produced_by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction, 14 October 2026, combining Cian Dorr's two-retraction category with Bacon's gluing construction (Logical Combinatorialism, Appendix A.3)
certificate.recorded_by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 14 October 2026

sources: Cian Dorr and Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), conversation of 14 October 2026 (transcript in the private notes); writeups/full-double-retraction-glued-constants.md.
Cian Dorr, the two-object retract with two retractions (model full-two-object-retract-double-retraction, 6 October 2026).
Andrew Bacon, Logical Combinatorialism, Appendix A.3 (the gluing of Σ-models at the sites of a self-similar frame); A Philosophical Introduction to Higher-Order Logics, §18.6, Definition 18.15.

references.note: The gluing construction, here carried out at the root of a two-object category.

settings.construction: Let $\mathcal C$ be the category of the two-object retract with two retractions: objects $W_0,W_1$, generated by $h:W_0\to W_1$ and $j_1,j_2:W_1\to W_0$ with $j_i\circ h=1_{W_0}$, so that $e_i:=h\circ j_i$ are idempotents with $e_i\circ h=h$. Let $\mathcal D:=\mathcal C*_{W_0}F$ be obtained by freely adjoining at $W_0$ the free monoid $F$ on countably many generators $f_1,f_2,\ldots$ (the pushout over the object $W_0$; its arrows are the alternating reduced words of non-identity arrows of $\mathcal C$ and non-identity elements of $F$). Take the full action model over $\mathcal D$ with a single individual, evaluated at $1_{W_0}$, and glue the constants of Σ at the sites $f_k$: enumerate the pure formulas $P_k(\bar x)$, with $\bar x$ matching a tuple of distinct constants, whose existential closure is true at the root, choose a witness tuple for each, and let each constant denote the intension at $W_0$ whose value at an arrow $u\circ f_k$ is the extension at $u$ of the $k$-th witness and whose value at the remaining arrows is empty. Each part has one job (write-up, §4): the sites give Witnessed Possibility; the two retractions of $h$ make Strong Actuality fail at $W_0$ while it holds at $W_1$, so a pure sentence is contingent; and every arrow into $W_1$ factors through $h$, whose transports never yield the true atom of $W_1$, so Possibly Witnessed Possibility fails.

meets.infinitely-many-propositions-everywhere: The model is full, and infinitely many arrows leave each object: the words $f_k$ at $W_0$, and $f_k\circ j_1$ at $W_1$.
meets.incomparable-free-arrows: The free generators $f_1$ and $f_2$ at $W_0$: in the pushout a reduced word is fixed under post- composition only by the identity when it ends in a free generator, and neither generator is a left multiple of the other.
meets.countably-many-arrows: The arrows of $\mathcal D$ are the reduced alternating words in the finitely many non-identity arrows of $\mathcal C$ and the countably many generators of $F$: countably many.
meets.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at both objects.
meets.full-action-model: A full action model with two objects.
meets.extensionally-full: The domains are full.
meets.identity-singletons: The singletons $\{1_{W_0}\}$ and $\{1_{W_1}\}$ are in the domains, the model being full.
meets.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present at both objects, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain; a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, and with persistence a weakly rigid relation equals it, so the rigid relations are exactly these, as in the group of full action models.
meets.one-individual: The construction fixes a single individual at each object.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: Infinitely many arrows leave $W_0$ (the sites $f_k$ alone), and the propositions are all sets of them.
meets.returning-arrow: $h$, which $j_1$ retracts.
meets.noninvertible-retracted-arrow: $h$ is retracted by $j_1$ and $j_2$ but has no inverse, since $h\circ j_i=e_i\ne1_{W_1}$.
meets.separated-retractions: $h$ has the retractions $j_1\ne j_2$, and these remain its only retractions in $\mathcal D$ (write-up, Corollary 3); the proposition $\{j_1\}$ at $W_1$ separates them.
meets.unretracted-arrow: $f_1$: by the cancellation lemma of the write-up, $x\circ f_1=1_{W_0}$ would need a left inverse of $f_1$ in the free monoid.
meets.trivial-isomorphisms-everywhere: By the cancellation lemma an isomorphism has only invertible syllables, and neither $\mathcal C$ nor $F$ has a non-identity invertible element ($h\circ j_i=e_i\ne1$).
meets.irreversible-arrow: The world $f_1$: no arrow $x$ has $x\circ f_1=1_{W_0}$, so no world after $f_1$ makes the actual-world proposition true.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: The write-up, §§1–2, verifies the gluing at the root: the sites $f_k$ are right-cancellable with pairwise disjoint left ideals in $\mathcal D$, so the glued intensions are well defined and, the model being full, in the domain at $W_0$; at the site $f_k$ the constants denote the $k$-th witness tuple. If $\exists\bar x\,P$ is true at the root, $P$ is enumerated and $P[\bar c]$ holds at its site.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: Strong Actuality fails at $W_0$, where $h$ has the two retractions $j_1,j_2$, and holds at $W_1$, where no non-identity arrow has a retraction (write-up, Corollary 3), so the true atom $\{1_{W_1}\}$ is a strong atom there; a closed pure sentence being true at an arrow iff true at its target, the pure sentence SA is true exactly at the worlds with target $W_1$. Let $c$ be a constant of type $t$ and $P(x)$ say that SA holds and $x$ is a true atom. $\Diamond\exists x\,P$ holds at the root, at the world $h$. But every arrow $W_0\to W_1$ is $h\circ v$, so at any world with target $W_1$ the constant denotes a transport along $h$ of a proposition at $W_0$, which contains $1_{W_1}$ iff it contains $e_1$ (as $e_1\circ h=h$) and so is not $\{1_{W_1}\}$; at worlds with target $W_0$, SA fails. So $P[c]$ is possible nowhere (write-up, §3.3).

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: Every object reaches every object ($h$ forward, $j_1$ back). A closed pure sentence true at the root is therefore possible at every world: at a world with target $W_0$ it holds there, and at one with target $W_1$ it holds after $j_1$ (write-up, §3.4).

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, auditing the withdrawn arguments for the failure of Analytic Necessitism
arguments.text: At type $\tau:=tt$. For each object $V$ reachable from the evaluation point fix an injection $A\mapsto E^A_V$ from the sets of natural numbers into the sets of propositions at $V$, possible as these are infinitely many, and let $Y_A$ be the intension whose value at an arrow into $V$ is $E^A_V$: it depends only on the codomain, so it is in the domain, and its transport along an arrow into $V$ is the $Y_A$ of $V$, distinct for distinct $A$. Carry the real numbers onto the $Y_A$ and take as relations the codomain-only intensions whose value at $V$ is the corresponding set of tuples of the $Y_A$ of $V$. Along every arrow the structure is carried to the like structure at the target, an isomorphic copy, which is a real number structure there: bounded sets of its elements have least upper bounds among them and every inductive subproperty contains its natural numbers. Such a structure is rigid, its instances are necessarily distinct, and it is necessarily a real number structure; and the codomain-only intension of type $((\tau)^kt)t$ whose value at each object is the set of codomain-only $k$-ary relations among the carrier there is a represented power of arity $k$, since at every world each $k$-ary relation agrees on the carrier with one of them. So the consequents of Analytic Necessitism and of its second-order form hold, and both principles hold. (The argument of the withdrawn analytic-necessitism-unretracted-arrow would refute this structure; its step from inextensibility is the gap.)

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: Let $h\colon w\to v$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with a retraction $j$ but no inverse. Then $e:=h\circ j$ is an idempotent arrow out of $v$ other than its identity, since $e=1_v$ would make $h$ invertible, and $e$ has no retraction: $i\circ e=1_v$ would give $e=i\circ e\circ e=1_v$. Suppose $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ at a relational type, necessarily a real number structure (Background, Analysis). Its boxed clauses hold at $h$ and along the arrows after $h$, which are arrows out of $w$; so at $v$ the instances $X_h$ of its carrier form a complete ordered field, and for $x\in X_h$ and any $y$ at $v$ with $e\cdot y=e\cdot x$, persistence gives $e\cdot y\in X_{e\circ h}$, inextensibility $y\in X_h$, and necessary distinctness $y=x$. But, the model being full at $v$ and $e$ having no retraction, no entity of a relational type at $v$ is determined by its transport along $e$, as in the argument analytic-necessitism-unretracted-arrow: its value at the identity of $v$ is free. So $X_h$ is empty, a contradiction. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds at the relational type $ttt$, as in that argument, the propositions at $w$ being infinitely many. So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

arguments.text: Write $w$ for the evaluation object and $k$ for an arrow out of it with no retraction. No entity $x$ of a relational type at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: the identity of $w$ is not of the form $j\circ k$, such a $j$ being a retraction, and the model being full, the intension $y$ agreeing with $x$ at every arrow but the identity, where it takes another value, is in the domain, while $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. Suppose then that $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ at a relational type, necessarily a real number structure (Background, Analysis), with carrier $X$. For an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above, persistence gives $k\cdot x\in X_k$, so $k\cdot y\in X_k$; inextensibility then gives $Xy$; and the necessary distinctness of the instances gives $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$, a contradiction. The propositions at $w$ are the sets of the infinitely many arrows out of it, the sets of sets of propositions are Dedekind-infinite (a theorem of ZF for any infinite set), and the entities of type $ttt$ at $w$, which include one with any given extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the real numbers; the model being full, the order, sum and product of the reals are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain, every subset of that carrier is the extension of a subproperty, so the structure is complete, and its least inductive subproperty is its natural numbers. So $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{ttt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$ while the consequent of Analytic Necessitism fails there: Analytic Necessitism fails. Taking it as the witness, $\Box_{\ne}p$ holds at an identity iff $p$ contains every arrow out of that object with a retraction (these are the arrows at which $\Diamond\{1\}$ holds), and $\hat{\hat\Box}p$ iff $p$ contains every invertible arrow out of it (an arrow lies in $\hat\Diamond\{1\}$ iff some retraction of it has a retraction, i.e. iff it is invertible). Full models satisfy necessary Actuality, so $\Box_5=\hat{\hat\Box}$ by Proposition D21 of The Bounds of Possibility. With only identities invertible, $\Box_5$ is the identity operator at every reachable object, so every truth is 5-necessary everywhere.

arguments.text: The propositions at the evaluation object are the sets of its countably many arrows, so they have the cardinality of the continuum, and a complete Boolean algebra that is finite or has strictly fewer elements than the propositions is finite, an infinite complete Boolean algebra having an infinite antichain and so at least continuum many elements (with choice). A finite Boolean algebra with $n$ atoms is isomorphic to the algebra of subsets of any $n$ arrows, the entailment algebra below the proposition consisting of those arrows, which is not top, the arrows being infinitely many; the one-element algebra is the entailment algebra below $\bot$. The isomorphism is a relation present in the full domains. The internal notions agree with the external ones: a property of entities carrying the order of a complete Boolean algebra, every subproperty having a least upper bound, is one in the metatheory, since every subset is the extension of a subproperty, and Dedekind finiteness and the existence of injective relations are read in a full model as in the metatheory. So Forcing Possibilism holds.

arguments.text: Given $X$ of type $\tau$ at an object $W$, let $Y$ be the relation whose extension at an arrow $i$ out of $W$ is $X$'s extension at $W$ transported along $i$, which is in the domain since the model is full. It is coextensive with $X$. It is persistent, since its extension at $i\circ j$ is its extension at $i$ transported along $j$. And it is inextensible: if $\Box X'$ holds at $i$ of everything $Y$ holds of there, then at $i\circ j$ everything $Y$ holds of is the transport along $j$ of something $Y$ holds of at $i$, of which $X'$ then holds. Every object being full, the same holds at every arrow, so Rigid Comprehension is necessary. The source notes that full models satisfy it (p. 61); stated once for the topic, in place of the full models' own arguments.

arguments.text: Write $X_0(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$. The extension at an arrow $h$ of the power property $\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le F$ is the set of rigid $X$ with $X\le h\cdot F$, the bound variable ranging over the domain untransported and the parameter transported. By the condition the rigid relations are the $X_0(E)$, and $X_0(T)\le X_0(S)$ iff $T\subseteq S$; so for rigid $F=X_0(S)$ the power property has extension $\{X_0(T'):T'\subseteq k\cdot S\}$ at $k$, while transporting its extension at the identity along $k$ gives $\{X_0(k\cdot T):T\subseteq S\}$. These coincide, since every $T'\subseteq k\cdot S$ is $k\cdot T$ for $T:=\{s\in S:k\cdot s\in T'\}$. So the power property is itself $X_0$ of its extension, hence rigid, and the same at every reachable object gives the boxed form.

A true proposition $p$ contains the identity, so under $h$ it becomes a proposition containing $j$ and $j^{\prime}$, since $j\circ h=j^{\prime}\circ h=1$. That proposition lies neither below $q$ nor below $\neg q$, so $p$ is not a strong atom. No true proposition is.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: In a full action model the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$ is in the domain at every object. Taking it as the witness, $\Box_{\ne}p$ holds at an identity iff $p$ contains every arrow out of that object with a retraction (these are the arrows at which $\Diamond\{1\}$ holds), and $\hat{\hat\Box}p$ iff $p$ contains every invertible arrow out of it (an arrow lies in $\hat\Diamond\{1\}$ iff some retraction of it has a retraction, i.e. iff it is invertible). Full models satisfy necessary Actuality, so $\Box_5=\hat{\hat\Box}$ by Proposition D21 of The Bounds of Possibility. Let $u$ have a retraction but no inverse. The true proposition $\{1\}$ excludes $u$, so it is not ND-necessary, while every invertible arrow is the identity or excluded from no such test: $\{1\}$ is two-hat necessary iff no non-identity arrow is invertible, and in any case the proposition $\{1\}\cup\{\text{invertible arrows}\}$ is in the domain, true, two-hat necessary and not ND-necessary.

models.notes: Built on 14 October 2026 to separate Witnessed Possibility from Separated Structure (equivalently Possibly Witnessed Possibility) and from Strong Actuality, which no model with Witnessed Possibility refuted: the coalesced sums of Appendix E have it without No Pure Contingency but keep both, and the glued one-object models have all of Logical Necessity. Bacon derives both Independence and Separated Structure from Logical Necessity; the recorded result from Witnessed Possibility to Independence and this model show that only the latter needs No Pure Contingency. The construction is a recipe: freely adjoining the free monoid of sites at the root of any category and gluing the constants gives Witnessed Possibility at the root while preserving the category's retractions, epimorphisms and reachability (write-up, §4). Being full, the model cannot separate Witnessed Possibility from the principles every full model satisfies. The failures of No Pure Contingency, Converse Witnessed Possibility and Modal Freedom are derived by the engine from Witnessed Possibility without Possibly Witnessed Possibility; the write-up, §3.2, gives them directly from the contingency of the pure sentence Strong Actuality.
models.definition:
Let $\mathcal C$ be the category of the two-object retract with two retractions: objects $W_0,W_1$, generated by $h:W_0\to W_1$ and $j_1,j_2:W_1\to W_0$ with $j_i\circ h=1_{W_0}$, so that $e_i:=h\circ j_i$ are idempotents with $e_i\circ h=h$. Let $\mathcal D:=\mathcal C*_{W_0}F$ be obtained by freely adjoining at $W_0$ the free monoid $F$ on countably many generators $f_1,f_2,\ldots$ (the pushout over the object $W_0$; its arrows are the alternating reduced words of non-identity arrows of $\mathcal C$ and non-identity elements of $F$). Take the full action model over $\mathcal D$ with a single individual, evaluated at $1_{W_0}$, and glue the constants of Σ at the sites $f_k$: enumerate the pure formulas $P_k(\bar x)$, with $\bar x$ matching a tuple of distinct constants, whose existential closure is true at the root, choose a witness tuple for each, and let each constant denote the intension at $W_0$ whose value at an arrow $u\circ f_k$ is the extension at $u$ of the $k$-th witness and whose value at the remaining arrows is empty. Each part has one job (write-up, §4): the sites give Witnessed Possibility; the two retractions of $h$ make Strong Actuality fail at $W_0$ while it holds at $W_1$, so a pure sentence is contingent; and every arrow into $W_1$ factors through $h$, whose transports never yield the true atom of $W_1$, so Possibly Witnessed Possibility fails.

The constants of Σ are glued as in the construction above.

settings.construction: Let M be the free monoid of finite sequences of natural numbers under concatenation; its induced Kripke frame is the infinitely branching tree with the initial-segment relation and the empty sequence as root. Take the standard model over this frame (propositions all sets of accessible worlds, function types all homomorphisms) whose individuals at a world are the functions from the infinite branches through that world to the natural numbers, with restriction as counterpart; equivalently, the full action model over M with this surjective M-set at type e. This higher-order frame is isomorphic to the coalesced sum of countably many copies of itself, so coalesced sums of Σ-models over it are again Σ-models over it. Enumerate the Σ-sentences satisfiable in some Σ-model over the frame, choose a model of each, and glue them by the book’s Definition 18.15. Evaluation point: the root.

The gap in the source was its Theorem A.8, stated without proof, and the deferred type-e case; the write-up closes both by choosing a self-similar individual domain and applying the book’s coalesced sums. The signature is assumed countable; for a larger signature use a tree with as many branches. Distinct constants of one type denote distinct entities at the root, since every domain, including the individuals, has more than one element; they are also possibly identical. Everything else follows from the listed principles by the map’s results. Bacon’s interpretation of his predicates Pure and Fun in this model, and the principles stated with them, are not recorded, following Zachary Goodsell’s decision to keep the map to the logical vocabulary and the constants of Σ.

models.definition:
Let M be the free monoid of finite sequences of natural numbers under concatenation; its induced Kripke frame is the infinitely branching tree with the initial-segment relation and the empty sequence as root. Take the standard model over this frame (propositions all sets of accessible worlds, function types all homomorphisms) whose individuals at a world are the functions from the infinite branches through that world to the natural numbers, with restriction as counterpart; equivalently, the full action model over M with this surjective M-set at type e. This higher-order frame is isomorphic to the coalesced sum of countably many copies of itself, so coalesced sums of Σ-models over it are again Σ-models over it. Enumerate the Σ-sentences satisfiable in some Σ-model over the frame, choose a model of each, and glue them by the book’s Definition 18.15. Evaluation point: the root.

The constants of Σ are glued as in the construction above.

met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.countably-many-arrows: The arrows are the finite sequences of natural numbers.
met.unretracted-arrow: A non-identity element of the free monoid has no left inverse, so no arrow retracts it.
met.infinitely-many-propositions: The arrows are infinitely many and the model is full, so every set of them is a proposition.
met.incomparable-free-arrows: The generators $f_1$ and $f_2$: in a free monoid only $1$ fixes an element, and no generator is a left multiple of another.
met.one-object-action-model: It has one object.
met.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition, true at the root alone, is in the domain, the model being full; under a non-identity arrow $i$ no arrow $k$ has $k\circ i$ the identity, since no arrow leads back to the root.
met.irreversible-arrow: Any non-identity arrow, since no arrow leads back to the root.

settings.construction: Let $M:=F_\infty * E * B * \mathbb Z_2$ be the free product of monoids, where $F_\infty$ is the free monoid on countably many generators $f_1,f_2,\ldots$, $E=\{1,e\}$ with $e^2=e$, $B=\langle b,c\mid cb=1\rangle$ is the bicyclic monoid, and $\mathbb Z_2=\{1,s\}$ with $s^2=1$. Take the full one-object action model over $M$ (Classicism, §3.5) with a single individual, evaluated at the identity. The constants of Σ are glued at the sites $f_k$: enumerate the pure formulas $P_k(\bar x)$, with $\bar x$ matching a tuple of distinct constants, such that $\exists\bar x\,P_k$ is true at the identity, choose a witness tuple for each, and let each constant denote the intension whose value at an arrow $u\circ f_k$ is $u$ applied to the $k$-th witness and whose value at the remaining arrows is empty. Each factor has one job (write-up, §4): the free generators are the gluing sites that give Logical Necessity; the idempotent $e$ is a non-epic arrow, so BF fails; $b$ is retracted by $c$ but not invertible, so ND-necessity and two-hat necessity come apart; $s$ is a non-identity unit, so some truth is not 5-necessary.

meets.incomparable-free-arrows: The free generators $f_1$ and $f_2$: in the free product only $1$ fixes a free generator, and neither is a left multiple of the other.
meets.countably-many-arrows: The arrows are the reduced alternating words in the finitely many non-identity arrows of the retract category and the countably many generators of the free monoid: countably many.
meets.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present.
meets.full-action-model: A full action model with one object.
meets.extensionally-full: The domains are full.
meets.one-individual: The construction fixes a single individual.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: $M$ is infinite and the propositions are all its subsets.
meets.nonepic-arrow: $1\circ e=e\circ e$ with $1\ne e$; also $1\circ b=(b\circ c)\circ b$.
meets.unretracted-arrow: $e$: no reduced word $x$ has $x\circ e=1$, the last syllable of $x\circ e$ being $e$ or a product with it.
meets.returning-arrow: $b$, which $c$ retracts: $c\circ b=1$.
meets.irreversible-arrow: $e$: no arrow after it returns to the identity, so no world after $e$ makes $\{1\}$ true.
meets.identity-singletons: $\{1\}$ is in the domain, the model being full.
meets.unique-retractions-everywhere: By Lemma 3 of the write-up, $xu=1$ forces the syllables of $x$ to be, in reverse order, left inverses in their own factors of the syllables of $u$, and left inverses are unique in each factor ($c^k$ for $b^k$, $s$ for $s$, none for $e$, the generators or any $b^ic^j$ with $j\ge1$); so every arrow has at most one retraction.
meets.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present at the one object, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain. A relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, that being the smallest intension whose transports contain the extension, and with persistence a weakly rigid relation equals it; so the rigid relations, the necessarily weakly rigid ones, are exactly these, as in the group of full action models.

arguments.text: The write-up, §2, verifies the gluing: the sites $f_k$ are right-cancellable with pairwise disjoint left ideals $Mf_k$, so the glued intensions are well defined and, the model being full, in the domain; at the site $f_k$ the constants denote the $k$-th witness tuple, and one-object models make pure sentences world-independent, which gives both directions of the schema.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, auditing the withdrawn arguments for the failure of Analytic Necessitism
arguments.text: At type $\tau:=tt$. With one object, an intension whose value is the same at every arrow is in the domain by the condition, and it is fixed by transport along every arrow: $(h\cdot Y)_j=Y_{jh}=Y_j$. The propositions are infinitely many, so the constant intensions $Y_E$, for $E$ a set of propositions, are at least continuum many and pairwise distinct. Carry the real numbers onto continuum many of them, and take as carrier, order, sum, product, $0$, $1$ and natural numbers the constant intensions whose values are the corresponding sets of tuples of the $Y_E$. All parameters are fixed, so a formula about them has the same truth value at every world, and at the evaluation point they form a real number structure: any bounded set of carrier elements has a least upper bound among them, and every inductive subproperty contains the copy of the natural numbers. Such a structure is rigid, its instances are necessarily distinct, and it is necessarily a real number structure; and the codomain-only intension of type $((\tau)^kt)t$ whose value at each object is the set of codomain-only $k$-ary relations among the carrier there is a represented power of arity $k$, since at every world each $k$-ary relation agrees on the carrier with one of them. So the consequents of Analytic Necessitism and of its second-order form hold, and both principles hold. (The argument of the withdrawn analytic-necessitism-unretracted-arrow would refute this structure; its step from inextensibility is the gap.)

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: Let $h\colon w\to v$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with a retraction $j$ but no inverse. Then $e:=h\circ j$ is an idempotent arrow out of $v$ other than its identity, since $e=1_v$ would make $h$ invertible, and $e$ has no retraction: $i\circ e=1_v$ would give $e=i\circ e\circ e=1_v$. Suppose $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ at a relational type, necessarily a real number structure (Background, Analysis). Its boxed clauses hold at $h$ and along the arrows after $h$, which are arrows out of $w$; so at $v$ the instances $X_h$ of its carrier form a complete ordered field, and for $x\in X_h$ and any $y$ at $v$ with $e\cdot y=e\cdot x$, persistence gives $e\cdot y\in X_{e\circ h}$, inextensibility $y\in X_h$, and necessary distinctness $y=x$. But, the model being full at $v$ and $e$ having no retraction, no entity of a relational type at $v$ is determined by its transport along $e$, as in the argument analytic-necessitism-unretracted-arrow: its value at the identity of $v$ is free. So $X_h$ is empty, a contradiction. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds at the relational type $ttt$, as in that argument, the propositions at $w$ being infinitely many. So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

withdrawn.reason: The step from $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ to $Xy$ (or $y\in X_h$) by inextensibility does not follow: inextensibility bounds a rigid carrier from above, by the transports of its actual instances, and puts nothing new into its actual extension. The conclusion is false in many of the models the argument was applied to: entities fixed by every arrow, or transported injectively, can carry a rigid real number structure that is necessarily one (see analytic-necessitism-codomain-fixed and analytic-necessitism-full-continuum).

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: Write $w$ for the evaluation object and $k$ for an arrow out of it with no retraction. No entity $x$ of a relational type at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: the identity of $w$ is not of the form $j\circ k$, such a $j$ being a retraction, and the model being full, the intension $y$ agreeing with $x$ at every arrow but the identity, where it takes another value, is in the domain, while $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. Suppose then that $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ at a relational type, necessarily a real number structure (Background, Analysis), with carrier $X$. For an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above, persistence gives $k\cdot x\in X_k$, so $k\cdot y\in X_k$; inextensibility then gives $Xy$; and the necessary distinctness of the instances gives $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$, a contradiction. So $X$ has no instance and is no complete ordered field. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds nevertheless, at some relational type. The propositions at $w$ are the sets of the infinitely many arrows out of it, the sets of sets of propositions are Dedekind-infinite (a theorem of ZF for any infinite set), and the entities of type $ttt$ at $w$, which include one with any given extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the real numbers; the model being full, the order, sum and product of the reals are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain, every subset of that carrier is the extension of a subproperty, so the structure is complete, and its least inductive subproperty is its natural numbers. So $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{ttt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$ while the consequent of Analytic Necessitism fails there: Analytic Necessitism fails. (When the arrows out of $w$ include a copy of the natural numbers, as in the recorded instances, the same argument runs at type $t$.) No choice is used.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: The propositions at the evaluation object are the sets of its countably many arrows, so they have the cardinality of the continuum, and a complete Boolean algebra that is finite or has strictly fewer elements than the propositions is finite, an infinite complete Boolean algebra having an infinite antichain and so at least continuum many elements (with choice). A finite Boolean algebra with $n$ atoms is isomorphic to the algebra of subsets of any $n$ arrows, the entailment algebra below the proposition consisting of those arrows, which is not top, the arrows being infinitely many; the one-element algebra is the entailment algebra below $\bot$. The isomorphism is a relation present in the full domains. The internal notions agree with the external ones: a property of entities carrying the order of a complete Boolean algebra, every subproperty having a least upper bound, is one in the metatheory, since every subset is the extension of a subproperty, and Dedekind finiteness and the existence of injective relations are read in a full model as in the metatheory. So Forcing Possibilism holds.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 3 October 2026 (full action models); extended by Claude Fable 5.1, prompted by Cian Dorr (Anthropic), 4 October 2026, at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: Write $X_0(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$. The extension at an arrow $h$ of the power property $\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le F$ is the set of rigid $X$ with $X\le h\cdot F$, the bound variable ranging over the domain untransported and the parameter transported. By the condition the rigid relations are the $X_0(E)$, and $X_0(T)\le X_0(S)$ iff $T\subseteq S$; so for rigid $F=X_0(S)$ the power property has extension $\{X_0(T'):T'\subseteq k\cdot S\}$ at $k$, while transporting its extension at the identity along $k$ gives $\{X_0(k\cdot T):T\subseteq S\}$. These coincide, since every $T'\subseteq k\cdot S$ is $k\cdot T$ for $T:=\{s\in S:k\cdot s\in T'\}$. So the power property is itself $X_0$ of its extension, hence rigid, and the same at every reachable object gives the boxed form.

conditions.reason: Every intension is present at the one object, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain. A relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, that being the smallest intension whose transports contain the extension, and with persistence a weakly rigid relation equals it; so the rigid relations, the necessarily weakly rigid ones, are exactly these, as in the group of full action models.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: Let $V$ be the evaluation object or the target of an arrow out of it, and $w:=\{1_V\}$, in the domain at $V$. It is true at $1_V$. Under an arrow $f$ out of $V$ it becomes $\{k : k\circ f=1_V\}$, the set of retractions of $f$, which has at most one member and so lies below $q$ or below $\neg q$ for every proposition $q$ at $f$'s target. So Strong Actuality holds at $1_V$. A closed sentence holds at an arrow iff it holds at the identity of the arrow's target, so Strong Actuality holds at every world after the evaluation point, and □Strong Actuality holds there.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), on Cian Dorr's question whether the failure of Boolean Completeness at type $t$ refutes its countable form here
arguments.text: The natural numbers are the finite cardinalities at type $e$ (Background, after Goodsell), and with a single individual there are three: $\mathbf{0}_e$, true of the empty property; $\operatorname{Suc}_e\mathbf{0}_e$, true of the universal one; and the empty cardinality, which is $\operatorname{Suc}_e$ of the second and of itself. By extensional fullness the property of being one of these three is in the domain, so it bounds natural numberhood. A countable property therefore has at most three members in its extension, and their join is its least upper bound.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: In a full action model the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$ is in the domain at every object. Taking it as the witness, $\Box_{\ne}p$ holds at an identity iff $p$ contains every arrow out of that object with a retraction (these are the arrows at which $\Diamond\{1\}$ holds), and $\hat{\hat\Box}p$ iff $p$ contains every invertible arrow out of it (an arrow lies in $\hat\Diamond\{1\}$ iff some retraction of it has a retraction, i.e. iff it is invertible). Full models satisfy necessary Actuality, so $\Box_5=\hat{\hat\Box}$ by Proposition D21 of The Bounds of Possibility. Let $u$ have a retraction but no inverse. The true proposition $\{1\}$ excludes $u$, so it is not ND-necessary, while every invertible arrow is the identity or excluded from no such test: $\{1\}$ is two-hat necessary iff no non-identity arrow is invertible, and in any case the proposition $\{1\}\cup\{\text{invertible arrows}\}$ is in the domain, true, two-hat necessary and not ND-necessary.

The propositions $\bot$ and $\{1\}$ are in the domain, the model being full, and $k$ transports both to $\bot$: no arrow $m$ after $k$ has $m\circ k=1$. So $k$'s action at type $t$ is not injective, and ND fails there (Proposition 3.24(i)).

models.notes: Built on 14 October 2026 to separate Logical Necessity from what the glued free-monoid models also satisfy. The free product is chosen so that each factor contributes one failure while the gluing sites stay free; models over $F_\infty * E$, $F_\infty * B$ or $F_\infty * \mathbb Z_2$ alone would disaggregate the failures (write-up, §4). Being full, the model satisfies Rigid Comprehension, Actuality, Atomicity, Boolean Completeness and the choice principles, so it cannot separate Logical Necessity from those; that needs a non-full gluing-closed construction. The failure of BF is derived by the engine from the non-epic arrow $e$ (write-up, §3). Strong Actuality, Rigid Power and Weakly Rigid Power, with their boxed forms, were settled on the evening of 14 October 2026 by the general arguments for full models with unique retractions (write-up, §3).

models.definition:
Let $M:=F_\infty * E * B * \mathbb Z_2$ be the free product of monoids, where $F_\infty$ is the free monoid on countably many generators $f_1,f_2,\ldots$, $E=\{1,e\}$ with $e^2=e$, $B=\langle b,c\mid cb=1\rangle$ is the bicyclic monoid, and $\mathbb Z_2=\{1,s\}$ with $s^2=1$. Take the full one-object action model over $M$ (Classicism, §3.5) with a single individual, evaluated at the identity. The constants of Σ are glued at the sites $f_k$: enumerate the pure formulas $P_k(\bar x)$, with $\bar x$ matching a tuple of distinct constants, such that $\exists\bar x\,P_k$ is true at the identity, choose a witness tuple for each, and let each constant denote the intension whose value at an arrow $u\circ f_k$ is $u$ applied to the $k$-th witness and whose value at the remaining arrows is empty. Each factor has one job (write-up, §4): the free generators are the gluing sites that give Logical Necessity; the idempotent $e$ is a non-epic arrow, so BF fails; $b$ is retracted by $c$ but not invertible, so ND-necessity and two-hat necessity come apart; $s$ is a non-identity unit, so some truth is not 5-necessary.

The constants of Σ are glued as in the construction above.
