models.notes: Explicit specialization of the source's standard Henkin construction to an infinite individual domain, recorded to separate the type-$e$ infinity principles from the type-$t$ ones: it satisfies the Axiom of Infinity at type $e$, hence Possible Infinity at type $e$, while violating the Axiom of Infinity at type $t$. It also shows that the sentence used in pure-possibility-implies-axiom-of-infinity-t, that there could be any positive number of individuals, does not follow from the Axiom of Infinity at type $e$: here there is not possibly exactly one individual. It also witnesses the consistency of C with Goodsell's $I$, assumed in n. 14 of Arithmetic is Necessary: with infinitely many individuals the numerals are pairwise distinct, so $\operatorname{Suc}_e$ is injective on finite cardinalities and $I^*$, hence $I$, is true. With Boolean Completeness listed, the model also shows Countable Boolean Completeness consistent with C. Everything that implies these fails with them.

meets.finitely-many-propositions-everywhere: There is one object, with four propositions, the sets of the two arrows.

models.definition:
The full model on {1,k} with k²=k, evaluated at its sole object.

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the construction is carried out in ZF together with a countable family $(P_n)_{n\in\omega}$ of pairwise disjoint two-element sets that has no choice function (Russell's socks), which is consistent with ZF (Fraenkel's second permutation model, transferred to ZF by the Jech–Sochor theorem). Every infinite set the construction leaves unspecified (the individuals, the worlds, a carrier) is their union. The verdicts of this record are relative-consistency claims of the same standing as those of a record with choice.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.fixed-infinite-individuals: This is the choice of individuals.
met.homogeneous-individuals: A permutation of $D$ commutes with every arrow's action, the identity, so it is an automorphism at type $e$ and extends, by conjugation, to the full domains of the other types, carrying each individual to its image.
met.comparable-free-arrows-everywhere: At the one object the only arrow fixed by nothing but $1$ is $1$ itself, since $k\cdot k=k$.
met.uniquely-factored-free-arrows-everywhere: $1=m\cdot h$ only for $m=h=1$, since $x\cdot k=k$ for both arrows $x$.
met.finitely-many-arrows-everywhere: There is one object, with two arrows out of it.
met.unretracted-arrow: $m\cdot k=k$ for both arrows $m$, so $k$ has no retraction.
met.finitely-many-propositions-everywhere: There is one object, with four propositions, the sets of the two arrows.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
met.one-object-action-model: It has one object.
met.finitely-many-propositions: The propositions at the evaluation object are the subsets of the two arrows out of it, four in all.
met.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition $\{1\}$ is in the domain, the model being full; under $k$, $x\circ k=k$ for both arrows, so no world outside it sees it.
met.irreversible-arrow: The arrow $k$: $x\circ k=k$ for both arrows $x$, so no composite with it is the identity.

models.name: Full action model: infinite S5

certificate.produced_by: Cian Dorr, 7 October 2026
certificate.recorded_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 7 October 2026

sources: Cian Dorr, suggestion of 7 October 2026, as a basic reference model.
Andrew Bacon and Cian Dorr, Classicism, draft of 16 May 2023, §3.5, pp. 58–61 (full action models).

references.note: Full action models; on this category the construction is the standard full S5 model.

settings.construction: The category whose objects are the members of an infinite set $W$, with exactly one arrow from each object to each object, evaluated at any object. The arrows out of an object correspond to the members of $W$, so this is the full S5 model with world set $W$ and a constant domain of individuals.

numbered-returning-arrows.text: $h_n$ is the arrow to world $n$, and $r_n$ the arrow back, once $W$ contains the natural numbers: by choice, or because $W$ is $\mathbb N$ in the variant without countable choice. With socks $W$ is their union, and no such arrows need be given.

meets.invertible-arrows: The unique arrow from $u$ to $v$ is inverted by the unique arrow from $v$ to $u$.
meets.epic-arrows: Every arrow is invertible; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
meets.retractions: Each arrow out of the evaluation object is retracted by the arrow back.
meets.unique-retractions-everywhere: Between two objects there is only one arrow, so an arrow has exactly one retraction.
meets.returning-arrow: The arrow to any other object, retracted by the arrow back.
meets.coherent-retractions: $r_g$ is the unique arrow back; any two arrows with the same ends are equal, so $r_{x\circ g}\circ x=r_g$.
meets.nonidentity-arrow: The arrow to any other object.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions are all the sets of arrows out of the evaluation object, one for each subset of $W$.
meets.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.

models.notes: A basic reference model, recorded at Cian Dorr's request: the full S5 model with infinitely many worlds. Except for Forcing Possibilism, no recorded verdict depends on which infinite set $W$ is. In the variant with infinitely many individuals the group fixes them as the natural numbers; any infinite set gives the same verdicts under choice. Its verdicts are those of the full permutation group model, whose arrows are likewise all invertible, again except for Forcing Possibilism, which the map leaves unknown here. Under choice, Forcing Possibilism holds iff $2^{|W|}=2^{\aleph_0}$ (GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi, 23 October 2026): if so, every small or Dedekind-finite complete Boolean algebra is finite, an infinite one having at least continuum many elements, and is isomorphic to the subsets of a finite set of worlds; if not, the regular-open algebra of Cantor space is small and atomless, while the algebra below any proposition is atomic. So it holds for $W=\mathbb N$ and fails for $|W|=2^{\aleph_0}$. With $W$ the union of Russell's socks it fails without choice (forcing-possibilism-socks).
models.definition:
The category whose objects are the members of an infinite set $W$, with exactly one arrow from each object to each object, evaluated at any object. The arrows out of an object correspond to the members of $W$, so this is the full S5 model with world set $W$ and a constant domain of individuals.

Individuals, fixed for this record: there is a single individual at every object, and every arrow sends it to the single individual at its target.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the axiom of choice is used freely, as in ordinary mathematics in ZFC, or in Lean's classical type theory for the verdicts certified there.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.one-individual: There is a single individual at every object.
met.finitely-many-individuals-everywhere: There is a single individual at every object.
met.numbered-returning-arrows: $h_n$ is the arrow to world $n$, and $r_n$ the arrow back, once $W$ contains the natural numbers: by choice, or because $W$ is $\mathbb N$ in the variant without countable choice. With socks $W$ is their union, and no such arrows need be given.
met.invertible-arrows: The unique arrow from $u$ to $v$ is inverted by the unique arrow from $v$ to $u$.
met.epic-arrows: Every arrow is invertible; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
met.retractions: Each arrow out of the evaluation object is retracted by the arrow back.
met.unique-retractions-everywhere: Between two objects there is only one arrow, so an arrow has exactly one retraction.
met.returning-arrow: The arrow to any other object, retracted by the arrow back.
met.coherent-retractions: $r_g$ is the unique arrow back; any two arrows with the same ends are equal, so $r_{x\circ g}\circ x=r_g$.
met.nonidentity-arrow: The arrow to any other object.
met.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions are all the sets of arrows out of the evaluation object, one for each subset of $W$.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.

In the variant with infinitely many individuals the group fixes them as the natural numbers; any infinite set gives the same verdicts under choice. Its verdicts are those of the full permutation group model, whose arrows are likewise all invertible, again except for Forcing Possibilism, which the map leaves unknown here. Under choice, Forcing Possibilism holds iff $2^{|W|}=2^{\aleph_0}$ (GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi, 23 October 2026): if so, every small or Dedekind-finite complete Boolean algebra is finite, an infinite one having at least continuum many elements, and is isomorphic to the subsets of a finite set of worlds; if not, the regular-open algebra of Cantor space is small and atomless, while the algebra below any proposition is atomic. So it holds for $W=\mathbb N$ and fails for $|W|=2^{\aleph_0}$. With $W$ the union of Russell's socks it fails without choice (forcing-possibilism-socks).
models.definition:
The category whose objects are the members of an infinite set $W$, with exactly one arrow from each object to each object, evaluated at any object. The arrows out of an object correspond to the members of $W$, so this is the full S5 model with world set $W$ and a constant domain of individuals.

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: one designated relational constant $c$ of type $\tau=\bar\sigma t$ denotes $\lambda\bar x\, .\,a$, where $a$ is the unique true atom of the model, the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$; every other constant of Σ, of which there is at least one, is relational and denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the axiom of choice is used freely, as in ordinary mathematics in ZFC, or in Lean's classical type theory for the verdicts certified there.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.fixed-infinite-individuals: This is the choice of individuals.
met.homogeneous-individuals: A permutation of $D$ commutes with every arrow's action, the identity, so it is an automorphism at type $e$ and extends, by conjugation, to the full domains of the other types, carrying each individual to its image.
met.numbered-returning-arrows: $h_n$ is the arrow to world $n$, and $r_n$ the arrow back, once $W$ contains the natural numbers: by choice, or because $W$ is $\mathbb N$ in the variant without countable choice. With socks $W$ is their union, and no such arrows need be given.
met.invertible-arrows: The unique arrow from $u$ to $v$ is inverted by the unique arrow from $v$ to $u$.
met.epic-arrows: Every arrow is invertible; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
met.retractions: Each arrow out of the evaluation object is retracted by the arrow back.
met.unique-retractions-everywhere: Between two objects there is only one arrow, so an arrow has exactly one retraction.
met.returning-arrow: The arrow to any other object, retracted by the arrow back.
met.coherent-retractions: $r_g$ is the unique arrow back; any two arrows with the same ends are equal, so $r_{x\circ g}\circ x=r_g$.
met.nonidentity-arrow: The arrow to any other object.
met.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions are all the sets of arrows out of the evaluation object, one for each subset of $W$.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.

Evaluate at the sole object. The propositions at the evaluation object are the subsets of the two arrows out of it, four in all, and every intension of a full model is present.

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: one designated relational constant $c$ of type $\tau=\bar\sigma t$ denotes $\lambda\bar x\, .\,a$, where $a$ is the unique true atom of the model, the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$; every other constant of Σ, of which there is at least one, is relational and denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the construction is carried out in ZF together with a countable family $(P_n)_{n\in\omega}$ of pairwise disjoint two-element sets that has no choice function (Russell's socks), which is consistent with ZF (Fraenkel's second permutation model, transferred to ZF by the Jech–Sochor theorem). Every infinite set the construction leaves unspecified (the individuals, the worlds, a carrier) is their union. The verdicts of this record are relative-consistency claims of the same standing as those of a record with choice.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.fixed-infinite-individuals: This is the choice of individuals.
met.homogeneous-individuals: A permutation of $D$ commutes with every arrow's action, the identity, so it is an automorphism at type $e$ and extends, by conjugation, to the full domains of the other types, carrying each individual to its image.
met.returning-arrow: $k$, its own inverse.
met.coherent-retractions: $r_g:=g^{-1}$: then $r_{x\circ g}\circ x=g^{-1}\circ x^{-1}\circ x=g^{-1}$.
met.epic-arrows: Every arrow is invertible; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
met.finitely-many-propositions-everywhere: There is one object, with four propositions, the sets of the two arrows.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
met.one-object-action-model: It has one object.
met.finitely-many-propositions: The propositions at the evaluation object are the subsets of the two arrows out of it, four in all.

settings.construction: The full model over the monoid $M:=\langle a,b,c\mid ac=bc\rangle$, the free monoid on three generators modulo the congruence generated by $ac=bc$, evaluated at its sole object. Its elements are the words in $a,b,c$ with no factor $ac$, since the rewriting $ac\to bc$ has no overlaps; the relation preserves length.

meets.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: The subsets of an infinite monoid.
meets.unretracted-arrow: The relation preserves length, so $m\cdot k=1$ forces $m=k=1$: no non-identity element has a retraction.
meets.irreversible-arrow: $c$, as no composite with it has length $0$.
meets.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition $\{1\}$ is in the domain, the model being full; no product with a non-identity element is $1$, the relation preserving length.
meets.unique-retractions-everywhere: No non-identity element has a retraction, at the one object.
meets.retracted-arrows-invertible-everywhere: Only $1$ is retracted.
meets.trivial-left-stabilisers-everywhere: The relation preserves length, so $m\cdot k=k$ forces $m$ to have length $0$.
meets.incomparable-free-arrows: $a$ and $b$: each is fixed only by $1$, and neither is a left multiple of the other, both having length $1$ and being distinct.
meets.free-nonepic-composite: $ac=bc$ with $a\ne b$, and $ac$ is fixed only by $1$.

models.definition:
The full model over the monoid $M:=\langle a,b,c\mid ac=bc\rangle$, the free monoid on three generators modulo the congruence generated by $ac=bc$, evaluated at its sole object. Its elements are the words in $a,b,c$ with no factor $ac$, since the rewriting $ac\to bc$ has no overlaps; the relation preserves length.

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: one designated relational constant $c$ of type $\tau=\bar\sigma t$ denotes $\lambda\bar x\, .\,a$, where $a$ is the unique true atom of the model, the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$; every other constant of Σ, of which there is at least one, is relational and denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the axiom of choice is used freely, as in ordinary mathematics in ZFC, or in Lean's classical type theory for the verdicts certified there.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).

met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. met.irreversible-arrow: $c$, as no composite with it has length $0$.

met.unique-retractions-everywhere: No non-identity element has a retraction, at the one object.

met.incomparable-free-arrows: $a$ and $b$: each is fixed only by $1$, and neither is a left multiple of the other, both having length $1$ and being distinct.

settings.construction: The full one-object action model whose arrows are all the permutations of a countably infinite set $X$, composed as functions. Propositions are all sets of arrows with the division action $i\cdot p=\{j : j\circ i\in p\}$, and every function type carries the full function-space M-set, which here is the set of all functions since every arrow acts bijectively. Evaluate at the identity arrow.

meets.continuum-many-arrows: With $X$ enumerated, a set $C$ of natural numbers is sent to the permutation that swaps $x_{2n}$ and $x_{2n+1}$ for each $n\in C$ and fixes the rest; distinct sets give distinct permutations.
meets.numbered-returning-arrows: With $X$ enumerated as $x_0,x_1,\ldots$, $h_0$ the identity and $h_n$ the transposition of $x_0$ and $x_n$, its own retraction.
meets.returning-arrow: Any permutation other than the identity, which its inverse retracts.
meets.nonidentity-arrow: Any permutation other than the identity.
meets.epic-arrows: Every arrow is invertible; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions are all the sets of arrows, and there are infinitely many permutations.
meets.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.

models.definition: Work in external ZFC. F is the full standard extensional relational hierarchy over omega with terminal modality, in its countable many-sorted first-order presentation including all finite parameterized-lambda templates. H is an elementary substructure obtained by the subset-code closure described below. Form its full classical present R: R_e=omega, and at each relational type tau=alpha_1...alpha_k t set R_tau=P(product_i R_alpha_i) x H_tau. The only proper future is terminal H, with transport q(S,h)=h and identity transport on individuals. All current rows occur. Application, logical operations and quantifiers have their current full-row values and the transported H-component. Equality is literal at each point. Evaluate at R. Put c=2^aleph_0 and lambda=2^c. Seed all of F_(et)t, all individuals, and every point and graph of an ordinary real-field copy at every infinite relational host. Through a c^+ elementary chain, at each successor stage add the exact F predicate of every external subset of every existing sort of size at most c, then take an elementary hull. The union H has size lambda and admits exact codes for all subsets of each H sort of size at most c. It retains H_(et)t=F_(et)t.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: The elementary closure provides external H unions for all families of size at most c, hence for countable families. The full present has countable canonical successor orbits at every counting source. Pairing current-row unions with H unions proves native CBC for every counting/output type; H itself has internal full BC. Thus the CBC schema holds necessarily. See sections 1–3.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: Parameter comprehension supplies every singleton in each leaf relation algebra. The root product algebra has atoms (current singleton,leaf bottom) and (empty current row,leaf singleton). Each decides every relation at R and every future H test; the first kind may become bottom, which the native definition permits. Every nonzero entity has one below it. Leaf singletons are strong atoms. Thus Strong Atomicity holds at both points and all relational types. See section 4.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: Every subset T of a finite power of a seeded real field has size at most c, so an exact code for T is admitted using a coded family of tuple haecceities and existential union. The whole family of supported relations is admitted by parameter comprehension, not by a size bound on that family. Lift the field by exact images and each T to its exact-image graph; the resulting whole family transports exactly onto the supported H relations and is rigid. At each point every relation restriction is represented. The same field works for every specified finite arity. Vacuous carriers are checked separately. See sections 5–6 and 8.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: Put delta=(et)t. The leaf retains all F_delta, of size lambda, whereas H_(delta t) has at most lambda members. Choose a missing extension A subset H_delta. Its singleton family has no leaf LUB, since complements of omitted singletons force any LUB to have exactly extension A. The corresponding admitted root family has no LUB either. The failure occurs at ((et)t)t. See section 3.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: At et every candidate rigid real carrier has c current members and injective transport. Exact continuum-subset closure makes its first canonical power a full carrier of size lambda=2^c. The whole second canonical power transports injectively into an H sort of size at most lambda. Root fullness supplies all 2^lambda subsets of the first power, so some lacks a representative. Thus every candidate field fails the height-1 FTAN clause, with possible Real active. This proves SOAN does not imply FTAN. FTN failure follows from AN and the FTN+AN-to-FTAN bridge; no redundant negative flag is added.

models.notes: A scaled version of the countably closed construction. It supplies whole finite-arity powers of each seeded real field while leaving a missing Boolean join one type higher. No CH is assumed. Necessary Actuality, necessary IC and necessary Transversal also follow from the proved geometry or recorded implications; no propositional BC failure is asserted. The finite-type supplement separates SOAN from FTAN at host et, height 1; e-counting has an active Box I*_e, with FTN heights 0 and 1 true and height 2 false. These bounded heights are not a positive full FTN schema.

Seed all individuals and every point and graph of an ordinary real-field copy at every infinite relational carrier. Through an omega_1 elementary chain, at each successor stage add the exact F predicate of every external countable subset of each existing sort, then take an elementary hull. arguments.text: Every canonical current number carrier is its external successor orbit, hence countable, because the full current row for that orbit is an admitted inductive predicate. A native countable family therefore has at most countably many current members. Its projected H family has an exact code and an H union; pair this union with the union of its current rows. Coordinatewise necessary order proves that this pair is a LUB against every root test. Terminal H has internal full BC by parameter comprehension. Thus CBC holds at both points for every counting type and every relational output type. See sections 1–3.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: At R the proposition (1,0) entails every current truth. A current relation with row S has the inextensible coextension (S,bottom_H); its future has no instances. arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi

sources: Andrew Bacon and Cian Dorr, Classicism, draft of 16 May 2023, §3.5, p. 59, third paragraph; p. 61 and n. 84.

references.locator: §3.5, p. 59, third paragraph; p. 61 and n. 84

settings.construction: Use the monoid of surjections of an infinite set, at its sole object.

meets.incomparable-free-arrows: Two surjections of $\mathbb N$ with incomparable kernels, say one identifying only $0,1$ and one identifying only $2,3$: a surjection is fixed only by the identity, and $k^{\prime}=m\circ k$ requires the kernel of $k$ to lie inside that of $k^{\prime}$.
meets.arbitrary-infinite-set: The monoid is that of the surjections of any infinite set.

continuum-many-arrows.text: Once the infinite set contains the natural numbers (by choice, or because it is $\mathbb N$ in the variant without countable choice), a set $C$ of natural numbers is sent to the surjection that swaps $2n$ and $2n+1$ for each $n\in C$ and fixes everything else, a bijection; distinct sets give distinct surjections. With socks the set need contain no copy of the natural numbers.

meets.numbered-returning-arrows: $h_0$ the identity and $h_n$ a transposition, a surjection that is its own retraction: of $0$ and $n$ when the infinite set is $\mathbb N$ (with choice, or in the variant without countable choice), and of the two members of $P_n$ when it is the union of the socks.
meets.returning-arrow: A bijection other than the identity, which its inverse retracts.
meets.unretracted-arrow: Halving is not injective, so no surjection $m$ has $m\circ k=1$ for it.
meets.epic-arrows: A surjection $k$ is an epimorphism among the surjections, $m\circ k=m^{\prime}\circ k$ giving $m=m^{\prime}$; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions are all the sets of arrows, and there are infinitely many surjections.
meets.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
meets.irreversible-arrow: A surjection that is not injective: no composite with it is the identity.

settings.construction: Use the monoid of surjections of an infinite set, at its sole object.

meets.incomparable-free-arrows: Two surjections of $\mathbb N$ with incomparable kernels, say one identifying only $0,1$ and one identifying only $2,3$: a surjection is fixed only by the identity, and $k^{\prime}=m\circ k$ requires the kernel of $k$ to lie inside that of $k^{\prime}$.
meets.arbitrary-infinite-set: The monoid is that of the surjections of any infinite set.

continuum-many-arrows.text: Once the infinite set contains the natural numbers (by choice, or because it is $\mathbb N$ in the variant without countable choice), a set $C$ of natural numbers is sent to the surjection that swaps $2n$ and $2n+1$ for each $n\in C$ and fixes everything else, a bijection; distinct sets give distinct surjections. With socks the set need contain no copy of the natural numbers.

meets.numbered-returning-arrows: $h_0$ the identity and $h_n$ a transposition, a surjection that is its own retraction: of $0$ and $n$ when the infinite set is $\mathbb N$ (with choice, or in the variant without countable choice), and of the two members of $P_n$ when it is the union of the socks.
meets.returning-arrow: A bijection other than the identity, which its inverse retracts.
meets.unretracted-arrow: Halving is not injective, so no surjection $m$ has $m\circ k=1$ for it.
meets.epic-arrows: A surjection $k$ is an epimorphism among the surjections, $m\circ k=m^{\prime}\circ k$ giving $m=m^{\prime}$; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions are all the sets of arrows, and there are infinitely many surjections.
meets.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
meets.irreversible-arrow: A surjection that is not injective: no composite with it is the identity.

models.notes:
The cited construction is a model of the map’s relational-type framework. The description identifies its evaluation point; construction and verification are given at the PDF locations in References.
The source takes infinitely many individuals with a surjective action, such as the surjections' action on the set by evaluation. That action gives, on the map's principles, what the variant with infinitely many fixed individuals gives: it is surjective and homogeneous, and the failure of ND at type $e$ that its non-injectivity brings adds nothing, ND failing already at type $t$.

models.definition:
Use the monoid of surjections of an infinite set, at its sole object.

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: one designated relational constant $c$ of type $\tau=\bar\sigma t$ denotes $\lambda\bar x\, .\,a$, where $a$ is the unique true atom of the model, the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$; every other constant of Σ, of which there is at least one, is relational and denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the axiom of choice is used freely, as in ordinary mathematics in ZFC, or in Lean's classical type theory for the verdicts certified there.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.fixed-infinite-individuals: This is the choice of individuals.
met.arbitrary-infinite-set: The monoid is that of the surjections of any infinite set.
met.homogeneous-individuals: A permutation of $D$ commutes with every arrow's action, the identity, so it is an automorphism at type $e$ and extends, by conjugation, to the full domains of the other types, carrying each individual to its image.
met.incomparable-free-arrows: Two surjections of $\mathbb N$ with incomparable kernels, say one identifying only $0,1$ and one identifying only $2,3$: a surjection is fixed only by the identity, and $k^{\prime}=m\circ k$ requires the kernel of $k$ to lie inside that of $k^{\prime}$.
met.continuum-many-arrows: Once the infinite set contains the natural numbers (by choice, or because it is $\mathbb N$ in the variant without countable choice), a set $C$ of natural numbers is sent to the surjection that swaps $2n$ and $2n+1$ for each $n\in C$ and fixes everything else, a bijection; distinct sets give distinct surjections. With socks the set need contain no copy of the natural numbers.
met.numbered-returning-arrows: $h_0$ the identity and $h_n$ a transposition, a surjection that is its own retraction: of $0$ and $n$ when the infinite set is $\mathbb N$ (with choice, or in the variant without countable choice), and of the two members of $P_n$ when it is the union of the socks.
met.returning-arrow: A bijection other than the identity, which its inverse retracts.
met.unretracted-arrow: Halving is not injective, so no surjection $m$ has $m\circ k=1$ for it.
met.epic-arrows: A surjection $k$ is an epimorphism among the surjections, $m\circ k=m^{\prime}\circ k$ giving $m=m^{\prime}$; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
met.infinitely-many-propositions: The propositions are all the sets of arrows, and there are infinitely many surjections.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
met.one-object-action-model: It has one object.
met.irreversible-arrow: A surjection that is not injective: no composite with it is the identity.

settings.construction: The category with objects $W_0$, $V$, $U$ generated by $h:W_0\to V$ and $g_1,g_2:V\to U$ subject to $g_1\circ h=g_2\circ h$; its arrows are the identities, $h$, $g_1$, $g_2$ and $d:=g_1\circ h$. Evaluated at $W_0$. Every endomorphism monoid is trivial and no arrow leads back towards $W_0$.

meets.irreversible-arrow: $h$: no arrow leads back to $W_0$.
meets.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition $\{1_{W_0}\}$ is in the domain, the model being full; no arrow leads back to $W_0$, so no other world sees it.
meets.unique-retractions-everywhere: No non-identity arrow has a retraction: the only arrows into $W_0$, $V$ and $U$ from elsewhere go forward along the fork.
meets.retracted-arrows-invertible-everywhere: Only identities are retracted.
meets.trivial-left-stabilisers-everywhere: Every endomorphism monoid is $\{1\}$, so $m\circ k=k$ forces $m=1$ everywhere.
meets.comparable-free-arrows: The arrows out of $W_0$ are $1$, $h=h\circ1$ and $d=g_1\circ h$: each is a left multiple of the one before.
meets.free-nonepic-composite: $d=g_1\circ h=g_2\circ h$ with $g_1\ne g_2$, and $d$ is fixed only by $1_U$.

sources: Original construction of 19 October 2026, to settle the recorded conjecture possible-infinity-t-implies-axiom-of-infinity-t; the full action model on the category described, which is a model of C by Classicism, §3.5 and Appendix D.

references.note: Full action models over a category are models of C.

settings.construction: Use two objects $W_0$ and $W_1$. The arrows are the identities, one arrow $h\colon W_0\to W_1$, and the powers $s^n$ ($n\ge0$) of one endomorphism $s$ of $W_1$, which compose as $s^m\circ s^n=s^{m+n}$ and $s^n\circ h=h$, $h$ being the only arrow from $W_0$ to $W_1$; there is no arrow from $W_1$ to $W_0$. Evaluate at $W_0$.

meets.comparable-free-arrows-everywhere: Out of $W_0$ only $1$ is fixed by nothing but the identity, $h$ being fixed by $s$; out of $W_1$ the arrows $s^n$ are comparable, $s^m=s^{m-n}\circ s^n$ for $n\le m$.
meets.uniquely-factored-free-arrows-everywhere: At $W_0$, $1=m\circ h$ is impossible and $1=m\circ1$ forces $m=1$; at $W_1$, $s^n=m\circ s^a$ forces $m=s^{n-a}$.
meets.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
meets.finitely-many-propositions: The propositions at $W_0$ are the subsets of the two arrows out of it, four in all.
meets.unretracted-arrow: There is no arrow from $W_1$ back to $W_0$.
meets.nonepic-arrow: The distinct arrows $s^0$ and $s$ out of $W_1$ agree after $h$, both composites being $h$.
meets.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition, the singleton of the identity of $W_0$, is in the domain, the model being full; the only other world out of $W_0$ is $h$, and every arrow after $h$ is $h$ again, so no world outside it sees a world in it.
meets.trivial-isomorphisms-everywhere: The only invertible arrows are the identities: $s^m\circ s^n=s^0$ only for $m=n=0$, and $h$ has no inverse.
meets.retracted-arrows-invertible-everywhere: No arrow other than an identity has a retraction, for the same reason.

models.notes:
The two-object chain with an infinite monoid of endomorphisms at the second object. It is recorded to refute the conjecture possible-infinity-t-implies-axiom-of-infinity-t: the evaluation object has four propositions and sees one with infinitely many. As the conjecture's notes anticipate, BF at type $t$ and No Pure Contingency both fail; the engine derives both from Possible Infinity (type $t$) and the failure of the Axiom of Infinity (type $t$), and they can be seen directly: transport along $h$ sends a proposition $p$ at $W_0$ to every arrow out of $W_1$ if $h\in p$ and to none otherwise, so the property of propositions whose extension at $h$ is $\{\emptyset,\{s^n:n\ge0\}\}$ and whose extension at the identity is everything necessarily holds of every proposition at $W_0$ and fails at $W_1$ of $\{s\}$; and the pure sentence that there are exactly four propositions is true at $W_0$ and false at $W_1$. With one individual the model is finite at $W_0$ in every type, and infinite at $W_1$ from type $t$ up.

Clarification (30 October 2026; GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi): the final sentence of the original notes overstates finiteness at W0. Only its proposition domain is four-element; already at type tt an arbitrary subset of D_t(W1) can be chosen as the h-row, giving infinitely many root entities. The new negative argument uses precisely the t instance and does not assert all-type finiteness.

As the conjecture's notes anticipate, BF at type $t$ and No Pure Contingency both fail; the engine derives both from Possible Infinity (type $t$) and the failure of the Axiom of Infinity (type $t$), and they can be seen directly: transport along $h$ sends a proposition $p$ at $W_0$ to every arrow out of $W_1$ if $h\in p$ and to none otherwise, so the property of propositions whose extension at $h$ is $\{\emptyset,\{s^n:n\ge0\}\}$ and whose extension at the identity is everything necessarily holds of every proposition at $W_0$ and fails at $W_1$ of $\{s\}$; and the pure sentence that there are exactly four propositions is true at $W_0$ and false at $W_1$. With one individual the model is finite at $W_0$ in every type, and infinite at $W_1$ from type $t$ up.

Clarification (30 October 2026; GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi): the final sentence of the original notes overstates finiteness at W0. Only its proposition domain is four-element; already at type tt an arbitrary subset of D_t(W1) can be chosen as the h-row, giving infinitely many root entities. The new negative argument uses precisely the t instance and does not assert all-type finiteness.
models.definition:
Use two objects $W_0$ and $W_1$. The arrows are the identities, one arrow $h\colon W_0\to W_1$, and the powers $s^n$ ($n\ge0$) of one endomorphism $s$ of $W_1$, which compose as $s^m\circ s^n=s^{m+n}$ and $s^n\circ h=h$, $h$ being the only arrow from $W_0$ to $W_1$; there is no arrow from $W_1$ to $W_0$. Evaluate at $W_0$.

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: one designated relational constant $c$ of type $\tau=\bar\sigma t$ denotes $\lambda\bar x\, .\,a$, where $a$ is the unique true atom of the model, the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$; every other constant of Σ, of which there is at least one, is relational and denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the construction is carried out in ZF together with a countable family $(P_n)_{n\in\omega}$ of pairwise disjoint two-element sets that has no choice function (Russell's socks), which is consistent with ZF (Fraenkel's second permutation model, transferred to ZF by the Jech–Sochor theorem). Every infinite set the construction leaves unspecified (the individuals, the worlds, a carrier) is their union. The verdicts of this record are relative-consistency claims of the same standing as those of a record with choice.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.fixed-infinite-individuals: This is the choice of individuals.
met.homogeneous-individuals: A permutation of $D$ commutes with every arrow's action, the identity, so it is an automorphism at type $e$ and extends, by conjugation, to the full domains of the other types, carrying each individual to its image.
met.comparable-free-arrows-everywhere: Out of $W_0$ only $1$ is fixed by nothing but the identity, $h$ being fixed by $s$; out of $W_1$ the arrows $s^n$ are comparable, $s^m=s^{m-n}\circ s^n$ for $n\le m$.
met.uniquely-factored-free-arrows-everywhere: At $W_0$, $1=m\circ h$ is impossible and $1=m\circ1$ forces $m=1$; at $W_1$, $s^n=m\circ s^a$ forces $m=s^{n-a}$.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
met.finitely-many-propositions: The propositions at $W_0$ are the subsets of the two arrows out of it, four in all.
met.unretracted-arrow: There is no arrow from $W_1$ back to $W_0$.
met.nonepic-arrow: The distinct arrows $s^0$ and $s$ out of $W_1$ agree after $h$, both composites being $h$.
met.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition, the singleton of the identity of $W_0$, is in the domain, the model being full; the only other world out of $W_0$ is $h$, and every arrow after $h$ is $h$ again, so no world outside it sees a world in it.
met.trivial-isomorphisms-everywhere: The only invertible arrows are the identities: $s^m\circ s^n=s^0$ only for $m=n=0$, and $h$ has no inverse.
met.retracted-arrows-invertible-everywhere: No arrow other than an identity has a retraction, for the same reason.

arguments.by: Cian Dorr, recorded by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
arguments.text: At type $e$. The haecceity $H$ of $a$, with extension $\{{a\}}$ at the identity of $W_0$ and $\{{b\}}$ at $f$, is necessary of everything at $W_0$, whose only individual is $a$; but after $f$ it fails of $c$. So $\forall x\, .\,\Box Hx$ holds at $W_0$ and $\Box\forall x\, .\,Hx$ fails.

arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Zachary Goodsell
arguments.text: Every type is finite at every object $v$ reachable from the evaluation point, by induction on types: the individuals at $v$ are finitely many by hypothesis, the propositions at $v$ are sets of the finitely many arrows out of it, and an entity of a relational type $\bar\sigma t$ at $v$ is an intension assigning to each of those arrows a set of tuples of entities of types $\bar\sigma$ at its target, which is reachable too, so that finitely many values are available at each arrow. An ordered field has infinitely many elements, its $0$, $1$, $1+1,\ldots$ being pairwise distinct, so no real number structure exists at any reachable object, at any type. The antecedents $\Diamond\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)$ of Analytic Necessitism and of Second-Order Analytic Necessitism are therefore false at every type, and both hold; and $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to A(\mathfrak R)$ holds for every sentence $A$, so the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, with the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis. No choice is used.

arguments.by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at Cian Dorr's direction
arguments.text: The relational half of full-epic-barcan. In an action model BF at a type $\sigma$ holds at a world iff transport along every arrow out of it is onto the entities of type $\sigma$ at its target: if some $z$ there is no transport, the property of being one is necessary of everything at the world and fails of $z$ after the arrow; and if transport is onto, a property necessary of everything holds of every transport. In a full model the transport of intensions along an epimorphism $k$ is onto at every relational type: an intension $Y$ at its target is the transport of $\{\langle\bar a,k\circ m\rangle:\langle\bar a,m\rangle\in Y\}$, since $k\circ m=k\circ m'$ only if $m=m'$. Nothing here concerns the individuals. So BF holds at every relational type at every object reachable from the evaluation point.

It is coextensive with $X$. It is persistent, since its extension at $i\circ j$ is its extension at $i$ transported along $j$. And it is inextensible: if $\Box X'$ holds at $i$ of everything $Y$ holds of there, then at $i\circ j$ everything $Y$ holds of is the transport along $j$ of something $Y$ holds of at $i$, of which $X'$ then holds. Every object being full, the same holds at every arrow, so Rigid Comprehension is necessary. arguments.text: Write $X_0(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$. The extension at an arrow $h$ of the power property $\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le F$ is the set of rigid $X$ with $X\le h\cdot F$, the bound variable ranging over the domain untransported and the parameter transported. By the condition the rigid relations are the $X_0(E)$, and $X_0(T)\le X_0(S)$ iff $T\subseteq S$; so for rigid $F=X_0(S)$ the power property has extension $\{X_0(T'):T'\subseteq k\cdot S\}$ at $k$, while transporting its extension at the identity along $k$ gives $\{X_0(k\cdot T):T\subseteq S\}$. These coincide, since every $T'\subseteq k\cdot S$ is $k\cdot T$ for $T:=\{s\in S:k\cdot s\in T'\}$. So the power property is itself $X_0$ of its extension, hence rigid, and the same at every reachable object gives the boxed form.

models.definition:
Use two objects with one nonidentity arrow from W0 to W1, evaluated at W0.

Individuals, fixed for this record: there is a single individual at every object, and every arrow sends it to the single individual at its target.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the axiom of choice is used freely, as in ordinary mathematics in ZFC, or in Lean's classical type theory for the verdicts certified there.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.

met.finitely-many-individuals-everywhere: There is a single individual at every object.

met.epic-arrows: Out of $W_1$ there is only the identity, so the arrow $W_0\to W_1$ is an epimorphism; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
met.finitely-many-propositions-everywhere: $W_0$ has four propositions and $W_1$ two.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
met.finitely-many-propositions: The propositions at the evaluation object are the subsets of the two arrows out of it, four in all.
met.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition, the singleton of the identity, is in the domain, the model being full; no arrow leads back from $W_1$ to $W_0$.

models.definition:
Use two objects with one nonidentity arrow from W0 to W1, evaluated at W0.

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the construction is carried out in ZF together with a countable family $(P_n)_{n\in\omega}$ of pairwise disjoint two-element sets that has no choice function (Russell's socks), which is consistent with ZF (Fraenkel's second permutation model, transferred to ZF by the Jech–Sochor theorem). Every infinite set the construction leaves unspecified (the individuals, the worlds, a carrier) is their union. The verdicts of this record are relative-consistency claims of the same standing as those of a record with choice.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.fixed-infinite-individuals: This is the choice of individuals.
met.homogeneous-individuals: A permutation of $D$ commutes with every arrow's action, the identity, so it is an automorphism at type $e$ and extends, by conjugation, to the full domains of the other types, carrying each individual to its image.
met.comparable-free-arrows-everywhere: Out of $W_0$ the arrows are $1$ and $h=h\circ1$; out of $W_1$ only $1$.
met.uniquely-factored-free-arrows-everywhere: $h=m\circ1$ only for $m=h$ and $h=m\circ h$ only for $m=1_{W_1}$; at $W_1$ only the identity.
met.finitely-many-arrows-everywhere: Two arrows out of $W_0$ and one out of $W_1$.
met.fewer-propositions-after: $W_0$ has four propositions and $W_1$, after which there is only itself, two.
met.unretracted-arrow: There is no arrow from $W_1$ back to $W_0$.
met.epic-arrows: Out of $W_1$ there is only the identity, so the arrow $W_0\to W_1$ is an epimorphism; and on the individuals every arrow is the identity.
met.finitely-many-propositions-everywhere: $W_0$ has four propositions and $W_1$ two.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
met.finitely-many-propositions: The propositions at the evaluation object are the subsets of the two arrows out of it, four in all.
met.actual-world-isolated: The actual-world proposition, the singleton of the identity, is in the domain, the model being full; no arrow leads back from $W_1$ to $W_0$.
met.trivial-isomorphisms-everywhere: The only arrows are the identities and $W_0\to W_1$, which has no inverse.
met.retracted-arrows-invertible-everywhere: No non-identity arrow has a retraction: nothing returns from $W_1$.

models.name: Full action model: two-object retract with two retractions

certificate.produced_by: Cian Dorr, 6 October 2026
certificate.recorded_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 6 October 2026

sources: Cian Dorr, suggestion of 6 October 2026, as a model of Actuality without Strong Actuality.
Andrew Bacon and Cian Dorr, Classicism, draft of 16 May 2023, §3.5, pp. 58–61; Appendix D, pp. 73–74 (full action models).

references.note: Full action models; the category is the two-object retract's with its arrow back doubled.

settings.construction: The category with objects $W_0,W_1$ generated by $h:W_0\to W_1$ and $j_1,j_2:W_1\to W_0$ subject to $j_1\circ h=j_2\circ h=1_{W_0}$, evaluated at $W_0$. Its arrows are $1_{W_0}$; $h$; $j_1,j_2$; and $1_{W_1}$ with the idempotents $e_i:=h\circ j_i$, which compose by $e_i\circ e_k=e_k$, $j_i\circ e_k=j_k$ and $e_i\circ h=h$ (the rewriting $j_i\circ h\mapsto1$ has no overlaps, so these normal forms are distinct).

meets.comparable-free-arrows: Out of $W_0$ only $1$ is fixed by nothing but the identity, $h$ being fixed by $e_1$.
meets.free-nonepic-composite: $j_1\circ h=j_2\circ h=1_{W_0}$ with $j_1\ne j_2$, and $1_{W_0}$ is fixed only by itself.
meets.finitely-many-arrows-everywhere: Two arrows out of $W_0$ and five out of $W_1$.
meets.returning-arrow: $h$, which $j_1$ retracts.
meets.retractions: The arrows out of $W_0$ are its identity and $h$, which $j_1$ retracts.
meets.finitely-many-propositions: $W_0$ has four propositions, the sets of its two arrows out.
meets.finitely-many-propositions-everywhere: $W_0$ has four propositions and $W_1$ thirty-two, the sets of its five arrows out.
meets.separated-retractions: $h$ has the retractions $j_1\ne j_2$, and $\{j_1\}$, in the domain at $W_1$ since the model is full, separates them.
meets.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
meets.noninvertible-retracted-arrow: $h$ is retracted by $j_1$ and $j_2$ but has no inverse, since $h\circ j_i=e_i\ne 1_{W_1}$.
meets.trivial-isomorphisms-everywhere: Out of $W_0$ only the identity is invertible; out of $W_1$, $j_i$ has no inverse ($h\circ j_i=e_i$) and the $e_i$ are non-identity idempotents.

models.notes: Proposed by Cian Dorr to separate Strong Actuality from Actuality: the model is full, so it has □Rigid Comprehension and hence □Actuality, while $h$'s two retractions keep every true proposition from being a strong atom. Unlike the two-object retract it does not meet coherent-retractions: with $r_h=j_i$, the arrow $x=e_k$ after $h$ for $k\ne i$ gives $r_{x\circ h}\circ x=r_h\circ e_k=j_k\ne r_h$. Gallin Extensional Comprehension fails, since it implies Strong Actuality (gallin-comprehension-implies-strong-actuality), though ND and □Rigid Comprehension hold.

Gallin Extensional Comprehension fails, since it implies Strong Actuality (gallin-comprehension-implies-strong-actuality), though ND and □Rigid Comprehension hold.
models.definition:
The category with objects $W_0,W_1$ generated by $h:W_0\to W_1$ and $j_1,j_2:W_1\to W_0$ subject to $j_1\circ h=j_2\circ h=1_{W_0}$, evaluated at $W_0$. Its arrows are $1_{W_0}$; $h$; $j_1,j_2$; and $1_{W_1}$ with the idempotents $e_i:=h\circ j_i$, which compose by $e_i\circ e_k=e_k$, $j_i\circ e_k=j_k$ and $e_i\circ h=h$ (the rewriting $j_i\circ h\mapsto1$ has no overlaps, so these normal forms are distinct).

Individuals, fixed for this record: at every object the individuals are the members of an infinite set $D$, the same at every object, and every arrow acts on them as the identity.

Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: one designated relational constant $c$ of type $\tau=\bar\sigma t$ denotes $\lambda\bar x\, .\,a$, where $a$ is the unique true atom of the model, the actual-world proposition $\{1\}$; every other constant of Σ, of which there is at least one, is relational and denotes the top element of its type.

Metatheory, fixed for this record: the axiom of choice is used freely, as in ordinary mathematics in ZFC, or in Lean's classical type theory for the verdicts certified there.

met.rigid-haecceity-disjunctions: Every intension is present, so for any set $E$ the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$ is in the domain, and a relation is weakly inextensible at a world iff it lies below that intension over its extension there, since that is the smallest intension satisfying the hypothesis; with persistence, a rigid relation equals it (the argument deferred in extraction.md, 3 October 2026).
met.codomain-intensions: The domains are full at every object.
met.full-model: Every intension of every relational type is present at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59).
met.full-action-model: An action model, full at every object (Classicism, §3.5, p. 59; Appendix D).
met.extensionally-full: A full model contains every intension, so in particular one with any given extension at the identity.
met.identity-singletons: The singleton of the identity arrow at any object is in the domain, the model being full.
met.actuality-contingent: The singleton $a$ of the identity arrow is in the domain, the model being full. It is necessary at no world: a world other than the identity sees itself, which lies outside $a$, and the identity sees an arrow other than itself. And a non-identity arrow $k$ does not fix it, since $1\in k\cdot a$ would need $1\circ k=1$.
met.fixed-infinite-individuals: This is the choice of individuals.
met.homogeneous-individuals: A permutation of $D$ commutes with every arrow's action, the identity, so it is an automorphism at type $e$ and extends, by conjugation, to the full domains of the other types, carrying each individual to its image.
met.comparable-free-arrows: Out of $W_0$ only $1$ is fixed by nothing but the identity, $h$ being fixed by $e_1$.
met.free-nonepic-composite: $j_1\circ h=j_2\circ h=1_{W_0}$ with $j_1\ne j_2$, and $1_{W_0}$ is fixed only by itself.
met.finitely-many-arrows-everywhere: Two arrows out of $W_0$ and five out of $W_1$.
met.returning-arrow: $h$, which $j_1$ retracts.
met.retractions: The arrows out of $W_0$ are its identity and $h$, which $j_1$ retracts.
met.finitely-many-propositions: $W_0$ has four propositions, the sets of its two arrows out.
met.finitely-many-propositions-everywhere: $W_0$ has four propositions and $W_1$ thirty-two, the sets of its five arrows out.
met.separated-retractions: $h$ has the retractions $j_1\ne j_2$, and $\{j_1\}$, in the domain at $W_1$ since the model is full, separates them.
met.sigma-apart: The construction does not mention Σ.
met.noninvertible-retracted-arrow: $h$ is retracted by $j_1$ and $j_2$ but has no inverse, since $h\circ j_i=e_i\ne 1_{W_1}$.
met.trivial-isomorphisms-everywhere: Out of $W_0$ only the identity is invertible; out of $W_1$, $j_i$ has no inverse ($h\circ j_i=e_i$) and the $e_i$ are non-identity idempotents.

Add a full-current root R over K and countably many terminal singleton-individual full models; use K's individual set at R, identity entrance into K and the unique entrances into the terminal models. For an arbitrary set-sized fixed free signature Sigma, take a model of the many-sorted Henkin theory of C(Sigma) and the eight verified packages below by finite satisfiability in these countable-signature constructions. All lambda templates and literal identity clauses are retained. Evaluate at the designated current truth predicate.

models.definition: In ZFC take a nonempty set-sized family of pointed C action models witnessing every C-consistent pure sentence, using the interpretation-root construction's action-model-existence input. Keep all old objects, domains and arrows unchanged. Choose infinite typed auxiliary name sets large enough to dominate their domains and to give distinct coordinates to a fixed set-sized constant signature Sigma. Add a root whose individuals are its individual names, whose loops are all type-preserving permutations of names, and whose arrows into each old object are all typed interpretations of names in that object's domains. There are no old-to-root arrows and the designated root symmetry group is trivial. Root relational entities are exactly all profiles pinned by finitely many typed names and landing as whole admitted entities at every old target; pinning applies to all root loops including identity. Transport is precomposition. Individual constants denote their designated names; relational constants denote their named lifts, with empty root-loop rows and whole interpreted old sections. Evaluate at the root identity.

arguments.text: For a finite pin S, the admitted root-only proposition q_S says that the root map fixes S. Progressiveness gives Diamond q_S=q_S at every coordinate. If S pins a current truth p, q_S <= p, so q_S witnesses the native ND-necessity of p. Every nonzero proposition splits at a fresh coordinate, either by moving a root individual-name image upwards or by assigning a fresh propositional name top/bottom in the same old target.

arguments.text: The empty-pinned root table E={q_{c_n}: n in N}, with empty old rows, is admitted at tt. Any coextension Y has a finite pin. Move a fresh c_k while fixing that pin. Y's future table still contains the whole q_{c_k}. A pinned tester omitting that whole proposition exactly when c_k moves, and containing bottom at all old targets, necessarily contains every current E-member because moved cylinders become bottom. It fails on the retained q_{c_k} in Y's future full domain, contradicting weak inextensibility.

Select a representative of each current equivalence class in ZFC and represent the selected subset by such a profile. All clauses of native Transversal Choice are current. Relational Choice and Transversal follow from recorded implications; their direct proofs are also given. Writeup Sections 6–7.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: Current relation fullness admits the higher predicate whose extension is exactly the whole standard numeral denotations Z_n. It contains Frege zero and is closed under successor, so every current finite cardinality is one of these entities. Finite induction shows Z_n holds of a property exactly when its current extension has n individuals. No Z_n holds of the universal infinite name set. This proves the impredicative Axiom of Infinity, not merely external infinitude. Writeup Section 8.

Every typed interpretation remains available, and whole named-lift landing gives the required possibility. Empty tuples are included. Pure Possibility+ and both Maximalisms are derived. arguments.text: Let c be the least individual name and q_c its root-only fixed-name proposition. If a progressive map moves c, its name image omits c, so every transported current proposition has a finite pin omitting c. The proposition q_c has no such pin. The admitted {c}-pinned tt tester is universal when c is fixed, omits q_c otherwise, and has universal whole old sections. It therefore necessarily holds of every transported current proposition but fails on q_c in a full future target domain. This directly refutes the native BF_t formula. Writeup Section 10.

M_k is the rooted Kripke modalized-domain model obtained by unravelling the full one-object action model on the monoid {1,k}, k²=k, with a single individual, as in §5.3. The new refinement-isolated root sees both components and itself. Actual individuals are a disjoint copy of ω, mapping identically into M_C and constantly to the sole individual of M_k. arguments.by: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic), prompted by Cian Dorr, 25 October 2026
arguments.text: In the chain component $M_k$, the unravelling of the idempotent monoid, the proposition $q$ true at $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ and false at $a_0$ exists at $a_0$ and is an atom there, its only parts existing at $a_0$ being itself and bottom; but at $a_1$ it is identical to $\top$, which has the strict nonzero part $\{a_1\}$ there, so $q$ is not an atom at $a_1$ and not a self-atom. The root proposition with chain component $q$ and the other components bottom is therefore an atom at the root that is not a self-atom, with no self-atom below it: Atoms are self-atoms (type t) and Self-Atomicity (type t) fail. The root proposition with the Cohen component the whole cloud and the rest bottom is a self-atom (the argument self-atoms of the cloud models) with no atom below it, so Self-atoms are atoms (type t) fails. Strong Actuality holds at the root, whose singleton is the true atom and is seen by no other point, so transports to bottom everywhere; at the chain points the singleton of the point is the true atom and is likewise unseen from later points; and at the cloud points every proposition is $\top$ or $\bot$, so the true atom decides everything. Hence □Strong Actuality holds.

The Cohen component is rigidifiable and admits global choice by Lemma 5.5(a). The idempotent action model validates □RC, is extensionally full at its root, and validates □IC by the natural selector constructed in Lemma 5.7. Its unravelled modalized-domain model therefore satisfies Lemma 5.5(b). The transfer theorem 5.6(b,c) gives RC and IC at the new root and throughout both components, hence □RC and □IC.

arguments.text: In the full action model on {1,k}, k sends every proposition to top or bottom while four propositions remain available at the target. Theorem 5.6(d) lifts a witnessing predicate to the rooted sum, using top in the other component and an everywhere-true root extension. All actual propositions satisfy it necessarily, while universal instantiation fails in the idempotent component.

arguments.text: At the root all relations on the identity classes are realized, so internal complete Boolean algebras and relation-based cardinal comparisons are external ones (Lemmas 6.6–6.7). For strong limit μ of countable cofinality, |RO(F)|=2^μ=μ^ω. Pierce’s theorem |C|^ω=|C| excludes complete Boolean algebras of size in [μ,2^μ). Every algebra that is finite or strictly smaller than the propositions therefore has size <μ. It occurs as a lottery factor and is realized below its component proposition; the degenerate algebra is realized below bottom. A root relation witnesses the isomorphism.

The points of the first component force a real number structure of sets of naturals satisfying $\neg\mathrm{CH}$, those of the second one satisfying CH; the root sees both, so neither disjunct of Non-contingency of CH holds at type $e\to t$.

models.definition:
Over ZFC start with the full singleton-individual action model on A,B, generated by h:A->B and distinct j_1,j_2:B->A with j_i h=1_A and e_i=h j_i. Add a root R, with singleton individuals, arrows y:R->A and x,z_n:R->B (n in N), and no nonidentity arrow into R. Put hy=x, j_i x=j_i z_n=y, and e_i x=e_i z_n=x. The replica z_n arrows remain distinct and are not factored through fresh A arrows. The old domains and outgoing arrows stay full and unchanged.
For a relational type tau, an old A entity a has rows A_0 at 1_A and A_1 at h. For any B-current table C, b(a,C) has row C at 1_B, A_0 at each j_i and A_1 at each e_i. Then j_i b(a,C)=a and e_i b(a,C)=ha as whole entities. A root relation consists of a current tuple extension K with finite support under replica permutations, an arbitrary old a, and B-current tables C_n equal to A_1 outside a finite set. Its whole transports are yX=a, xX=ha, z_nX=b(a,C_n). Define the action and root domains recursively on argument types. Replica permutations act on root arguments and on the C_n sequence, fixing all old entities. At each object, truth, application and quantifiers use its full admitted domain. Evaluate at R. The write-up proves closure, C soundness and the whole-profile order.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: Necessary inclusion is inclusion at the free coordinates K, A_0 and every C_n. Each nonzero relation contains a singleton at one of these coordinates. Root-current and replica singletons are strong. An A_0 singleton becomes an ordinary atom at A and a false-current two-j-row profile at B. It is an atom wherever instantiated and therefore is a self-atom, although it is not strong. Any nonzero dependent A_1 row appears cofinitely among the C_n rows and is covered by a replica singleton. This proves all-type Self-Atomicity. See sections 5–6.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: A current family has a finite support J. Union its free rows. The union current row is J-supported, and transpositions outside J make the union C_n tables equal outside J. Recompute A_1 as that common table and choose the full A entity with this row and the union A_0 row. The resulting admitted entity is the least upper bound in the exact free order; complements give greatest lower bounds. The coordinate singleton atoms also give root Atomicity. All old typed profile algebras are full and finite, so both properties hold at every old point as well. These are the boxed all-type verdicts. See sections 5–7.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: At R retain any relation's supported current extension and set all old data to bottom. This is an admitted inextensible coextension: every strict future image is bottom, and a root tester necessarily covering its current instances bounds it. At each old full object, exact-image profiles of arbitrary current tuple sets are admitted inextensible coextensions at every continuation. Thus IC holds at R,A,B. See section 9.

arguments.by: GPT-6 Astra, prompted by Daniel Kodsi
arguments.text: At A any true proposition contains 1_A, so its h-image contains both j_1 and j_2. The full B proposition with only j_1 separates them; no true proposition at A is strong. Since y reaches A, necessary Strong Actuality fails at R. Section 8 also directly refutes root Strong Atomicity_t using the nonstrong A_0 propositional atom; the map derives that failure from the recorded negative verdict.

models.notes: This one construction separates Self-Atomicity from necessary Strong Actuality while retaining necessary all-type BC, Atomicity and IC. Root completeness is internal to admitted families. Strong Atomicity_t fails and is derived; this is not a counterexample to Strong Atomicity plus necessary BC implying necessary IC. No claim about necessary Self-Atomicity, Barcan, Choice, Rigid Power or a signature expansion is made.

models.definition:
An ideally full action model in the sense of Classicism, Appendix D, over a category with two objects, each carrying the ideal of finite sets: a model of C by Proposition D.4. The member's construction and evaluation point follow.

A two-object ideally full action model. Fix a fixed-point-free involution $\pi$ on $\mathbb N$ (say $2k\leftrightarrow 2k+1$), which partitions $\mathbb N$ into two-element blocks. The objects are $W_0$, with individuals $\mathbb N$, and $V$, with individuals $\mathbb N\sqcup\{\star\}$ where $\star$ forms a block by itself. The arrows are all surjective block-respecting maps between these sets: $g(\pi c)\in\{g(c),\pi g(c)\}$ for every $c$, so a block maps into a block, either injectively or collapsed to a point, there are surjective arrows $W_0\to V$, obtained by collapsing one block onto $\star$ and mapping the remaining blocks onto all blocks; and the new individual $\star$ can be hit only by collapsing a block onto it. The pinning action is the identity on individuals, the ideal is the finite sets, and the individuals are the type-$e$ domains, so the model is ideally full in the sense of Classicism, Appendix D, and a model of C by its Proposition D.4. The evaluation point is the identity on $V$, the object with the new individual $\star$; every object is reachable from it, since there are surjective arrows $V\to W_0$ (send $\star$ anywhere).


Interpretation of Σ, fixed for this record: every constant of Σ is relational, and each denotes the top element of its type.

meets.no-atoms-anywhere: At either object let $p\ne\bot$ be pinned down by a finite $N$ and contain $h$. Take a block $B$ disjoint from $N$ and its $\pi$-image and $b\in B$: some arrow agreeing with $h$ on $N$ sends $b$ to $h(b)$ and some sends it elsewhere, both in $p$ (in the surjective model the infinitely many other blocks keep it surjective), so the arrows in $p$ sending $b$ to $h(b)$ lie strictly between $\bot$ and $p$.
meets.infinitely-many-propositions-everywhere: At both objects the propositions that an arrow sends $0$ to $n$, one for each $n$, are pinned down by $\{0\}$ and pairwise distinct.
meets.finitely-pinned-domains: Ideally full with the ideal of finite sets: every intension pinned down by a finite set is in the domain, and every entity in a domain is one.
