# Classicism: import coverage

Source: Andrew Bacon and Cian Dorr, *Classicism*, in Fritz and Jones (eds),
*Higher-Order Metaphysics*, Oxford University Press, 2024, pp. 109–190. The
import was made from the draft dated 16 May 2023, 87 pages, which does not
differ materially from the published version; locators refer to that draft,
including its footnotes.

The import includes the positive extension principles in §§1.4–2.6,
distinguished type instances used by the paper, boxed variants used in its
connections, the Gallin comparison, the choice decomposition, and the
pure/signature variants of the maximalist schemata. The named background
consequences in §1.5 have separate nodes. The defining rules of H and C,
Boolean identities, and the machinery of action-model semantics remain
part of the framework rather than separate extension nodes.

| Source | Connections recorded |
| --- | --- |
| §1.4, pp. 15–16 | Fregean Axiom, Extensionality, Functionality |
| §1.5, pp. 16–19 | K, T, 4, NI, CBF, Broad Necessitism, Intensionality, Modalized Functionality |
| Proposition 2.1, pp. 20–21 | Functionality, Tractarianism and BF equivalence |
| Proposition 2.2, p. 22 | ND, ND at t, 5 and B equivalence |
| Propositions 2.3–2.4, pp. 22–23 | Boxed ND implies BF; ND and BF imply boxed ND |
| Propositions 2.5–2.7, pp. 25–26 | C5, completeness, atomicity and Actuality connections |
| §2.2, p. 27 | Reported No Pure Contingency theorem; proof pending |
| Propositions 2.8–2.10, pp. 29–30 | Rigid Comprehension, completeness and Actuality |
| Propositions 2.11–2.12, p. 30 | Rigid Comprehension from boxed Atomicity, completeness and BF; boxed BF |
| §2.3, pp. 31–32 | Functional Choice = Plenitude + Relational Choice |
| Propositions 2.13–2.16, pp. 32–33 | Plenitude, ND, Actuality, completeness and Rigid Comprehension |
| §2.3, p. 33 | Boxed equivalences and C5 + Atomicity package |
| §§2.4–2.5, pp. 35–40 | Distinctness Maximalism, Possibility Maximalism, Separated Structure, Witnessed Possibility, Logical Necessity |
| §2.6, pp. 41–42 | Maximalist incompatibilities, Possibility+, Strong Possibility |
| §3.5, pp. 59–61 | Full action-model examples and pure-sentence B |
| Appendix D, Proposition D.5, pp. 74–79 | Eight finite-support packages and two multiple-object examples |
| Theorem 3.26; Appendix E, pp. 80–83 | Coalesced-sum models and distinctness-preserving collapse |

Model descriptions give the source construction and the point at which
the properties hold. The map uses the paper's relational type system, so
the source constructions apply directly. One explicitly described full
Henkin model over a singleton individual domain is credited as an original
specialization of the standard construction. So are the two full one-object
action models over the group of all permutations of an infinite set (§3.5), with
the natural action on the individuals and with one individual; they witness
the joint consistency of □ND, the Axiom of Infinity at type t and □Relational
Choice. The singleton-root coalesced
model retains a separate pending obligation to interpret the map's fixed
nonlogical signature; its pure-language source construction is proved.

Two reported results lack proofs in this draft: the Goodsell–Yli-Vakkuri
No Pure Contingency result (p. 27) and Goodsell's incompatibility of
Maximalist Classicism with Rigid Comprehension (p. 41). Their records retain
the attribution and claim with pending verification status. No claim is
made that the source authors regarded them as conjectures.

The formalized statement of Proposition 2.15 uses the intended second
disjunct with the output variable equal to top; its record identifies the
printed variable typo. Proposition 2.11 is recorded as a conjecture since 28 September 2026: the
proof in note 42 has two gaps (see the record). In that proof, Actuality is obtained
from Proposition 2.7; note 42's reference to Proposition 2.6 would require
an extra C5 premise. The question in note 93 about BF + Atomicity without
Actuality is not imported as open: Proposition 2.7 already rules it out.

Fundamental Possibility (§2.5, pp. 39–40) and the principle that every
individual is fundamental (§2.6, n. 60, p. 41) are not imported. Both use
the fundamentality predicate $\operatorname{Fun}$, a nonlogical constant,
so they lie outside the map's logical vocabulary; the connection recorded
from n. 60 went with them.

Type-system comparison variants and their specialization arrows are omitted.
All schemata use the fixed relational type system; restrictions on
particular type parameters remain explicit.
The inference engine treats each schema as a proposition; it does not
perform type substitution automatically. The useful recorded instances
and their connecting results make those steps explicit.

## Arithmetic is Necessary (Goodsell, 2024 draft)

Source: Zachary Goodsell, *Arithmetic is Necessary*, draft dated 5 June 2024,
28 pages. Its logic HKC is H plus K plus Countable Boolean Completeness,
which C extends, so its theorems transfer to the map with the type $\nu$
instantiated as $(\sigma t)t$ at every type $\sigma$ (see Background; until 16 October
2026 the map fixed $\sigma=e$).

| Source | Connections recorded |
| --- | --- |
| §3, Definitions 1 and 6, pp. 7–8, 13 | Countable Boolean Completeness; Boolean Completeness restricts to it |
| §4, Definitions 3–5 and 8, pp. 11–13, 19 | The arithmetical vocabulary, $I$, arithmetical sentences |
| §5, Lemmas 2–8 and Theorem 9, pp. 14–21 | Countable Boolean Completeness implies the Necessity of Arithmetic |
| §6, Theorem 11, pp. 24–26 | Possibility Maximalism (pure) is incompatible with the Necessity of Arithmetic, hence with Countable and full Boolean Completeness and with Rigid Comprehension |

Theorems 10 (arithmetical signatures) and the truth-predicate extension of
§5.3 are not imported. The consistency of C with $I$, assumed in the
source's n. 14, is witnessed on the map by the full Henkin model with a
countably infinite individual domain.

## Logical Combinatorialism (Bacon, 2020)

Source: Andrew Bacon, *Logical Combinatorialism*, *Philosophical Review*
129(4), 2020, pp. 537–589, read directly on 22 September 2026. Its
background system HFE is contained in C, and its schemata are taken in the
map's relational type system (see Background).

| Source | Connections recorded |
| --- | --- |
| §2, pp. 544–547 | Logical Necessity (already recorded), with direct locators |
| §3, pp. 550–557 | Modal Freedom (signature Σ) from Logical Necessity; No Brute Necessities as an alias of Witnessed Possibility; nn. 29–30 on the failure of ND and B |
| §4, pp. 560–565 | Logical Necessity ⇒ Separated Structure; General Separated Structure and its equivalence with Separated Structure; Possibly Witnessed Possibility as a further equivalent |
| §4, p. 568 and n. 53 | Independence (signature Σ) from Separated Structure |
| Appendix A.2–A.3, pp. 580–587 | The glued full action model over the free monoid, in a thread-individual and a singleton-individual variant, proved on 22 September 2026 with a write-up that supplies the unproved Theorem A.8 from the 2024 book's coalesced sums |

Not imported, following Zachary Goodsell's decision of 21 September 2026
that the map's vocabulary is the logical constants together with the
constants of $\Sigma$: everything stated with Bacon's predicates
$\operatorname{Fun}_\sigma$ and $\operatorname{Pure}_\sigma$, namely
Quantified Logical Necessity and its necessitation, Quantified Separated
Structure, Fundamental Independence and Completeness, Purity, Pure
Application, the purity of purity and of fundamentality, the
fundamentality-quantified forms of Logical Necessity, Witnessed Possibility
and Modal Freedom, the §3 consequences for fundamental entities, and the
propositional liar of n. 60; likewise Classicism's Fundamental Possibility
and its n. 58 consequence about converses. Also not imported: the
fine-grained converse-uniqueness principle (nn. 45–46), Russell and
Hawthorne's set-theoretic Pattern and the inaccessible-order-type example
(§3, pp. 551–553), Structure, which is inconsistent (§4, p. 558), and
Melianism (§4, p. 571). The glued models' interpretation of
$\operatorname{Pure}$ and $\operatorname{Fun}$ (Appendix A.3) is not
recorded either; the models are recorded for the pure and signature
principles only.

## A Philosophical Introduction to Higher-Order Logics (Bacon, 2024)

Source: Andrew Bacon, *A Philosophical Introduction to Higher-Order Logics*,
Routledge, 2024, chapters 8 and 18, read directly on 22 September 2026.
Locators are the book's page numbers.

| Source | Connections recorded |
| --- | --- |
| §8.2, pp. 164–171 | Strong Leibniz Biconditionals and their necessitation; Weak Leibniz Biconditionals as an alias of Atomicity; SL ⇒ Atomicity, Atomicity + BF ⇒ SL, their boxed forms, and □SL + Rigid Comprehension ⇒ □BF (type t) (Theorem 8.2) |
| §18.1, §18.3, §18.6 | Modal models, standard models and coalesced sums, used to prove the glued free-monoid models of Logical Necessity |

The rest of chapter 8 restates material already imported from Classicism.
Chapter 18's coherence results (Corollary 18.2, Proposition 18.8,
Corollaries 18.3–18.4, Propositions 18.9–18.11) concern maximalizations of
extensions of C other than C itself; whether to record them as relativized
Possibility Maximalism principles awaits a decision.

## Deferred model verdicts: Tame Rigidity and Intensional Choice (recorded 3 October 2026)

**4 October 2026 (Claude Fable 5.1, at Cian Dorr's direction).** The collapse lemma is now the
topic's general argument `arguments/intensional-choice-collapse.yaml`, under the conditions
`symmetric-domains`, `construction-individuals` and `collapse-onto-point`; the six symmetric models
meet it as before, and so do the new symmetry-constrained full models
(`groups/symmetry-constrained-full.yaml`), finite models in which Intensional Choice fails while
Actuality, Atomicity, Boolean Completeness and Rigid Comprehension hold. qualitative-contrast's
positive verdict and qualitative-links' failure (via the constant pair property) are worked out in
the transcript of 3 October and not yet recorded.

The verdicts deferred here on 2 and 3 October, until the model records' new format landed, are now
recorded; the arguments, not yet checked by a human, moved into the records and are no longer kept
here (see git history before 3 October for the notes). Tame Rigidity: the finite-support group's
argument `tame-rigidity` under the condition `arrows-finitely-determined` (truncations, dyadic
roundings, truncated shifts), and the result `c5-implies-necessary-tame-rigidity`. Intensional
Choice: the collapse lemma as the symmetric group's argument `intensional-choice` under
`collapse-onto-point`, at the base individuals only; and, from a Classicism session of the same
day, the general argument `intensional-choice-well-ordering` under `codomain-intensions` (ideally
full and full models), the coalesced group's `intensional-choice-component`, and the own arguments
of the Boolean-valued, ultralimit-fork, all-finite coalesced, qualitative-links and
qualitative-contrast models. Open: Intensional Choice in the symmetric models' one-individual
variants.

## Deferred model verdicts: Rigid Power (3 October 2026)

**Done, 4 October 2026 (Claude Fable 5.1, at Cian Dorr's direction).** The argument below is the general
argument `arguments/rigid-power-tight.yaml`, under the condition `rigid-haecceity-disjunctions`, met by
the full action models and the symmetry-constrained full models. The finite-support group has a shared
argument `rigid-power` under its condition `uniformly-pinned-rigidity`, met by truncations (eventual
constancy) and by monotone-maps and identity-or-collapse (the jump-map lemma). Dyadic roundings and truncated shifts
followed the same day by own arguments (finitely determined arrows give tightness, and the composition laws
$f_n\circ f_m=f_n$, $k_{n-m}\circ k_m=k_n$ give the closure). Open: the surjective finite-support monoids
monotone-surjections and identity-or-collapse-surjections, the two-object finite-support models, the symmetric models,
the coalesced roots and the ultralimit fork.

**To do.** Record `rigid-power-r` and `necessary-rigid-power-r` as satisfied, in the
new model-record format (an argument of the full action models' group would cover them), in `full-idempotent-monoid`,
`full-two-object-chain` and `full-two-object-retract`, with the argument below. (Moved here from the `classicism-edits`
worktree on 3 October 2026, after the new format had landed.)
The engine already derives both in the other full models, through C5 or
□BF + □Atomicity + □Rigid Comprehension.

**Argument** (Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), 3 October 2026; not yet checked by a
human). In a full action model, write $X_0(S)_k:=k\cdot S$. At any object,
$X_0(S)$ is in the domain, so a relation $Y$ is weakly rigid iff $Y=X_0(Y_1)$.
Every such $Y$ is rigid, since $(h\cdot Y)_k=k\cdot(h\cdot Y_1)$. So the rigid
relations are exactly the $X_0(S)$. Moreover $X_0(T)\le X_0(S)$ iff $T\subseteq S$.
For rigid $F=X_0(S)$ and $P:=\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le F$:
- at an arrow $k$, $P_k=\{X_0(T'):T'\subseteq k\cdot S\}$;
- transport gives $k\cdot P_1=\{X_0(k\cdot T):T\subseteq S\}$;
- these coincide, because the image map $T\mapsto k\cdot T$ from subsets of $S$ to
  subsets of $k\cdot S$ is onto.

So $P=X_0(P_1)$, and $P$ is rigid. The same holds at every object, so both forms of
Rigid Power hold in every full action model.

## Model verdicts on the analysis principles (23 October 2026)

**23 October 2026 (Claude Fable 5.1, prompted by Zachary Goodsell).** The Mathematical contingency
principles added on 23 October (Analytic Necessitism, its second-order form, the Necessity of
Analysis and of Second-Order Analysis, the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis) were tagged

(every extensionally full model has the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis, all its real number
structures being the real numbers with full second-order semantics); `analysis-finite-everywhere`

`finitely-many-arrows-everywhere` and `finitely-many-individuals-everywhere`; and four arguments

`unretracted-arrow` or `noninvertible-retracted-arrow`, resting on one lemma: an instance of a rigid
carrier is determined by its transport along any arrow, and in a full model no entity of a
relational type is determined by its transport along an arrow without a retraction. The same lemma
runs in the finitely pinned models when some arrow identifies two points (new condition
`non-injective-arrow`, the argument `analytic-necessitism-collapsing-arrow-pinned`) and in the
symmetric ideally-full models (new condition `exact-collapses-of-every-size`, which also supplies
the real number structure of type $tt$ from the orbits of the propositions "the arrow is constant
on $N$", the argument `analytic-necessitism-exact-collapses-symmetric`). Own arguments: the
permutation model, where every arrow is invertible, has Second-Order Analytic Necessitism at every
type (write-up `finite-support-permutations.md`); the free-loop chain, the ultralimit fork, the
Boolean-valued model (the Cohen algebra adds a real, so no crisp structure is necessarily complete)
and the two re-rooted or sectioned two-object pinned models fail Analytic Necessitism.

Left unknown, 25 models: the coalesced sums (their roots see components of every kind, so a
rigid real number structure at the root needs a case analysis of the components), Bacon's
modalized cloud models and the lottery and Cohen idempotent-sum models (where the principles
belong to his own analysis of CH), the two-object symmetric models (old-new individuals,

A side effect: a verdict on a principle without a Lean definition removes a model's generated Lean
statement, so the certificates of 40 models went from `lean: stated` to `lean: none` (three of

**Arithmetic Necessitism, the same day.** Settled in every model. The map's inextensibility is Dorr's:
a property may not gain instances beyond the transports of its old ones. Since the numerals are
closed terms, which transport to numerals, $\mathbb N_\sigma$ is rigid wherever the numbers at every
reachable object are exactly the numerals, that is, wherever some property has the numerals as its
extension there; persistence and necessary distinctness are theorems of C given $\Box I^*_\sigma$.
Two general arguments give that: `arithmetic-necessitism-extensionally-full` and
`arithmetic-necessitism-finitely-pinned` (the constant intension of numerals is pinned down by the
empty set and symmetric). The complete coalesced sums have the principle vacuously, $\neg I^*_\sigma$
being a pure sentence consistent with C and so possible at the root (shared argument

$\mathbb N_\sigma$ is crisp. The one failure is coalesced-two-extensional-arithmetics-root: in its

member $c$, and the root entity whose $M_2$-part is $x<c$ necessarily holds of every root number

open, the countermodel not being S5.

## Self-Atomicity and the bridge principles (25 October 2026)

Cian Dorr proposed the notion of a self-atom, a possible entity that is necessarily an atom whenever it
is instantiated, the principle Self-Atomicity (every possible entity is entailed by a self-atom) as a
weakening of the Strong Leibniz Biconditionals, and four bridge principles: atoms are self-atoms,
self-atoms are atoms, self-atoms are strong worlds, atoms are strong worlds. Claude Fable 5.1
(Anthropic), prompted by him, surveyed the recorded Strong Leibniz results. Recorded, each at relational
types and at type t, boxed and unboxed, in the category More Boolean structure: the five principles;
the structural results (type-t instances, boxed to unboxed, No Pure Contingency); the Strong Leibniz
Biconditionals as Atomicity with Atoms are strong worlds, BF giving the latter (Bacon’s Exercise 8.12
refactored, the old records kept with cross-references); the implications among the bridges; □Actuality,
Two-hat implies ND-necessity, 5 ⇒ □B and the intensional-choice result with Self-Atomicity for the Strong
Leibniz Biconditionals; 5 and □5 giving self-atoms are atoms and are strong worlds. Models: the
three-object fork and the monoid with ac = bc (Self-Atomicity with Atomicity and Strong Actuality but
without the Strong Leibniz Biconditionals or BF), the Cantor fan (Self-Atomicity with Actuality, Strong
Actuality and BF (type t) but without Atomicity), general arguments for full models, group arguments for
the symmetry-constrained models and the coalesced sums. Open: whether Self-Atomicity implies Strong
Actuality (it does in every full and every plain ideally full model), and whether Self-Atomicity with
Rigid Comprehension implies its own boxed form or □Rigid Comprehension. Transcript in .private
(25 October 2026).

shared_arguments.text:
The transfer of tame-rigidity-component, applied to a rigid relation whose power property is not rigid. The pure sentence $\exists A^{tt}\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(A)\land\neg\operatorname{Rigid} (\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le A)$ is consistent with C (it holds in the one-individual variants of finite-support-pair-injections-or-collapses and symmetric-collapse-pair, with $A:=\top$), so some component $m$ satisfies it at its root, with witness $A$. Its extension $D$ there is nonempty: otherwise weak inextensibility tested on $\bot$ makes $A=\bot$, whose power property is the haecceity of $\bot$, which is rigid.
For $p\in D$ let $\widehat p$ be the root proposition false at the root, with $m$-component $p$ and $\bot$ in every other component; let $F$ have root extension $\{\widehat p:p\in D\}$, $m$-component $A$, and in each other component $i$ the haecceity of $\bot$. Both are in the domain, the root domains being fullest. $F$ is weakly persistent at the root, $A$ and the haecceities being persistent. It is weakly inextensible there: if $H$ necessarily holds of every $\widehat p$, its root extension contains them, $A\le H_m$ by the weak inextensibility of $A$, and the haecceity of $\bot$ entails $H_i$; entailment in the sum is componentwise. Every other accessible world lies in a component, where $F$'s components are rigid; so $F$ is rigid. The $m$-component of its power property is that of $A$, transport respecting abstraction, rigidity and entailment, and every arrow into $m$ factors through the distinguished one; so it is not rigid. Rigid Power fails at the root, at type $t\to t$.

shared_arguments.text: Let $v$ be any object reachable from the evaluation point and $\mathfrak R$ a real number structure at $v$ (Background, Analysis). Its completeness is tested against the subproperties of its carrier present at $v$, and by extensional fullness every subset of the carrier's extension there is the extension at the identity of one of them; so the carrier, with the extensions of $\le$, $+$ and $\times$, is a complete ordered field in the sense of the metatheory and, by Huntington's theorem, a theorem of ZF, is isomorphic to the real numbers. For the same reason the extension of $N$, the least subproperty containing $0$ and closed under adding $1$, is its set of natural numbers, that set being the extension of a subproperty. A second-order analytical sentence $A(\mathfrak R)$ quantifies over the relations among entities of the structure's type at $v$, applied to the structure's elements, and their extensions at the identity are all the relations on the carrier, again by extensional fullness. So $A(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $v$ exactly when $A$ holds in the real numbers under full second-order semantics, which depends neither on $v$ nor on $\mathfrak R$. Hence $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to A(\mathfrak R)$ holds when $A$ is true of the reals and $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to\neg A(\mathfrak R)$ when it is false: every instance of the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, and with it the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis, as recorded. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: Write a relation $Y$ as its intension $k\mapsto Y_k$. Then $Y\bar a$ holds at $k$ iff $k\cdot\bar a\in Y_k$, $(h\cdot Y)_k=Y_{k\circ h}$, and $\le$ is inclusion of intensions. Put $X_0(S)_k:=k\cdot S$. (1) In any one-object model, if $Y_k=k\cdot Y_1$ for every $k$ then $Y$ is rigid: persistence is immediate, and for the boxed weak inextensibility, $(h\cdot Y)_k=k\cdot(h\cdot Y_1)=X_0(Y_h)_k$, which lies inside every $X$ that contains $X_0(Y_h)$. (2) Let $Y$ be weakly rigid with extension $S$. For each finite $N^{\prime}$ the intension $B_{N^{\prime}}(S)_k:=\bigcup_{k^{\prime}\equiv_{N^{\prime}}k}k^{\prime}\cdot S$ is pinned down by $N^{\prime}$, so it is in the domain. It contains $X_0(S)$, so weak inextensibility gives $Y\subseteq B_{N^{\prime}}(S)$, and persistence gives $Y\supseteq X_0(S)$; hence $k\cdot S\subseteq Y_k\subseteq\bigcap_{N^{\prime}}\bigcup_{k^{\prime}\equiv_{N^{\prime}}k}k^{\prime}\cdot S$. With one object, an intension whose value is the same at every arrow is in the domain by the condition, and it is fixed by transport along every arrow: $(h\cdot Y)_j=Y_{jh}=Y_j$. shared_arguments.text: Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with $ka=kb$ for two distinct points $a$ and $b$ of the set the arrows act on, and let $q$ be the set of arrows $j$ out of $w$ with $ja\ne jb$. It contains the identity, is pinned down by $\{a,b\}$, is symmetric (an arrow separates $a$ from $b$ iff its composite with a permutation of the points does), and contains no arrow $j\circ k$. Let $\tau$ be $tt$, or $tttt$ in the case noted below. No entity $x$ of type $\tau$ at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: let $y$ agree with $x$ except at the arrows in $q$, where the top entity of the argument type of $\tau$ is added to its value or removed from it. Then $y$ is pinned down by a finite set along with $x$, is symmetric if $x$ is, so is in the domain; it differs from $x$ and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. If $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ of type $\tau$, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$ (Background, Analysis), an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above would give $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ by persistence, $Xy$ by inextensibility, and $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$ by the necessary distinctness of the instances: so $X$ has no instance. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds, however, at type $\tau$. The propositions are infinitely many and, in the recorded instances, include a copy of the natural numbers, so by extensional fullness the entities of type $tt$, which include one with any set of propositions as extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the reals, whose order, sum, product and natural numbers are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain; the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty, so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{tt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$. (Should the propositions be infinite without including a copy of the natural numbers, the same holds at type $tttt$, the sets of sets of propositions being Dedekind-infinite in ZF.) So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

At any object $v$ reachable from the evaluation point, extensional fullness gives a property whose extension at $v$ is exactly the numerals there; it contains $\mathbf 0_\sigma$ and is closed under successor, so the numbers at $v$ are exactly the numerals, every numeral being an instance of every inductive property. Persistence of $\mathbb N_\sigma$ and, given $\Box I^*_\sigma$, the necessary distinctness of the numbers are theorems of C (the proof of necessary-rigid-comprehension-implies-arithmetic-necessitism). Inextensibility, $\Box\forall X\,.\,(\forall n\,.\,\mathbb N_\sigma n\to\Box Xn)\to\mathbb N_\sigma\le X$: at a reachable $v$ and for an arrow $j$ from $v$ to $u$, the numbers at $u$ are the numerals there, which are the transports along $j$ of the numbers at $v$, so any $X$ that necessarily holds of the numbers at $v$ holds at $u$ of the numbers there. So $\mathbb N_\sigma$ is rigid, and Arithmetic Necessitism holds at every type. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: Let $v$ be any object reachable from the evaluation point and $\mathfrak R$ a real number structure at $v$ (Background, Analysis). Its completeness is tested against the subproperties of its carrier present at $v$, and by extensional fullness every subset of the carrier's extension there is the extension at the identity of one of them; so the carrier, with the extensions of $\le$, $+$ and $\times$, is a complete ordered field in the sense of the metatheory and, by Huntington's theorem, a theorem of ZF, is isomorphic to the real numbers. For the same reason the extension of $N$, the least subproperty containing $0$ and closed under adding $1$, is its set of natural numbers, that set being the extension of a subproperty. A second-order analytical sentence $A(\mathfrak R)$ quantifies over the relations among entities of the structure's type at $v$, applied to the structure's elements, and their extensions at the identity are all the relations on the carrier, again by extensional fullness. So $A(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $v$ exactly when $A$ holds in the real numbers under full second-order semantics, which depends neither on $v$ nor on $\mathfrak R$. Hence $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to A(\mathfrak R)$ holds when $A$ is true of the reals and $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to\neg A(\mathfrak R)$ when it is false: every instance of the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, and with it the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis, as recorded. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: Self-Atomicity at every relational type, necessarily, there being one object. Let $I\ne\bot$ be an entity of type $\bar\sigma t$, pinned down by $N$, with a pair $\langle k,\bar x\rangle$ in it. If $k=1$, the singleton of the pair is in the domain, pinned down by $\{0,1\}$, and is a self-atom. Otherwise $k$ is a collapse with $k(0)=k(1)=0$ and $k(y)=1$ for some $y$; let $N^{\prime}:=N\cup\{0,y\}$ and $J$ the set of pairs $\langle k_1,\bar x\rangle$ with $k_1$ agreeing with $k$ on $N^{\prime}$, below $I$ and pinned down by $N^{\prime}$. Its transport along $\langle k_1,\bar x\rangle$ is the set of $\langle m,\bar x\rangle$ with $m$ fixing $k(N^{\prime})\supseteq\{0,1\}$ pointwise, which only the identity does; so it is the singleton of $\langle1,\bar x\rangle$, an atom, and $J$ is a self-atom below $I$.

shared_arguments.text: $\{1\}$ is in the domain and is the only atom, the propositions over the collapses refining. A monotone surjection sends $0$ to $0$, so a collapse $k$ has $k(0)=k(1)=0$ and $k(y)=1$ for some $y$. For such $k$ and a finite $N\supseteq\{0,y\}$, the set $q$ of collapses agreeing with $k$ on $N$ is pinned down by $N$, and a collapse $m$ has $m\circ k^{\prime}\in q$, for $k^{\prime}\in q$, only if it fixes $k^{\prime}(N)\supseteq\{0,1\}$ pointwise, which no collapse does; so the transport of $q$ along each member is $\{1\}$, and $q$ is a self-atom, not an atom. So Self-atoms are atoms (type t) fails, and with it Self-atoms are strong atoms (type t). Self-Atomicity (type t) holds, and necessarily, there being one object: a possible proposition contains $1$, and then $\{1\}$, or a collapse $k$, and then, being pinned down by some $N$, the self-atom built from $k$ and $N\cup\{0,y\}$. The relational form is the argument that follows.

shared_arguments.text: The source (n. 92) conjectures this but does not show it. Any set $F$ of propositions is the extension at the identity of an element of the domain at type $t\to t$, namely the profile $\langle h,p\rangle\mapsto\{i : i\cdot p\in F\}$: it is natural, independent of $h$ and so pinned down by the empty set, and each of its values is pinned down by the pinning set of $p$, since $i\cdot p$ depends only on the values of $i$ there. A least upper bound of $F$ under entailment is a least finitely pinned superset of $\bigcup F$, and it exists only if the least $S$-pinned superset of $\bigcup F$ stops shrinking as the finite set $S$ grows. So the family $F$ of the condition has no least upper bound, and, taking pointwise negations, the family of complements has no greatest lower bound.

shared_arguments.text: Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with $ka=kb$ for two distinct points $a$ and $b$ of the set the arrows act on, and let $q$ be the set of arrows $j$ out of $w$ with $ja\ne jb$. It contains the identity, is pinned down by $\{a,b\}$, is symmetric (an arrow separates $a$ from $b$ iff its composite with a permutation of the points does), and contains no arrow $j\circ k$. Let $\tau$ be $tt$, or $tttt$ in the case noted below. No entity $x$ of type $\tau$ at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: let $y$ agree with $x$ except at the arrows in $q$, where the top entity of the argument type of $\tau$ is added to its value or removed from it. Then $y$ is pinned down by a finite set along with $x$, is symmetric if $x$ is, so is in the domain; it differs from $x$ and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. If $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ of type $\tau$, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$ (Background, Analysis), an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above would give $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ by persistence, $Xy$ by inextensibility, and $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$ by the necessary distinctness of the instances: so $X$ has no instance. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds, however, at type $\tau$. The propositions are infinitely many and, in the recorded instances, include a copy of the natural numbers, so by extensional fullness the entities of type $tt$, which include one with any set of propositions as extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the reals, whose order, sum, product and natural numbers are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain; the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty, so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{tt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$. (Should the propositions be infinite without including a copy of the natural numbers, the same holds at type $tttt$, the sets of sets of propositions being Dedekind-infinite in ZF.) So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: Write $B_N(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto\bigcup\{k^{\prime}\cdot E:k^{\prime}\text{ agrees with }k \text{ on }N\}$; it is pinned down by $N$, and symmetric when the model is, since the symmetry group consists of arrows and $(gk)\cdot E=g\cdot(k\cdot E)$, so it is in the domain. (1) A relation $Y$ pinned down by $S$, with extension $E$ at the identity, is weakly rigid iff $Y=B_S(E)=B_N(E)$ for every finite $N\supseteq S$: weak persistence gives $k\cdot E\subseteq Y_k$, and with pinning $B_S(E)\subseteq Y$; a domain element $X$ with $\Box X$ true of each member of $E$, pinned down by $N$, contains $B_N(E)$, so weak inextensibility says exactly that $Y\subseteq B_N(E)$ for every finite $N$, and $B_N(E)\subseteq B_S(E)$ for $N\supseteq S$. (2) Rigidity is (1) at every world: for each arrow $h$, $h\cdot Y$, with $(h\cdot Y)_k=Y_{kh}$, must satisfy $k\cdot Y_h\subseteq Y_{kh}\subseteq B_N(Y_h)_k$ for all $k$ and finite $N$. (3) Let $Y$ be weakly rigid. Persistence at $h$: $k\cdot Y_h=\bigcup\{(kk^{\prime\prime})\cdot E:k^{\prime\prime}\text{ agrees with }h\text{ on }S\}\subseteq B_S(E)_{kh}=Y_{kh}$. Inextensibility at $h$: given $N$, take $N^{\prime\prime}$ from the condition. By (1), $Y_{kh}=B_{N^{\prime\prime}}(E)_{kh}$, so a member of it is $k^{\prime}\cdot e$ with $e\in E$, pinned down by some finite $M$, and $k^{\prime}$ agreeing with $kh$ on $N^{\prime\prime}$. The condition gives $k^{\prime\prime}$ agreeing with $h$ on $N^{\prime\prime}$ and $j$ agreeing with $k$ on $N$ with $jk^{\prime\prime}$ agreeing with $k^{\prime}$ on $M$, so $k^{\prime}\cdot e=j\cdot(k^{\prime\prime}\cdot e)$, where $k^{\prime\prime}\cdot e\in B_{N^{\prime\prime}}(E)_h=Y_h$; hence $k^{\prime}\cdot e\in B_N(Y_h)_k$. So every weakly rigid relation, at every type, is rigid. With No Pure Contingency, which holds in one-object models, the map's results give $\Box$Tame Rigidity.

shared_arguments.text: Write $X_0(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$. Witnessed Possibility fails for the pure formula $x=\top_\tau$, witnessed by $\top_\tau$: $\Diamond(c=\top_\tau)$ is $\Diamond\Box p_0$, and $\Box p_0$ holds at no arrow $h$, since the constant map to $1$ composed after $h$ moves $0$. shared_arguments.text: Write $\mathrm{fix}_N$ for the arrows agreeing with the identity on the finite set $N$, the least true proposition pinned by $N$, and $\delta_N$ for the arrows injective on $N$. An arrow $v$ is in $\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}_{[n]}$ iff some monotone $x$ has $x\circ v$ fixing $[n]$, iff $v$ is injective on $[n]$; and $\Diamond\delta_{[n]}=\delta_{[n]}$. So $\Box_{\ne}p$ holds iff $p\supseteq\delta_{[n]}$ for some $n$, and the true proposition $\{h:h(0)=0\}$ is not ND-necessary, since the shift $m\mapsto m+1$ is injective. Two-hat necessity, however, is truth: $u\in\hat\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}_{[n]}$ requires, for every $m$, a monotone $v$ injective on $[m]$ with $v\circ u$ fixing $[n]$; injectivity of $v$ on $[m]$ gives $v(j)\ge j$ for $j\le m$, so $i=v(u(i))\ge u(i)\ge i$ and $u$ fixes $[n]$. Thus $\hat\Diamond\,\mathrm{fix}_{[n]}=\mathrm{fix}_{[n]}$, every truth is two-hat necessary, and $\{h:h(0)=0\}$ is two-hat necessary but not ND-necessary. (The verdicts this argument also establishes but does not record are derived by the engine.)

shared_arguments.text: The source (n. 92) conjectures this but does not show it. Any set $F$ of propositions is the extension at the identity of an element of the domain at type $t\to t$, namely the profile $\langle h,p\rangle\mapsto\{i : i\cdot p\in F\}$: it is natural, independent of $h$ and so pinned down by the empty set, and each of its values is pinned down by the pinning set of $p$, since $i\cdot p$ depends only on the values of $i$ there. A least upper bound of $F$ under entailment is a least finitely pinned superset of $\bigcup F$, and it exists only if the least $S$-pinned superset of $\bigcup F$ stops shrinking as the finite set $S$ grows. So the family $F$ of the condition has no least upper bound, and, taking pointwise negations, the family of complements has no greatest lower bound.

shared_arguments.text: At type $e\to t$, for the property of being even, which is in the domain as the constant intension $\{\langle b,h\rangle : b\text{ even}\}$, pinned down by $\emptyset$. Unpacking $\operatorname{Inextensible}$ as in the left-to-right half of Dorr’s rigidity criterion (draft, Lemma 14, p. 7, with Lemma 13): even the unboxed matrix, evaluated at the identity, says that $Y$ is contained in every persistent (transport-closed) $B$ in the domain whose extension includes $Y$’s. For a finite $N^{\prime}$, the smallest such $B$ pinned down by $N^{\prime}$ is $B_{N^{\prime}}:=\{\langle b^{\prime\prime},i^{\prime}\rangle : i^{\prime\prime}(b)=b^{\prime\prime}\text{ for some even }b\text{ and some arrow }i^{\prime\prime}\text{ agreeing with }i^{\prime}\text{ on }N^{\prime}\}$, which is transport-closed and pinned down by $N^{\prime}$. Now let $Y$ be coextensive with evenness and pinned down by a finite $N_0$; then $\langle b,i\rangle\in Y$ for every even $b$ and every arrow $i$ fixing $N_0$ pointwise. Take the arrow $i$, the even $b$ and the finite $N^{\prime}$ that the condition provides for $N_0$: no arrow agreeing with $i$ on $N^{\prime}$ sends an even number to $b$. So $\langle b,i\rangle\in Y\setminus B_{N^{\prime}}$, and $Y$ is not even weakly inextensible.

shared_arguments.text: Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with $ka=kb$ for two distinct points $a$ and $b$ of the set the arrows act on, and let $q$ be the set of arrows $j$ out of $w$ with $ja\ne jb$. It contains the identity, is pinned down by $\{a,b\}$, is symmetric (an arrow separates $a$ from $b$ iff its composite with a permutation of the points does), and contains no arrow $j\circ k$. Let $\tau$ be $tt$, or $tttt$ in the case noted below. No entity $x$ of type $\tau$ at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: let $y$ agree with $x$ except at the arrows in $q$, where the top entity of the argument type of $\tau$ is added to its value or removed from it. Then $y$ is pinned down by a finite set along with $x$, is symmetric if $x$ is, so is in the domain; it differs from $x$ and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. If $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ of type $\tau$, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$ (Background, Analysis), an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above would give $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ by persistence, $Xy$ by inextensibility, and $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$ by the necessary distinctness of the instances: so $X$ has no instance. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds, however, at type $\tau$. The propositions are infinitely many and, in the recorded instances, include a copy of the natural numbers, so by extensional fullness the entities of type $tt$, which include one with any set of propositions as extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the reals, whose order, sum, product and natural numbers are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain; the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty, so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{tt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$. (Should the propositions be infinite without including a copy of the natural numbers, the same holds at type $tttt$, the sets of sets of propositions being Dedekind-infinite in ZF.) So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: In a one-object finitely pinned model, BF (type t) fails as soon as there are a finite $N$, an arrow $i$ and a proposition $q$ in the domain that is the transport $i^{\prime}\cdot p=\{k : k\circ i^{\prime}\in p\}$ of no proposition $p$ along any arrow $i^{\prime}$ agreeing with $i$ on $N$: the intension $X:=\{\langle r,j\rangle : r\ne q\text{ or }j\text{ disagrees with }i\text{ on }N\}$, which the condition puts in the domain, contains $\langle i^{\prime}\cdot p,i^{\prime}\rangle$ for every $p$ and $i^{\prime}$, so $\forall p\, .\,\Box Xp$ holds at the identity, and omits $\langle q,i\rangle$, so $\Box\forall p\, .\,Xp$ fails there. Since membership of $k$ in $i^{\prime}\cdot p$ depends only on $k$ restricted to the range of $i^{\prime}$, it suffices that $q$ separate two arrows agreeing on every such range, as the condition provides.

shared_arguments.text: A self-atom of any relational type at an object $W$ is instantiated at some arrow $k$ out of $W$, and its transport along $k$ is an atom at $k$’s target instantiated at the identity there. The existential projection of an atom $I$ of a relational type, the proposition $\exists\bar x\, .\,I\bar x$, is an atom of type $t$: it is in the domain, it is not bottom, and for any proposition $p$ the entity $I\land\lambda\bar x\, .\,p$ lies below the atom $I$, so is $I$ or bottom, which puts $p$ above the projection or disjoint from it. So the projection is a true atom at $k$’s target, which the condition excludes. Hence no reachable object has a self-atom, and Self-atoms are atoms and Self-atoms are strong atoms hold vacuously at every type and every reachable object, while Self-Atomicity (type t) fails at the evaluation point, the top proposition having no self-atom below it.

All four bridge principles therefore hold vacuously at every type and every reachable object, and Self-Atomicity (type t) fails at the evaluation point.

shared_arguments.text: For a true proposition $p$ pinned down by a finite set take as the witness $q$ the proposition that the arrow fixes $0,\ldots,N$ for $N$ beyond the pinning set. An arrow fixing $0,\ldots,N$ agrees with the identity on that set and so is in $p$. An arrow $h$ that does not, with least moved point $m\le N$, has $hm<m$ by monotone surjectivity and so collapses $m-1$ and $m$; then no $k\circ h$ can fix both, so $\Diamond q$ fails at $h$. Hence $\Box(\Diamond q\to p)$.

For $k^{\prime}$ agreeing with $kh$ there and $M\subseteq[0,m]$, $m\ge n^{\prime\prime}$: let $k^{\prime\prime}$ be $h$ on $[0,n^{\prime\prime}]$ and then rise by one at each step, and let $j$ be $k$ on $[0,h(n^{\prime\prime})]$, send $h(n^{\prime\prime})+i$ to $k^{\prime}(n^{\prime\prime}+i)$ for $0<i\le m-n^{\prime\prime}$, and then rise by one. shared_arguments.text: Write $B_N(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto\bigcup\{k^{\prime}\cdot E:k^{\prime}\text{ agrees with }k \text{ on }N\}$; it is pinned down by $N$, and symmetric when the model is, since the symmetry group consists of arrows and $(gk)\cdot E=g\cdot(k\cdot E)$, so it is in the domain. (1) A relation $Y$ pinned down by $S$, with extension $E$ at the identity, is weakly rigid iff $Y=B_S(E)=B_N(E)$ for every finite $N\supseteq S$: weak persistence gives $k\cdot E\subseteq Y_k$, and with pinning $B_S(E)\subseteq Y$; a domain element $X$ with $\Box X$ true of each member of $E$, pinned down by $N$, contains $B_N(E)$, so weak inextensibility says exactly that $Y\subseteq B_N(E)$ for every finite $N$, and $B_N(E)\subseteq B_S(E)$ for $N\supseteq S$. (2) Rigidity is (1) at every world: for each arrow $h$, $h\cdot Y$, with $(h\cdot Y)_k=Y_{kh}$, must satisfy $k\cdot Y_h\subseteq Y_{kh}\subseteq B_N(Y_h)_k$ for all $k$ and finite $N$. (3) Let $Y$ be weakly rigid. Persistence at $h$: $k\cdot Y_h=\bigcup\{(kk^{\prime\prime})\cdot E:k^{\prime\prime}\text{ agrees with }h\text{ on }S\}\subseteq B_S(E)_{kh}=Y_{kh}$. Inextensibility at $h$: given $N$, take $N^{\prime\prime}$ from the condition. By (1), $Y_{kh}=B_{N^{\prime\prime}}(E)_{kh}$, so a member of it is $k^{\prime}\cdot e$ with $e\in E$, pinned down by some finite $M$, and $k^{\prime}$ agreeing with $kh$ on $N^{\prime\prime}$. The condition gives $k^{\prime\prime}$ agreeing with $h$ on $N^{\prime\prime}$ and $j$ agreeing with $k$ on $N$ with $jk^{\prime\prime}$ agreeing with $k^{\prime}$ on $M$, so $k^{\prime}\cdot e=j\cdot(k^{\prime\prime}\cdot e)$, where $k^{\prime\prime}\cdot e\in B_{N^{\prime\prime}}(E)_h=Y_h$; hence $k^{\prime}\cdot e\in B_N(Y_h)_k$. So every weakly rigid relation, at every type, is rigid. With No Pure Contingency, which holds in one-object models, the map's results give $\Box$Tame Rigidity.

shared_arguments.text: The witness is the proposition $p:=\{h : h0\ne h1\}$, the pair-preserving injections, pinned down by $\{0,1\}$ and true. Let $q$ be true, pinned down by a finite $N$, and let $k$ be a pair-preserving injection. The inverse of $k$ on $k[N\cup\{0,1\}]$ maps $\{0,1\}$ onto itself and every other point outside $\{0,1\}$, so it extends to a pair-preserving injection $j$. Then $j\circ k$ agrees with the identity on $N$, so $j\circ k\in q$. Hence every $p$-world can reach a $q$-world: $p\le\Diamond q$.

shared_arguments.text: The source (n. 92) conjectures this but does not show it. Any set $F$ of propositions is the extension at the identity of an element of the domain at type $t\to t$, namely the profile $\langle h,p\rangle\mapsto\{i : i\cdot p\in F\}$: it is natural, independent of $h$ and so pinned down by the empty set, and each of its values is pinned down by the pinning set of $p$, since $i\cdot p$ depends only on the values of $i$ there. A least upper bound of $F$ under entailment is a least finitely pinned superset of $\bigcup F$, and it exists only if the least $S$-pinned superset of $\bigcup F$ stops shrinking as the finite set $S$ grows. So the family $F$ of the condition has no least upper bound, and, taking pointwise negations, the family of complements has no greatest lower bound.

shared_arguments.text: Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with $ka=kb$ for two distinct points $a$ and $b$ of the set the arrows act on, and let $q$ be the set of arrows $j$ out of $w$ with $ja\ne jb$. It contains the identity, is pinned down by $\{a,b\}$, is symmetric (an arrow separates $a$ from $b$ iff its composite with a permutation of the points does), and contains no arrow $j\circ k$. Let $\tau$ be $tt$, or $tttt$ in the case noted below. No entity $x$ of type $\tau$ at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: let $y$ agree with $x$ except at the arrows in $q$, where the top entity of the argument type of $\tau$ is added to its value or removed from it. Then $y$ is pinned down by a finite set along with $x$, is symmetric if $x$ is, so is in the domain; it differs from $x$ and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. If $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ of type $\tau$, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$ (Background, Analysis), an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above would give $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ by persistence, $Xy$ by inextensibility, and $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$ by the necessary distinctness of the instances: so $X$ has no instance. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds, however, at type $\tau$. The propositions are infinitely many and, in the recorded instances, include a copy of the natural numbers, so by extensional fullness the entities of type $tt$, which include one with any set of propositions as extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the reals, whose order, sum, product and natural numbers are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain; the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty, so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{tt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$. (Should the propositions be infinite without including a copy of the natural numbers, the same holds at type $tttt$, the sets of sets of propositions being Dedekind-infinite in ZF.) So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: As the argument arithmetic-necessitism-extensionally-full, with the property of being a numeral supplied by pinning. The intension $Z$ whose value at each arrow $k$ out of the evaluation object is the set of numerals $\mathbf 0_\sigma,\operatorname{Suc}_\sigma\mathbf 0_\sigma,\ldots$ at the target of $k$ is pinned down by the empty set, its value depending on the arrow only through its target, and is symmetric, transport along a permutation of the points carrying numerals to numerals, as transport along any arrow does, numerals being closed terms; so it is in the domain, and so is its transport $k\cdot Z$ to any reachable object, whose extension there is exactly the numerals. Hence at every reachable object the numbers at $\sigma$, the instances of the least inductive property, are exactly the numerals, which transport to numerals; persistence and, given $\Box I^*_\sigma$, necessary distinctness are theorems of C, and inextensibility follows as in that argument. So Arithmetic Necessitism holds at every type. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: Let $v$ be reachable from the evaluation point. If every type is finite at $v$ there is no real number structure there, an ordered field having the infinitely many distinct elements $0$, $1$, $1+1$, and so on. Otherwise let $D$ be as in the condition. Carry the real numbers onto $D$ by a bijection: the carrier, order, sum, product, $0$, $1$ and natural numbers are sets of tuples from $D$, so extensions at $v$ of entities there, which form a real number structure $\mathfrak R^*$ at $v$, its completeness and the leastness of its natural numbers being tested against subproperties whose extensions are all the subsets of $D$. Its second-order quantifiers, applied to tuples from $D$, range over all relations on $D$, so for each second-order analytical sentence $A$, $A(\mathfrak R^*)$ holds at $v$ iff $A$ is true of the real numbers under full second-order semantics. Any real number structure $\mathfrak R$ at $v$, of any type, is isomorphic to $\mathfrak R^*$ by a relation in the domain there (Huntington's theorem, a theorem of C: Background, Analysis), and $A(\mathfrak R)\leftrightarrow A(\mathfrak R^*)$ is a theorem of C given such an isomorphism, relations on one carrier being carried to the other by comprehension. So at every reachable object every real number structure satisfies exactly the second-order analytical sentences true of the reals, and each instance $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R) \to A(\mathfrak R)$ or $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to\neg A(\mathfrak R)$ of the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, with the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis. The choice of the bijection with the reals needs no choice principle, $D$ having the cardinality of the continuum.

shared_arguments.text: Every arrow $k_n$ is determined by its value at $n+1$, so every singleton is in the domain, and the only atom containing the identity is $\{1\}$. A self-atom containing $k_n$ and $k_m$ with $n<m$ would have $k_{m-n}$ in its transport along $k_n$, since $k_{m-n}\circ k_n=k_m$, so that transport would not be $\{1\}$. So the self-atoms are the singletons, atoms, and each is a strong atom: $\{k_n\}$ becomes under $k_m$ the set of $k_j$ with $j+m=n$, of at most one arrow. A self-atom of a relational type sits over one arrow with one tuple, by the transport condition, so is an atom and a strong atom likewise. One object, so this holds at every world.

shared_arguments.text: Write $X_0(E)$ for the intension $n\mapsto k_n\cdot E$. Every arrow is finitely determined, so, as in the group's argument for Tame Rigidity, a weakly inextensible relation is $X_0$ of its extension at the identity, and the rigid relations are the $X_0(E)$ that are in the domain, namely those with $k_n\cdot E$ constant for all $n$ beyond some $s$. For rigid $F=X_0(S)$ the power property $\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le F$ has extension $\{X_0(T'):T'\subseteq k_m\cdot S,\ X_0(T')\text{ in the domain}\}$ at $k_m$, while its extension at the identity transported along $k_m$ is $\{X_0(k_m\cdot T):T\subseteq S,\ X_0(T)\text{ in the domain}\}$. Given such a $T'$, put $T:=\{q\in S: k_m\cdot q\in T'\}$, so that $k_m\cdot T=T'$. Since $k_{n-m}\circ k_m=k_n$ for $n\ge m$, transport gives $k_n\cdot T=k_{n-m}\cdot T'$ for $n\ge m$, constant for large $n$; so $X_0(T)$ is in the domain. Hence the power property is $X_0$ of its extension; and $k_n$ applied to that extension is, by the same correspondence, $\{X_0(T''):T''\subseteq k_n\cdot S,\ X_0(T'')\text{ in the domain}\}$, constant for $n>s$, so the power property is in the domain and rigid. The boxed form follows from No Pure Contingency.

shared_arguments.text: Write a relation $Y$ as its intension $k\mapsto Y_k$. Then $Y\bar a$ holds at $k$ iff $k\cdot\bar a\in Y_k$, $(h\cdot Y)_k=Y_{k\circ h}$, and $\le$ is inclusion of intensions. Put $X_0(S)_k:=k\cdot S$. (1) In any one-object model, if $Y_k=k\cdot Y_1$ for every $k$ then $Y$ is rigid: persistence is immediate, and for the boxed weak inextensibility, $(h\cdot Y)_k=k\cdot(h\cdot Y_1)=X_0(Y_h)_k$, which lies inside every $X$ that contains $X_0(Y_h)$. (2) Let $Y$ be weakly rigid with extension $S$. For each finite $N^{\prime}$ the intension $B_{N^{\prime}}(S)_k:=\bigcup_{k^{\prime}\equiv_{N^{\prime}}k}k^{\prime}\cdot S$ is pinned down by $N^{\prime}$, so it is in the domain. It contains $X_0(S)$, so weak inextensibility gives $Y\subseteq B_{N^{\prime}}(S)$, and persistence gives $Y\supseteq X_0(S)$; hence $k\cdot S\subseteq Y_k\subseteq\bigcap_{N^{\prime}}\bigcup_{k^{\prime}\equiv_{N^{\prime}}k}k^{\prime}\cdot S$. By the condition, for $k$ other than the identity some finite $N^{\prime}$ has $k$ as the only arrow agreeing with it there, and the bounds meet: $Y_k=k\cdot S$. So every weakly rigid relation at every type is rigid by (1), and Tame Rigidity holds. With No Pure Contingency, which holds in a one-object model, the map's results give $\Box$Tame Rigidity.

Any set $F$ of propositions is the extension at the identity of an element of the domain at type $t\to t$, namely the profile $\langle h,p\rangle\mapsto\{i : i\cdot p\in F\}$: it is natural, independent of $h$ and so pinned down by the empty set, and each of its values is pinned down by the pinning set of $p$, since $i\cdot p$ depends only on the values of $i$ there. A least upper bound of $F$ under entailment is a least finitely pinned superset of $\bigcup F$, and it exists only if the least $S$-pinned superset of $\bigcup F$ stops shrinking as the finite set $S$ grows. So the family $F$ of the condition has no least upper bound, and, taking pointwise negations, the family of complements has no greatest lower bound.

shared_arguments.text: Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with $ka=kb$ for two distinct points $a$ and $b$ of the set the arrows act on, and let $q$ be the set of arrows $j$ out of $w$ with $ja\ne jb$. It contains the identity, is pinned down by $\{a,b\}$, is symmetric (an arrow separates $a$ from $b$ iff its composite with a permutation of the points does), and contains no arrow $j\circ k$. Let $\tau$ be $tt$, or $tttt$ in the case noted below. No entity $x$ of type $\tau$ at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: let $y$ agree with $x$ except at the arrows in $q$, where the top entity of the argument type of $\tau$ is added to its value or removed from it. Then $y$ is pinned down by a finite set along with $x$, is symmetric if $x$ is, so is in the domain; it differs from $x$ and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. If $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ of type $\tau$, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$ (Background, Analysis), an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above would give $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ by persistence, $Xy$ by inextensibility, and $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$ by the necessary distinctness of the instances: so $X$ has no instance. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds, however, at type $\tau$. The propositions are infinitely many and, in the recorded instances, include a copy of the natural numbers, so by extensional fullness the entities of type $tt$, which include one with any set of propositions as extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the reals, whose order, sum, product and natural numbers are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain; the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty, so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{tt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$. (Should the propositions be infinite without including a copy of the natural numbers, the same holds at type $tttt$, the sets of sets of propositions being Dedekind-infinite in ZF.) So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: Write $X_0(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$. For $E$ pinned down uniformly by a finite $S_0$, $X_0(E)$ is in the domain, pinned down by $S_0$, and so is $X_0(T)$ for every $T\subseteq E$ and $X_0(k\cdot E)$ for every arrow $k$. The extension at $k$ of the power property $\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le F$ is the set of rigid $X$ with $X\le k\cdot F$, the bound variable untransported and the parameter transported; by the condition, for rigid $F=X_0(S)$ it is $\{X_0(T'):T'\subseteq k\cdot S\}$, and transporting the extension at the identity along $k$ gives $\{X_0(k\cdot T):T\subseteq S\}$, the same set, since $T'\subseteq k\cdot S$ is $k\cdot T$ for $T:=\{s\in S:k\cdot s\in T'\}$. So the power property is $X_0$ of its own extension, which is pinned down uniformly, hence in the domain and rigid. In these models the rigid relations are thus (a) the haecceities, (b) the properties "being pinned down by $S$", which are $X_0(\operatorname{Pin}(S))$, and (c) the disjunctions, finite or infinite, of haecceities of entities pinned down by one finite set; the boxed form follows from No Pure Contingency.

shared_arguments.text: Write a relation $Y$ as its intension $k\mapsto Y_k$. Then $Y\bar a$ holds at $k$ iff $k\cdot\bar a\in Y_k$, $(h\cdot Y)_k=Y_{k\circ h}$, and $\le$ is inclusion of intensions. Put $X_0(S)_k:=k\cdot S$. (1) In any one-object model, if $Y_k=k\cdot Y_1$ for every $k$ then $Y$ is rigid: persistence is immediate, and for the boxed weak inextensibility, $(h\cdot Y)_k=k\cdot(h\cdot Y_1)=X_0(Y_h)_k$, which lies inside every $X$ that contains $X_0(Y_h)$. (2) Let $Y$ be weakly rigid with extension $S$. For each finite $N^{\prime}$ the intension $B_{N^{\prime}}(S)_k:=\bigcup_{k^{\prime}\equiv_{N^{\prime}}k}k^{\prime}\cdot S$ is pinned down by $N^{\prime}$, so it is in the domain. It contains $X_0(S)$, so weak inextensibility gives $Y\subseteq B_{N^{\prime}}(S)$, and persistence gives $Y\supseteq X_0(S)$; hence $k\cdot S\subseteq Y_k\subseteq\bigcap_{N^{\prime}}\bigcup_{k^{\prime}\equiv_{N^{\prime}}k}k^{\prime}\cdot S$. By the condition, for $k$ other than the identity some finite $N^{\prime}$ has $k$ as the only arrow agreeing with it there, and the bounds meet: $Y_k=k\cdot S$. So every weakly rigid relation at every type is rigid by (1), and Tame Rigidity holds. With No Pure Contingency, which holds in a one-object model, the map's results give $\Box$Tame Rigidity.

shared_arguments.text: The source (n. 92) conjectures this but does not show it. Any set $F$ of propositions is the extension at the identity of an element of the domain at type $t\to t$, namely the profile $\langle h,p\rangle\mapsto\{i : i\cdot p\in F\}$: it is natural, independent of $h$ and so pinned down by the empty set, and each of its values is pinned down by the pinning set of $p$, since $i\cdot p$ depends only on the values of $i$ there. A least upper bound of $F$ under entailment is a least finitely pinned superset of $\bigcup F$, and it exists only if the least $S$-pinned superset of $\bigcup F$ stops shrinking as the finite set $S$ grows. So the family $F$ of the condition has no least upper bound, and, taking pointwise negations, the family of complements has no greatest lower bound.

shared_arguments.text: Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with $ka=kb$ for two distinct points $a$ and $b$ of the set the arrows act on, and let $q$ be the set of arrows $j$ out of $w$ with $ja\ne jb$. It contains the identity, is pinned down by $\{a,b\}$, is symmetric (an arrow separates $a$ from $b$ iff its composite with a permutation of the points does), and contains no arrow $j\circ k$. Let $\tau$ be $tt$, or $tttt$ in the case noted below. No entity $x$ of type $\tau$ at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: let $y$ agree with $x$ except at the arrows in $q$, where the top entity of the argument type of $\tau$ is added to its value or removed from it. Then $y$ is pinned down by a finite set along with $x$, is symmetric if $x$ is, so is in the domain; it differs from $x$ and has $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. If $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ of type $\tau$, necessarily a real number structure, with carrier $X$ (Background, Analysis), an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above would give $k\cdot y=k\cdot x\in X_k$ by persistence, $Xy$ by inextensibility, and $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$ by the necessary distinctness of the instances: so $X$ has no instance. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds, however, at type $\tau$. The propositions are infinitely many and, in the recorded instances, include a copy of the natural numbers, so by extensional fullness the entities of type $tt$, which include one with any set of propositions as extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the reals, whose order, sum, product and natural numbers are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain; the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty, so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{tt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$. (Should the propositions be infinite without including a copy of the natural numbers, the same holds at type $tttt$, the sets of sets of propositions being Dedekind-infinite in ZF.) So Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

Take a countable maximal antichain $(a_n)$ in $A$, put $w_n:=(0,\neg a_n)$, choose $c_n\in A$, and let $X$ of type $t\to t$ have $\rho X(w_n)=c_n$ and $0$ elsewhere. With $s$ the fuzzy subset of $\omega$ given by the $c_n$, a direct computation gives $\rho[\![\exists y\, .\,\operatorname{GLB}_t(y,X)]\!]=\bigvee_{U\subseteq\omega}[\![s=\check U]\!]$, the value of "$s$ is a ground set". Forcing with $A$ adds a Cohen real; taking the $c_n$ to be its coordinates, $[\![s=\check U]\!]=0_A$ for every $U$, so the closed instance of Boolean Completeness (type $t$) has value exactly $a$: true, and not necessary. shared_arguments.text: The four-element Boolean algebra is finite, hence small, and present internally on any four propositions with the right order, the model being full. Forcing Possibilism would give a proposition $p\ne\top$ with exactly four propositions entailing it. In $B=\mathbf 2\times A$ the propositions below $(0,a)$ are the $(0,b)$ with $b\le a$, one of them if $a=0_A$ and infinitely many otherwise, $A$ being atomless; and those below $(1,a)$ are the $(\varepsilon,b)$ with $b\le a$, two of them if $a=0_A$ and infinitely many otherwise. No proposition has exactly four, so Forcing Possibilism fails.

shared_arguments.text: At type $t$, for the algebra fixed in the definition. Here $\Box p$ is $p=\top$, so a property $X$ of type $t\to t$ satisfies $\Box\forall x\,.\,(Xx\to\Box Xx)\land(\neg Xx\to\Box\neg Xx)$ with first coordinate $1$ only if $X$ is crisp, taking the values $\top$ and $\bot$ alone, and likewise for relations; so a rigid real number structure $\mathfrak R$ is crisp, the check of a structure $(S,\le,+,\times,0,1,N)$ of the ground model, and $\Box\operatorname{Real}_t(\mathfrak R)$ asks that $\operatorname{Real}_t(\mathfrak R)$ have value $\top$, in particular $\rho$-coordinate $1_A$. That fails: forcing with $A$ adds a real $r$; the $A$-valued subproperty of $S$ naming the lower Dedekind cut of $r$ in $S$ is in the full domain and is bounded, but has no least upper bound in $S$ with positive value, since $[\![r=\check s]\!]=0$ for every ground real $s$. So the consequent of Analytic Necessitism is false at the evaluation point. Its antecedent is true: $B$ has at least continuum many elements, the crisp characteristic functions of a set $S\subseteq B$ in bijection with the reals and of its order, sum, product and natural numbers are in the full domains, and $\operatorname{Real}_t$ of this structure has $\pi$-coordinate $1$, every bounded crisp subset of $S$ having a least upper bound in it; so $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_t(\mathfrak R)$ is not $\bot$ and its possibility is $\top$.

shared_arguments.text: At type $t$. Write $\pi,\rho$ for the coordinate projections of $B=\mathbf 2\times A$. By extensional fullness, for a box-free formula whose relation variables are only applied to elements of a fixed carrier, with identity only between those elements, the $\pi$-coordinate is its truth in the full standard model over the same domains, and the $\rho$-coordinate its value in $V^A$, relations on a ground set ranging over all names for subsets of it. (Not every box-free sentence transfers: identity between relations is crisp, so box-free Extensionality has value $\bot$.) The sentences below are in this fragment. Both $V$ and $V^A$ have a real number structure on a subset of $D_t=B$: $|B|\ge2^{\aleph_0}$, and $|B|\ge(2^{\aleph_0})^{V^A}$, which is $\aleph_2$ in the first case (where $|B|=\aleph_2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_2$, by CH) and $\aleph_1$ in the second. Real number structures are unique up to isomorphism, so $\exists\mathfrak R\, .\,\operatorname{Real}_t(\mathfrak R)\land\operatorname{CH}(\mathfrak R)$ has $\pi$-coordinate $1$ iff CH holds in $V$ and $\rho$-coordinate $1_A$ iff CH holds in $V^A$, and likewise for $\neg\operatorname{CH}$, the value otherwise being $0$. CH takes opposite values in $V$ and $V^A$, so each of $\forall\mathfrak R\, .\,\operatorname{Real}_t(\mathfrak R)\to\operatorname{CH}(\mathfrak R)$ and $\forall\mathfrak R\, .\,\operatorname{Real}_t(\mathfrak R)\to\neg\operatorname{CH}(\mathfrak R)$ is $(1,0_A)$ or $(0,1_A)$, not $\top$. As $\Box p$ is $p=\top$, both disjuncts of Non-contingency of CH are $\bot$.

shared_arguments.text: At every type. The numerals are crisp entities, and the crisp characteristic function of the set of numerals at $\sigma$ is in the full domain and inductive with value $\top$, so $\mathbb N_\sigma$ is crisp, with the numerals as its instances. Here $\Box p$ is $p=\top$, so persistence, $\Box\forall n\,.\,\mathbb N_\sigma n\to\Box\mathbb N_\sigma n$, has value $\top$; inextensibility, $\Box\forall X\,.\,(\forall n\,.\,\mathbb N_\sigma n\to\Box Xn)\to\mathbb N_\sigma\le X$, has value $\top$, since for each $X$ both sides of the implication are $\bigwedge_n[\![Xn=\top]\!]$ over the numerals $n$; and distinct numerals are necessarily distinct, identity being crisp. So $\mathbb N_\sigma$ is rigid with necessarily distinct instances, whether or not $\Box I^*_\sigma$ holds.

shared_arguments.text: Let $v$ be any object reachable from the evaluation point and $\mathfrak R$ a real number structure at $v$ (Background, Analysis). Its completeness is tested against the subproperties of its carrier present at $v$, and by extensional fullness every subset of the carrier's extension there is the extension at the identity of one of them; so the carrier, with the extensions of $\le$, $+$ and $\times$, is a complete ordered field in the sense of the metatheory and, by Huntington's theorem, a theorem of ZF, is isomorphic to the real numbers. For the same reason the extension of $N$, the least subproperty containing $0$ and closed under adding $1$, is its set of natural numbers, that set being the extension of a subproperty. A second-order analytical sentence $A(\mathfrak R)$ quantifies over the relations among entities of the structure's type at $v$, applied to the structure's elements, and their extensions at the identity are all the relations on the carrier, again by extensional fullness. So $A(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $v$ exactly when $A$ holds in the real numbers under full second-order semantics, which depends neither on $v$ nor on $\mathfrak R$. Hence $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to A(\mathfrak R)$ holds when $A$ is true of the reals and $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to\neg A(\mathfrak R)$ when it is false: every instance of the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, and with it the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis, as recorded. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: At type $\tau:=tt$. With one object, an intension whose value is the same at every arrow is in the domain by the condition, and it is fixed by transport along every arrow: $(h\cdot Y)_j=Y_{jh}=Y_j$. The propositions are infinitely many, so the constant intensions $Y_E$, for $E$ a set of propositions, are at least continuum many and pairwise distinct. Carry the real numbers onto continuum many of them, and take as carrier, order, sum, product, $0$, $1$ and natural numbers the constant intensions whose values are the corresponding sets of tuples of the $Y_E$. All parameters are fixed, so a formula about them has the same truth value at every world, and at the evaluation point they form a real number structure: any bounded set of carrier elements has a least upper bound among them, and every inductive subproperty contains the copy of the natural numbers. Such a structure is rigid, its instances are necessarily distinct, and it is necessarily a real number structure; and the codomain-only intension of type $((\tau)^kt)t$ whose value at each object is the set of codomain-only $k$-ary relations among the carrier there is a represented power of arity $k$, since at every world each $k$-ary relation agrees on the carrier with one of them. shared_arguments.text: Write $w$ for the evaluation object and $k$ for an arrow out of it with no retraction. No entity $x$ of a relational type at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$: the identity of $w$ is not of the form $j\circ k$, such a $j$ being a retraction, and the model being full, the intension $y$ agreeing with $x$ at every arrow but the identity, where it takes another value, is in the domain, while $k\cdot y=k\cdot x$, transport along $k$ reading only the values at the arrows after $k$. Suppose then that $\mathfrak R$ were a rigid real number structure at $w$ at a relational type, necessarily a real number structure (Background, Analysis), with carrier $X$. For an instance $x$ of $X$ and $y$ as above, persistence gives $k\cdot x\in X_k$, so $k\cdot y\in X_k$; inextensibility then gives $Xy$; and the necessary distinctness of the instances gives $k\cdot y\ne k\cdot x$, a contradiction. So $X$ has no instance and is no complete ordered field. The antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds nevertheless, at some relational type. The propositions at $w$ are the sets of the infinitely many arrows out of it, the sets of sets of propositions are Dedekind-infinite (a theorem of ZF for any infinite set), and the entities of type $ttt$ at $w$, which include one with any given extension at the identity, include a copy of the sets of natural numbers and so of the real numbers; the model being full, the order, sum and product of the reals are the extensions at the identity of relations in the domain, every subset of that carrier is the extension of a subproperty, so the structure is complete, and its least inductive subproperty is its natural numbers. So $\exists\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_{ttt}(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $w$ while the consequent of Analytic Necessitism fails there: Analytic Necessitism fails. (When the arrows out of $w$ include a copy of the natural numbers, as in the recorded instances, the same argument runs at type $t$.) No choice is used.

The isomorphism is a relation present in the full domains. The internal notions agree with the external ones: a property of entities carrying the order of a complete Boolean algebra, every subproperty having a least upper bound, is one in the metatheory, since every subset is the extension of a subproperty, and Dedekind finiteness and the existence of injective relations are read in a full model as in the metatheory. shared_arguments.text: The numbers at a type $\sigma$ are the instances of $\mathbb N_\sigma$, the least property containing $\mathbf 0_\sigma$ and closed under $\operatorname{Suc}_\sigma$ (Background); the numerals $\mathbf 0_\sigma$, $\operatorname{Suc}_\sigma\mathbf 0_\sigma,\ldots$ are closed terms, so each denotes at every object, and transport along an arrow carries its denotation at the source to its denotation at the target. At any object $v$ reachable from the evaluation point, extensional fullness gives a property whose extension at $v$ is exactly the numerals there; it contains $\mathbf 0_\sigma$ and is closed under successor, so the numbers at $v$ are exactly the numerals, every numeral being an instance of every inductive property. Persistence of $\mathbb N_\sigma$ and, given $\Box I^*_\sigma$, the necessary distinctness of the numbers are theorems of C (the proof of necessary-rigid-comprehension-implies-arithmetic-necessitism). Inextensibility, $\Box\forall X\,.\,(\forall n\,.\,\mathbb N_\sigma n\to\Box Xn)\to\mathbb N_\sigma\le X$: at a reachable $v$ and for an arrow $j$ from $v$ to $u$, the numbers at $u$ are the numerals there, which are the transports along $j$ of the numbers at $v$, so any $X$ that necessarily holds of the numbers at $v$ holds at $u$ of the numbers there. So $\mathbb N_\sigma$ is rigid, and Arithmetic Necessitism holds at every type. No choice is used.

shared_arguments.text: Let $v$ be any object reachable from the evaluation point and $\mathfrak R$ a real number structure at $v$ (Background, Analysis). Its completeness is tested against the subproperties of its carrier present at $v$, and by extensional fullness every subset of the carrier's extension there is the extension at the identity of one of them; so the carrier, with the extensions of $\le$, $+$ and $\times$, is a complete ordered field in the sense of the metatheory and, by Huntington's theorem, a theorem of ZF, is isomorphic to the real numbers. For the same reason the extension of $N$, the least subproperty containing $0$ and closed under adding $1$, is its set of natural numbers, that set being the extension of a subproperty. A second-order analytical sentence $A(\mathfrak R)$ quantifies over the relations among entities of the structure's type at $v$, applied to the structure's elements, and their extensions at the identity are all the relations on the carrier, again by extensional fullness. So $A(\mathfrak R)$ holds at $v$ exactly when $A$ holds in the real numbers under full second-order semantics, which depends neither on $v$ nor on $\mathfrak R$. Hence $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to A(\mathfrak R)$ holds when $A$ is true of the reals and $\Box\forall\mathfrak R\,.\,\operatorname{Real}_\sigma(\mathfrak R)\to\neg A(\mathfrak R)$ when it is false: every instance of the Necessity of Second-Order Analysis holds, and with it the Necessity of Analysis and the Non-contingency of the Continuum Hypothesis, as recorded. No choice is used.

(The finite-germ argument of the 3 October 2026 analysis, for full models; with choice the well-ordering argument gives the same.)

shared_arguments.text: Write $X_0(E)$ for the intension $k\mapsto k\cdot E$. The extension at an arrow $h$ of the power property $\lambda X\, .\,\operatorname{Rigid}(X)\land X\le F$ is the set of rigid $X$ with $X\le h\cdot F$, the bound variable ranging over the domain untransported and the parameter transported. By the condition the rigid relations are the $X_0(E)$, and $X_0(T)\le X_0(S)$ iff $T\subseteq S$; so for rigid $F=X_0(S)$ the power property has extension $\{X_0(T'):T'\subseteq k\cdot S\}$ at $k$, while transporting its extension at the identity along $k$ gives $\{X_0(k\cdot T):T\subseteq S\}$. These coincide, since every $T'\subseteq k\cdot S$ is $k\cdot T$ for $T:=\{s\in S:k\cdot s\in T'\}$. So the power property is itself $X_0$ of its extension, hence rigid, and the same at every reachable object gives the boxed form.

shared_arguments.text: As in the argument analytic-necessitism-unretracted-arrow, with the individuals supplying the real numbers in place of the propositions. Let $k$ be an arrow out of the evaluation object $w$ with no retraction; as there, the model being full, no entity of a relational type at $w$ is determined by its transport along $k$, so no rigid real number structure of a relational type at $w$ is necessarily a real number structure. But there is a real number structure at $w$ of the relational type $((et)t)t$: the individuals at $w$ are infinitely many, the sets of sets of individuals are Dedekind-infinite (a theorem of ZF for any infinite set), so the entities of type $(et)t$, which include one with any given set of properties of individuals as extension at the identity, include a copy of the natural numbers, and the entities of type $((et)t)t$ a copy of the sets of natural numbers, hence of the reals; the full domains equip that copy, at the identity, with the order, sum, product and natural numbers of the reals, and the structure is complete, every subset of its carrier being the extension of a subproperty. So the antecedent of Analytic Necessitism holds at that type and its consequent fails: Analytic Necessitism fails. No choice is used.

Relational Choice at types $t$ and $t$: let $U$ relate $p_{\{n\}}$ to each $p_C$ with $C\in A_n$, and every other proposition to every proposition. It is serial, and a functional subrelation would relate each $p_{\{n\}}$ to a single $p_{C_n}$ with $C_n\in A_n$, again a choice function. Both principles therefore fail. (The analysis of 3 October 2026: Intensional Choice is choice over worlds, Relational Choice over the elements of a domain.)

shared_arguments.text: As in the general argument forcing-possibilism-continuum-arrows, with the worlds the union $W$ of the socks $P_n$, so that the propositions are the sets of worlds. The regular-open algebra $B$ of Cantor space has the size of the continuum in ZF, and it injects into the propositions, $S\mapsto\bigcup_{n\in S}P_n$ injecting the sets of natural numbers. The propositions do not inject into $B$: an injection would give one of $W$ into the sets of natural numbers, through $w\mapsto\{w\}$, and the lexicographic order of those sets would then choose a member of each sock. So $B$, realised at type $t$ by fullness, is a small complete Boolean algebra, atomless, while every entailment algebra below a proposition is atomic or has one element. (From Astra's note "Forcing Possibilism, Choice and Infinity", §6, in Daniel Kodsi's submission of 24 October 2026.)
